News.title: UK weather: Up to 4 INCHES of rain to hit parts of Britain today as Met Office warns of flooding & yellow warning issued
News.content:
POUR CONDITION UK weather: Up to 4 INCHES of rain to hit parts of Britain today as Met Office warns of flooding & yellow warning issued







Next

UP TO four inches of rain could hit Britain today as the Met Office warns of flooding and issues a yellow weather warning.

An alert over parts of the southeast is in place from 6am and will remain throughout the day.



A slow-moving band of heavy rain is expected to batter Devon and Cornwall – potentially bringing flooding and delaying transport in the region.

It comes after an overnight frost saw temperatures plummet over two consecutive nights.



The lowest temperatures of the season were recorded on Friday night with Saturday night also seeing low temps.

In rural spots across Scotland and northern England temperatures were expected to reach -7C.

And through today, heavy rain will plague the South West with up to four inches expected to fall.

The rest of the south, as well as Northern Ireland, will be dry and cloudy while the north is cold and sunny.



It comes after the first snow warning of the season, with more than an inch recorded in parts of northern England on Tuesday.

A yellow cold health alert is in force for the North West, North East and Yorkshire and the Humber until 9am on Tuesday.

The alert means weather conditions could lead to an increased use of healthcare services and a greater risk to life for vulnerable people, the UK Health Security Agency said.

And, the heavy rainfall could see homes and businesses flooded or damaged.

The Met Office has warned people to check if their property is at risk as a slow-moving band of heavy rain makes its way over the southeast.



According to the forecaster, bus and train services might be affected with journey times taking longer and a chance of cancellations.

People are advised to check their route ahead of travelling to avoid delays as the rain lashes the country.

The forecaster warned that heavier rain could develop over time with low-lying areas likely to experience further downpours.

Met Office Chief Forecaster Matthew Lehnert said: “Within the warning area, 20-40mm of rain is likely quite widely, but some parts of south Devon and Cornwall could see 60-80mm.

“Over Dartmoor, there is a chance of more than 100mm falling through the day.”



RECOMMENDED STORIES

“This slow-moving band of rain will gradually ease on Sunday night, but flooding and travel disruption is possible within the warning area, with south Devon and south Cornwall more likely to see higher totals.

“There is still some uncertainty about where the heaviest rain will fall, so it’s important to stay up to date with the forecast and any warning updates.”

News.title: Twisted female teacher, 29, on sex offenders register after sexting student is arrested AGAIN for ‘holding newborn baby’
News.content:
BACK IN CUFFS Twisted female teacher, 29, on sex offenders register after sexting student is arrested AGAIN for ‘holding newborn baby’







Next

A TWISTED female teacher who is on the sex offenders register after sexting a student has been arrested again for allegedly holding a newborn baby.

Rachel Clement, 29, was hauled back into custody after reportedly cradling a two-week-old infant – despite being banned from having contact with children.



The former Kentucky educator had pleaded guilty to two counts of sexual abuse after sending raunchy messages to a student at Henderson County High School.

But the convicted sex offender is now accused of breaching her court-imposed restrictions during a visit to church attached to a school.



Clement reportedly turned up at the church on November 13 to drop off decorations for a birthday party.

While there, she allegedly held a newborn baby, sparking a fresh legal nightmare for the disgraced teacher.



Under her plea agreement, Clement is banned from having contact with children, with the sole exception of her biological niece.

She is also banned from entering school premises and must remain on the national sex offenders register for life.

But her lawyer, Jonathan Coomes, insisted the former teacher had only visited the church at the pastor’s request.

He argued she had not come into contact with any school-age children and had left the premises before pupils arrived.



Coomes also claimed the baby was “not similar in characteristics to the victim in the present case”.

Clement’s original victim was a teenage boy.

The alleged breach could now see the shamed educator’s bond revoked ahead of her sentencing.

A crunch court hearing to decide whether she should remain free is scheduled for Monday.

Clement is already facing up to 11 years behind bars after admitting to two counts of sexual abuse in a position of authority and one count of evidence tampering.



Her sickening misconduct first came to light in May when school officials received a report accusing her of sending sexual messages to a pupil.

The teacher was swiftly sacked and banned from the school district’s property as cops launched an investigation.

She was initially slapped with charges including using electronic communications to induce a minor to engage in sexual activity, first-degree sexual abuse and evidence tampering.

Clement denied the allegations in June before later striking a plea deal with prosecutors.

Her charges were amended to two counts of first-degree sexual abuse in a position of authority or special trust, while the original first-degree sexual abuse charge was dropped.



As part of the deal, the former teacher agreed to a lifetime ban on teaching anywhere in the United States.

Prosecutors said the revised charges were agreed upon following discussions with the victim and his family, detectives and the school district.

One official said: “We believe the evidence fit those charges.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Clement faces up to three years in prison for each sexual abuse charge and another five years for tampering with evidence.

She is due to be sentenced on January 4, 2027.

News.title: Three dead & 50 missing after horror blaze rips through sweet factory as roof collapses & rescuers search for survivors
News.content:
FACTORY INFERNO Three dead & 50 missing after horror blaze rips through sweet factory as roof collapses & rescuers search for survivors







Next

AT LEAST three people are dead and 50 others are missing after a massive fire raged through a sweet factory in Indonesia.

Rescue teams were scrambled to search for survivors after the terrifying inferno erupted in Banten province on Saturday.



The blaze broke out at the sprawling PT Fonusa Agung Mulia factory which produces Milkita – an Indonesian brand of milk-based candies.

Television reports showed flames engulfing the three-story factory, sending thick black smoke into the sky.



Those who managed to escape the fire said it originated in a cooling unit on the third floor.

Rizky Dwianto from the Banten Search and Rescue Agency said the fire was still burning in “several locations” on Sunday morning.



Firefighters battled flames in several parts of the facility more than 12 hours after the fire began, Dwianto added.

Meanwhile rescue workers swept sections of the factory where victims could be trapped, while parts of the building remained at risk of collapse.



Videos shared by rescuers show officers entering the charred building as small fires continue to burn inside.

“All members of the joint SAR team are making every effort to locate the missing victims while prioritising the safety of personnel on the ground,” the rescue agency said.

The National Search and Rescue Agency said in a statement that 15 people were rescued alive, including four injured workers.

Four people had been rushed to nearby hospitals by emergency medical teams, officials said.

The factory owner said at a news conference that around 300 people were present for Saturday’s shift.



Banten Governor, Andra Soni, said the factory caught fire at 4.30pm local time and was already engulfed by flames when firefighters arrived.

“When we arrived … a large area was already on fire. So we could not determine whether the company’s protection system was functioning properly or not,” the governor said.

Footage from Sunday morning shows the burned-out structure littered with debris including twisted metal and blackened, corrugated iron.



Authorities said the intensity of the fire had rendered the recovered victims unidentifiable from visual inspection.

To help identification efforts cops collected DNA samples from relatives and personal belongings of the missing workers.

Outside the factory, a crowd of anxious relatives waited for news of family members who could not be contacted.

Victims’ families broke down in tears as they phoned loved ones about the tragedy.

Authorities have not yet determined the fire’s cause. The cause of the incident is still under investigation, the local disaster agency said.



The factory is owned by PT Fonusa Agung Mulia, according to search and rescue authorities.

On LinkedIn the company describes itself as a subsidiary of UNIFAM, one of Indonesia’s largest food and beverage companies.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Deadly fires are not uncommon in Indonesia.

In December last year, a blaze that was likely caused by a drone battery explosion tore through a seven-storey building killing at least 22 people.

News.title: I was stripped naked and sexually assaulted by my evil ex in the snow… he battered & abused me until I finally snapped
News.content:
Next

TERRIFIED Gemma Willis was marched outside in the freezing cold and ordered to strip naked by her evil ex.

Convinced she’d cheated, the paranoid thug humiliated the mum in full view of neighbours’ homes before carrying out a painful rudimentary “examination” of her.





At the hands of Richard Ridley, mum-of-one Gemma suffered a three-year campaign of severe physical, sexual and emotional abuse.

In her darkest moment, she even begged her abuser to kill her, before making a desperate escape bid with the help of her friend.

In June 2017 Ridley pleaded guilty to seven offences, including two counts of sexual assault and two counts of common assault, and was sentenced to nine and a half years.

But even behind bars, he continued to torment Gemma, including cryptically posting on Facebook: “They can lock the locks, but they can’t stop the clocks.”

It was the same haunting threat he used to make to her during his campaign of abuse.

Ridley has already been released once before breaching licence conditions and being hauled back inside early last year.

He’s currently subject to a parole review, which could see him released next year.

Gemma, 42, from Stockton-on-Tees, Teesside, told The Sun: “He subjected me to depraved torture, but I won’t let him ruin my life.”





Having waived her right to lifetime anonymity, she was speaking as part of her campaign Not Another Finger, which calls on the UK government to pass stricter laws preventing convicted domestic and sexual abusers from stalking, harassing, or intimidating their victims while in prison or after release.

Bags in hand, Ridley had turned up on Gemma’s doorstep in September 2014 “and never left”.

They’d met around 10 years earlier, and vaguely kept in touch, before he was jailed for offences against a different victim and they began exchanging prison letters.

On his release, they decided to try a relationship.

Gemma said she remembered him being “cheeky and funny… acting the big ‘I am’” but quickly his dark side was exposed.

Weeks after moving in, during a freezing and snowy November evening, Ridley came home intoxicated after a night out and accused Gemma of cheating.

“He started shouting at me that there were footprints in the snow leading up to the front door,” she explained.

Ridley dragged Gemma’s three-year-old son outside.



She said: “It was absolutely Baltic and he was only in a onesie, so I ran out after them.

“He made me strip and refused to let me back in the house or give my son back until I was naked.

“All the lights were on in the other houses and he made me squat and then put his fingers inside me.

“He said he could tell if somebody had been there.”

Following that night, Gemma suffered an escalating series of assaults, including being dragged upstairs by her hair, woken up by a crossbow in the face, as well as being attacked with a trowel and hammer.

“He once put my head through a glass door,” she continued.

“I’ve got what me and my son call a Harry Potter scar… that’s actually what it looks like on my head.”

During the horror assault, his hands around her throat, Gemma relaxed her shoulders and told Ridley “just do it”.



“I said, I can’t take this anymore, just do it. That’s when my head went through the door.”

She added: “It was eventually either he’s going to kill me or I’m going to take on my own life.”

During the lengthy ordeal, often her only protection was her dog Dusty, a Rottweiler and German Shepherd cross.

Ridley often locked him outside but he’d stand up against the window and bark.

Holding back tears, Gemma said: “He’d be trying to get in and I can remember his big brown eyes.”

But Ridley’s anger would then turn on the dog, including savagely beating him in the garden shed and later shooting him with a BB gun as he comforted Gemma.

Ridley’s paranoia meant he constantly suspected Gemma was cheating on him.

He even removed the bath panel because he was convinced men were hiding under the floorboards or inside her mattress.

You're Not Alone EVERY 90 minutes in the UK a life is lost to suicide It doesn’t discriminate, touching the lives of people in every corner of society – from the homeless and unemployed to builders and doctors, reality stars and footballers. It’s the biggest killer of people under the age of 35, more deadly than cancer and car crashes. And men are three times more likely to take their own life than women. Yet it’s rarely spoken of, a taboo that threatens to continue its deadly rampage unless we all stop and take notice, now. If you, or anyone you know, needs help dealing with mental health problems, the following organisations provide support: CALM, www.thecalmzone.net, 0800 585 858

Heads Together,www.headstogether.org.uk

HUMEN www.wearehumen.org

Mind, www.mind.org.uk, 0300 123 3393

Papyrus, www.papyrus-uk.org, 0800 068 41 41

Samaritans,www.samaritans.org, 116 123

“He stabbed my mattress up, threw it out the window, along with the bed frame, and I had to sleep on the floor for the last year of the relationship because he wouldn’t let me get another bed,” Gemma said.



During one occasion, while she and her son were “camping” on the floor, he covered her “head to toe in salad cream” from the fridge.

Gemma said: “My son, God love him, looked at me and said ‘don’t worry, I’ll clean you’.”

It was an old school pal who ultimately helped the mum, child and dog finally escape.

Ridley had changed the locks on the back door without giving Gemma a key, and added extra locks to the front door in an effort to stop her fleeing his attacks.

After reconnecting over texts, the friend helped Gemma devise a plan in which they’d pretend they were going for a dog walk before driving off.

The pal had already secretly helped find her and her son a place at a refuge.

Once away, Gemma then felt safe enough to go to the police.

Prior to Ridley’s original release last year, Gemma had special locks fitted, as well as reinforced doors, a 6ft-high fence and spotlights.

Gemma was then appalled to hear he is up for parole early next year.

“He knows where I live and it terrifies me,” she said.



She claims Ridley’s friends continue to subject her to public harassment over his imprisonment, while illicit social media accounts share threatening posts targeted at her.

“Even with him in prison, I’ve never felt safe,” she said. “I’m always looking over my shoulder.”

Gemma continued: “He needs to stay where he is, that’s the end of it for me.

“I can’t live, I’m not living – I don’t go out, I don’t leave the house unless I have to.”

She added: “He’s a massive danger to me and other women – and what kind of justice system could allow him out.”

News.title: ‘Much-loved’ daughter, 19, killed after being hit by BMW outside hospital A&E is pictured – as family pay tribute
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

TRAGIC CRASH ‘Much-loved’ daughter, 19, killed after being hit by BMW outside hospital A&E is pictured – as family pay tribute







Next

A 19-YEAR-OLD woman who was hit and killed by a BMW outside an A&E has been pictured as her family pay touching tribute.

Cops scrambled to Arrowe Park Hospital in Wirral on Tuesday, November 17, after reports of a collision outside the emergency department.

Medics battled to save Charlotte “Chaz” Lipscombe’s life after she was struck by the vehicle and she was rushed for treatment.

Tragically, despite the best efforts of medical staff, she sadly passed away at the scene.





Her heartbroken family have since said: “Our beautiful girl, a much-loved daughter, sister, girlfriend, niece, cousin and friend to so many.

“Chaz was clever, fiercely loyal, a true petrol head with a passion for motor sports.

“She was one of a kind with a heart and spirit that could never be replaced.

“The world feels emptier without her and our hearts will never be the same.



“We will carry her love, her laughter and her memory with us for the rest of our lives.

“Gone far too soon, loved beyond words and missed beyond measure. Forever ours. Forever 19.

“Please respect our privacy while we are grieving our tremendous loss.”

An investigation has been launched into the circumstances surrounding the tragic incident.



The female driver of the BMW remained at the scene and is assisting police with their enquiries.

Officers have carried out witness and CCTV enquiries as part of their investigation.

News.title: Girl, 17, among three dead in horror mass shooting after two gunmen open fire at baby shower
News.content:
BABY SHOWER SHOOTOUT Girl, 17, among three dead in horror mass shooting after two gunmen open fire at baby shower







Next

THREE people have been killed in a horror shooting at a baby shower after two men opened fire.

A 17-year-old girl and two men, aged 19 and 45, died during the gathering at an events venue in Parma, Ohio.



A woman, 39, suffered a non-life-threatening injury after she was shot in the leg, police said.

Cops said shots were fired between the baby’s 19-year-old father and a 29-year-old man at around 6pm at Pandora’s Magical Events Venue.



The expectant dad, the pregnant woman’s father, and the teenage girl were all found dead from gunshot wounds when police arrived at the scene, the New York Post reports.

It was not clear what sparked the shootout but witnesses reported the 29-year-old man, who has been taken into custody, may have been acting in self-defence, officials said.



The second shooter involved was the 19-year-old, who died at the scene.

Following the shooting, a fight broke out involving up to 25 people while cops were speaking to witnesses, FOX8 reports.

People were knocked to the ground in the fight and a woman could be heard yelling that her brother had been killed, according to reports.

The Parma Police Department said it “extends its deepest condolences to the families and loved ones of those who lost their lives in this tragic incident”.



On its website, Pandora’s Magical Events describes itself as a “modern, intimate event space”, which is “perfect for weddings, receptions, bridal showers, birthday parties and other special celebrations”.

News.title: Russian sailor threatens to shoot dead crewmate after warship crashes into refuelling vessel off Kent coast
News.content:
KILL THREAT Russian sailor threatens to shoot dead crewmate after warship crashes into refuelling vessel off Kent coast







Next

A RUSSIAN sailor threatened to shoot dead his crewmate after their warship crashed into a refuelling vessel off the Kent coast.

The heavily-armed Neustrashimy smashed into the Valentin Rykov while attempting to secure itself to it in rough seas between October 21 and October 23.

Radio transmissions revealed after an engineer delayed the operation over an issue with paperwork, one crew member fumed: “We need to bring him out onto the helipad and execute him there in front of everyone.”

Another crew said: “F***, this is an absolute nightmare, I’m getting really worked up.”





They added: “We’ve just been waiting around for this f***ing ridiculous wind and current.”

The operation was later abandoned and both crews the headed to shorelines off eastern Scotland where they managed to refuel, The Times reports.

A defence source described the collision as a “shambolic and reckless” display of seamanship that risked spilling oil into British waters and probably left the vessels with damage to their hulls and upper decks.

The warship only had two days worth of fuel left during its botched attempt to raft together with the vessel.



Earlier this year sanctioned Russian vessels were still sailing through the English Channel at a rate of almost one a day – with experts warning Andy Burnham must act now to stop tyrant Vladimir Putin.

A Sun investigation revealed that at least 28 ‘banned’ boats were caught on radar transiting the channel since June 19.

It included many flying under a false flag, like Gabon, Panama or Comoros, which are part of Putin’s illegal “shadow fleet” of tankers.

Our probe tracked more than 600 Foreign Office-sanctioned boats around the world using open-source radar tracking data.

News.title: Paedo Gary Glitter’s outrageous jail demands – from poster of HIMSELF to luxury watches… and he’s not the only one
News.content:
YOU WANT WHAT? Paedo Gary Glitter’s outrageous jail demands – from poster of HIMSELF to luxury watches… and he’s not the only one







Next

HIGH-profile jailbirds think they can demand the world while inside.

And paedo Gary Glitter – who the Sun revealed has won a new parole hearing – is no different.



This hearing could be the pervert’s last chance at freedom before he dies.

Glitter, a glam-rock star of the 1970s, was first jailed in 1997 after being caught with 4,000 child abuse images.



He was released from prison in 2023 after serving half his 16-year sentence.

But he was recalled within weeks after the The Sun obtained footage of him at a halfway house hostel discussing net browsers and the dark web.



In a bid to make his second stint in jail more cushy, Glitter is said to have made a long list of outrageous demands.

Glitter, real name Paul Gadd, is understood to have had his designer clothes, Bluetooth headphones, an XBox and an expensive Longines watch delivered to his jail.

He also requested a copy of his own autobiography Leader, and a poster of himself in his glam-rock heyday, which is said to be plastered

on his cell wall.

Speaking out at the time, an insider told the Mirror: “It’s a disgrace this was allowed. He was recalled for utterly vile behaviour and is the most hated pervert in Britain.



“He’s a serial child abuser and this should not be happening.

“His poor victims would rather the belongings be burnt than transported at a cost to the taxpayer just in case he gets bored.”

Glitter is understood to spend his time locked up watching Freeview TV and DVDs that have been deemed suitable by jail censors.

And he is believed to be “on his last legs” as his health woes pile up with the prisoner often using a wheelchair to move around his Category C jail.

And he’s not the only one… Here we break down all the outrageous jail demands made by Britain’s most high-profile lags.



Russell Brand

The Sun this week revealed Russell Brand has been begging prison guards to let him use his specialist shampoos and hair loss pills over fears his trademark long locks will fall out behind bars.

The vain rapist pleaded with warders to let him have Alpecin caffeine shampoo and Propecia tablets, a prescription drug used to treat male pattern baldness.

Both were confiscated when he entered category A prison HMP Wandsworth at the start of his 10 and a half year sentence. He’s now in HMP Littlehey.

One insider told The Sun : “He was kicking off because he’s worried he’s going to lose his hair. He takes Propecia pills for his hair, but he had them confiscated inside.



“He isn’t allowed to take them because they’re not essential. They’re considered cosmetic.”

Finasteride, the drug in Propecia, is not available on the NHS for hair loss because baldness is classed as a cosmetic problem instead of a medical one.

Former comic Brand has already been shipped out to cushy category C prison HMP Littlehey in Cambridgeshire.

Experts say those who stop taking the daily pill can expect hair loss problems to return within six to 12 months.



Ronnie Kray

Twin brothers Ronnie and Reggie Kray ran a gangland empire in London during the 1950s and 60s and were sent to prison for 30 years for murder.

Ronnie spent 16 years in Broadmoor Hospital after being judged to be criminally insane before dying in 1995.

During his time in the high-security psychiatric hospital, Ronnie was allowed a few home comforts.

After his death, Ronnie’s second ex-wife Kate spoke out as some of the late screws’ possessions went up for auction.

She told the Mirror: “Ron did probably have nights out with Diana Dors and Barbara Windsor in the dinner jacket with velvet lapels, but he wore the green Lester Bowden sports jacket, in Broadmoor.



“Because it’s a hospital not a prison, inmates wear their own clothes. And Ron took advantage of this privilege.

“He had his tailors go in to measure him up for Italian-cut suits. I’d get them dry-cleaned but he got inmates to iron his shirts and polish his shoes. I gave him a Giorgio Armani tie.

“He sent me to Russell & Bromley to get crocodile shoes. He’d say: ‘Don’t worry if the size isn’t quite right, I’ve hardly got far to walk’.”

Ronnie also kept a framed portrait of Kate by his bed alongside a clock with a canary in a cage, as well as watches, including one sent to him from twin brother Reggie and gold cufflinks.



Charles Bronson

One of the most demanding prisoners living at taxpayers’ expense is also one of the country’s most notorious – Charles Bronson.

Now in his 70s, his weekly menu requests include an astonishing 18 bacon rolls, whole goose and chicken, 10 Pot Noodles, a big tub of ice cream, curry, steak and chips.

He also wanted ‘liquid Wednesdays’ featuring three pints of Guinness, and gallons of tea, coffee, water and squash



But he won’t get any of that inside, instead directing his requests to his then wife and former Coronation Street actress Paula Williamson.

The ‘Salvador diet’ was his dream should he ever get

released.

Bronson was convicted of armed robbery in 1974 and has earned a reputation as a violent and dangerous inmate.

He has held 11 hostages in nine different sieges – including governors, doctors, staff and, on one occasion, his solicitor.

In one chilling siege, Bronson ambushed a jail librarian, demanding an inflatable doll, a helicopter and a cup of tea.



Robert Maudsley

Serial killer Robert Maudsley tried his luck by writing directly to a newspaper for his prison cell demands.

Quadruple killer – who was given the name Hannibal the Cannibal – killed a fellow inmate by jamming a plastic spoon in their ear after taking them hostage and torturing them.

He’s spent most of his time inside in solitary confinement.

In 2000 he wrote a series of letters to The Times asking why he couldn’t have a pet budgie, promising to love it and “not eat it”.



He also questioned why he couldn’t have a TV to “see the world” as well as classical music tapes and pictures. He wrote: “Why can’t I have a budgie instead of the flies and cockroaches and spiders I currently have? I promise to love it and not eat it.”

In another, he wrote: “If the prison service says no then I ask for a simple cyanide capsule which I shall willingly take and the problem of Robert John Maudsley can easily and swiftly be resolved.”

… and it’s not just famous faces

This summer, we reported how prisoners are flaunting their cells on social media – complete with TVs, games consoles and cupboards crammed with food.

A Sun investigation unearthed dozens of videos posted online which show lags bragging about their set-up, which also include rows of trainers, laptops, and impressive speaker systems.

All of the footage appeared to have been filmed on illicit mobile phones and posted online, despite handsets and internet access being prohibited across all UK prisons.



The behind-bars videos are a far cry from the bleak image many Brits associate with prison life and raises questions about the standards of security and access to contraband.

Vanessa Frake, former prison governor of Wormwood Scrubs said: “The broadcast of recent “Jail Tok” footage from within His Majesty’s Prison Service represents an appalling and absolute breakdown of institutional control that will deeply shock the public and veteran prison professionals alike.

“I find the images entirely unbelievable and deeply offensive to the standards of our profession.”

Andrea Coomber, Chief Executive at the Howard League for Penal Reform, said: “People in prisons should not be filming videos on banned mobile phones and sharing them online. However, the ability to earn privileges encourages good behaviour, and access to equipment and extra food forms a key motivating factor for those who are locked up.

“Ultimately, many problems in prison are exacerbated by the poor regimes across our system. Week after week, we see inspection reports showing that men are spending up to 23 hours a day locked in their cells with nothing to do.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Overcrowded and overstretched prisons are not able to provide the work, education and training that ought to be getting men out of their cells and into more productive pursuits, and the result is not just boredom but adverse impacts on mental health, violence and rehabilitation.”

News.title: Medication expert issues warning to certain Wegovy and Mounjaro users
News.content:
Medication expert issues warning to certain Wegovy and Mounjaro users

The expert clarified how to get the latest guidance for your weight loss medication

View 2 Images There are several weight loss treatments you can get, both in injection and pill form (Image: Getty)

People taking Wegovy or Mounjaro may need to seek medical professional help regarding their weight loss treatment. A medication expert spoke out to explain the guidance that applies depending on your situation.

‌



‌



Dr Kate Bunyan, medical director at heart check test kit provider PocDoc, said these new medications to help people lose weight are a major development, but they have to be used properly. The treatment expert said: "Weight loss medications such as Mounjaro and Wegovy have become an important development in obesity management, offering significant benefits for people who are clinically eligible."

‌



'Important consideration'

However, she added some words of caution for those thinking of using a weight loss medication. One group of people she says should take care are women who take the contraceptive pill. Dr Bunyan said: "One important consideration for women is how treatment fits alongside reproductive health.

‌



Paul Whitehouse says he's "on diabetes territory" after health tests

"Women taking Mounjaro who use the pill (combined or progestogen-only) are advised to use a barrier method as well for four weeks after starting treatment and for four weeks after each dose increase, or to switch to a non-oral method. This is because Mounjaro slows how quickly the stomach empties, which can reduce how well the pill is absorbed. Vomiting or diarrhoea, which are common side effects, can have a similar effect."

Ensure our latest health headlines always appear at the top of your Google Search by making us a Preferred Source. Click here to activate or add us as Preferred Source in your Google search settings.

‌



Barrier methods are physical ways to prevent you from conceiving, such as condoms or cervical caps. In contrast, if you are trying to become pregnant, you may want to talk to your doctor before starting a course of weight loss medication.

'Not recommended'

Dr Bunyan said: "Women who are planning a pregnancy should talk to their healthcare professional first. Like many medicines, weight loss treatments such as Mounjaro and Wegovy aren't recommended during pregnancy.

‌



"That's because they haven't been tested in pregnant women in clinical trials, so we don't have the evidence to know they’re safe. Each medicine needs to be stopped for a set period before trying to conceive, and that period differs between treatments."

Whatever your gender, if you decide to try a weight loss treatment it's important to understand the guidance. The expert said: "Whether you're a man or a woman, the most important thing is to read the instructions that come with your medication in full, and to ask your prescriber or pharmacist if anything isn't clear."

‌



How do I find out the official guidance for my weight loss medication?

If you want to do some research to make sure you have all the information about your particular medication, the doctor explained what to do. Dr Bunyan said: "The best starting point is always the healthcare professional prescribing your medication, who can give advice tailored to your individual health needs and treatment plan."

View 2 Images There is a range of weight loss treatments you can get (Image: Getty)

‌



Some other official sources of information to note include:

If you are buying online, check that the pharmacy is registered with the General Pharmaceutical Council (GPhC)

The NHS and the Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA) are also "reliable sources" of information - they can provide guidance on how different treatments work, how they should be taken and any updates to prescribing advice.

Article continues below

Another basic check is to read the leaflet that comes with your medication. Dr Bunyan explained: "People should also read the patient information leaflet supplied with their medication, as recommendations vary between treatments.

"The electronic medicines compendium (emc) is another useful resource, with detailed information about medicines licensed in the UK."

News.title: Theresa May fires off Brexit warning to Andy Burnham as PM pledges closer EU ties
News.content:
Theresa May fires off Brexit warning to Andy Burnham as PM pledges closer EU ties

Theresa May and Tony Blair became the latest political heavyweights to weigh in on Andy Burnham's push for closer ties with Europe after a crunch summit in Brussels

View 2 Images Theresa May broke her silence on Brexit as Andy Burnham pushes for closer ties (Image: PA)

Theresa May has warned Andy Burnham to "move on" from Brexit amid spiralling tensions over the Prime Minister's plans to move closer to the EU.

‌



The former Tory Prime Minister, whose premiership was wrecked by rows over the EU divorce, said: "Brexit is done. Just accept Brexit and move on".

Sir Tony Blair also waded into the row, saying any return to the bloc should be conditional on reform of the EU.

Mr Burnham told a Brussels summit on Friday he would kick off a "brainstorming" process on how the UK could move closer to the bloc, after finalising deals on food and drink, emissions and a youth mobility scheme. But the summit was dominated by a row over demands for cuts to tuition fees paid by EU students in the UK, which has not yet been agreed.

The PM, who said he wanted to see Brexit reversed in his lifetime, has left all options on the table after the next election. Labour's red lines - no customs union, single market or freedom of movement - will remain in place until the end of this Parliament.

To see more of the stories you love from The Mirror and to find them easily in Google then make us your preferred source. Free and easy-to-do, just click on the link here to find more from The Mirror at the top of your feed.

View 2 Images Andy Burnham received a warm welcome from European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen and President of the EU Council Antonio da Costa at the summit (Image: Getty Images)

Andy Burnham would be 'crazy' not to look for closer ties with the EU READ MORE :

The PM is expected to spell out the next steps when he sets out his 10-year plan for Britain next month. The move has been hailed by pro-EU MPs, with former Foreign Secretary David Lammy among those calling for a second referendum. But opening the door to rejoining the bloc has sparked widespread tensions.

Speaking to the BBC's Laura Kuenssberg, Baroness May said: "What I saw was that the extent of those negotiations, the hours that have to be put in - it's across the whole of government.

"It's not just prime ministerial time, cabinet ministers' time, officials' time, to-ing and fro-ing on those negotiations. Because you have to negotiate hard in order to make sure that you're getting out what you want.

"And that's one of the reasons why I look slightly aghast at what Andy Burnham is talking about, further negotiations of going into the EU. And also we, as a country, we voted for Brexit.

"When I was Prime Minister I was very clear, we should deliver on that vote. So I'm afraid my message to him really is, you know, people voted for Brexit. Brexit is done. Just accept Brexit and move on."

Tony Blair also warned the PM to be cautious about rejoining the EU. The Europhile ex-PM has long been a critic of Brexit, but he told The Sunday Times: "I was painted as saying Britain should just go back and rejoin - I'm not saying that - it's heavily conditioned."

He said: "The problem if we go back and join Europe is that; I can't say that the technology revolution is the single biggest thing, and then if Europe moves in the wrong direction on technology innovation, which they might do and presently probably are doing, that it's a good idea for Britain to rejoin. That's what's changed in this last ten years."

It comes after Alan Johnson, who launched Labour’s 2016 campaign to remain in Europe, told the Sunday Mirror to continue his push for closer EU ties - but not spend political capital on a second referendum.

The former Cabinet Minister said: "Europe is still the biggest commercial market in the world — bigger than China, bigger than America. Right on our doorstep, we would be crazy not to look for closer ties. Particularly as the deal that Johnson did was so awful.”

But he warned the PM's time could become “devoted to this one single issue”. Mr Johnson said: “What I don’t want to see is another referendum."

News.title: Pharmacist issues '7-day rule' warning to anyone taking regular NHS prescriptions
News.content:
Pharmacist issues '7-day rule' warning to anyone taking regular NHS prescriptions

The advice follows the Government's Be Ready campaign

View 3 Images Do not stockpile medication, the pharmacist warns (Image: georgeclerk via Getty Images)

People across the UK are being urged to prepare for potential disruption from cyberattacks and other emergencies under a new national initiative. The Be Ready campaign advises keeping three days' worth of food, water and other essentials, but one key item many could overlook is medication.

‌



‌



In a message to anyone who relies on medication, a pharmacist has urged people to keep an adequate supply of their regular medicines and to order repeat prescriptions at least a week in advance, so they are prepared should anything happen. However, while some people may be stockpiling food, the pharmacist warned the same approach shouldn’t be taken with medication.

‌



Duncan Reid, Deputy Superintendent Pharmacist at Pharmacy2U explained: "With the Government encouraging households to prepare for emergencies, it's important that people don't overlook access to their regular medication.

‌



“New NHS England figures reveal that more than one in four NHS 111 Online sessions are now for urgent repeat prescriptions, suggesting that a significant number of patients are already finding themselves in situations where they urgently need access to their regular medication."

This can have 'serious health consequences'

Running out of medication isn’t just an inconvenience - it can have a serious impact on a person’s health. And Duncan stresses that this is the last thing you need in an emergency.

View 3 Images Duncan Reid, Deputy Superintendent Pharmacist at Pharmacy2U (Image: Pharmacy2U)

‌



He said: "For people managing long-term conditions, suddenly running out of medication can have serious health consequences. Patients should always aim to have an adequate supply of their regular medication and order repeat prescriptions at least seven working days before running out. This allows time for GP approval, dispensing and delivery, helping to avoid an unnecessary last-minute emergency."

Do not stockpile

Duncan stressed that preparation should be sensible, without stockpiling. He urged people to buy only what they’ll use and to check with a pharmacist if they’re unsure what’s safe for them or their family.

‌



He urged: “This is about sensible preparation, not stockpiling. People should buy only what they are likely to use, keep medicines in their original packaging, follow the instructions and check expiry dates regularly.

"Over-the-counter medicines are not suitable for everyone, particularly children, people who are pregnant, those with certain health conditions or anyone taking other medicines. Anyone unsure about what is appropriate for them or their family should speak to a pharmacist.”

‌



Have a 'well-stocked medicine cabinet'

The medications expert said a few simple health essentials can make a big difference if day-to-day life is briefly disrupted - think pain relief and antihistamines to first-aid basics and hygiene items. While urging people against stockpiling, he said they should get into the habit of checking ingredients and expiry dates and speaking to a pharmacist if they need help.

Duncan explains: “A well-stocked medicine cabinet can help people manage common minor illnesses during a short period of disruption. Depending on the needs of the household, useful items may include paracetamol and, where suitable, ibuprofen, an antihistamine, indigestion relief, oral rehydration salts and anti-diarrhoeal treatment where appropriate. A basic first-aid kit and digital thermometer are also sensible additions.

‌



View 3 Images Always consult a doctor if you are worried (Image: Peter Dazeley/Getty)

“It is also worth checking practical health and hygiene essentials, such as toothpaste, period or continence products, contact lens solution, an up-to-date pair of glasses, sunscreen and any dressings, testing equipment or other medical supplies used regularly by someone in the household.

‌



“For contact lens wearers, I would also recommend keeping an up-to-date pair of glasses available as a backup. Water or saliva should never be used as a substitute for contact lens solution.

“Cough and cold medicines can be helpful for relieving particular symptoms, but people should check the active ingredients carefully. Many combination cold and flu remedies already contain paracetamol, so taking them alongside another paracetamol-containing medicine could result in someone taking more than the recommended dose."

Article continues below

Pharmacist’s top tips for preparing your medicine cabinet

Stay on top of repeat prescriptions: Order regular medication at least seven working days before running out, rather than waiting until your final few doses. Keep essential over-the-counter medicines at home: Consider having a sensible supply of everyday essentials such as paracetamol, ibuprofen, antihistamines, antiseptic creams and basic first-aid supplies, where appropriate for your household. Keep a record of your medication: Write down the names and doses of any regular prescriptions, so you have the information available if your phone, internet or usual pharmacy services are disrupted. Check expiry dates: Review your medicine cabinet regularly, replacing expired products and storing medication correctly. Get your repeat prescriptions online: Managing your repeat prescriptions online can make it easier to keep track of your medication, check what you need and order in good time, helping avoid last-minute requests or unnecessary trips to the pharmacy. You can also have your NHS repeat prescriptions delivered directly to your door at no additional cost, helping you maintain a regular supply of essential medication. Prepare, don’t stockpile: Being prepared doesn't mean panic-buying or building up unnecessary supplies of medication and first-aid essentials. Keep a sensible amount of what your household needs, and only order medication you require, avoiding requests for additional supplies unless clinically necessary. If you're unsure what to include in your medicine cabinet or concerned about accessing medication during an emergency, speak to your pharmacist for advice.

News.title: Pharmacist issues warning to anyone who uses daily pill organiser
News.content:
Pharmacist issues warning to anyone who uses daily pill organiser

A UK pharmacist has issued a warning over a common item found in millions of homes

View 4 Images The pharmacist advises checking before mixing daily supplements with prescriptions (Image: Getty)

A pharmacist has issued a warning to anyone who uses a pill organiser. Phil Day, Superintendent Pharmacist at Pharmacy2U, said that while it may seem like a simple solution, "not all medications are suitable" for doing this - and it "can sometimes cause problems."

‌



‌



A pill organiser is a small box with separate compartments for tablets and supplements. It's usually labelled with the days of the week, and meant to be pre-filled so each section contains the doses you need for each day. Often available online for around £5, they’re useful for keeping medication organised, simplifying your routine by reducing the number of bottles, helping to avoid missed or double doses, and making it easier to take pills when travelling.

‌



View 4 Images Phil Day, Superintendent Pharmacist at Pharmacy2U (Image: Pharmacy2U)

‌



Why it might be a problem

While the idea is a good one, it is not always suitable for all types of medication. The pharmacist explains: “Weekly pill organisers can be a convenient way to keep track of daily medication, particularly for people on several prescriptions or taking multiple supplements. Not all medicines are suitable for storing outside their original packaging, however, and mixing different tablets in the same compartment can sometimes cause problems.

“Some medications are sensitive to moisture, heat or light, meaning removing them from their protective packaging could lead to them breaking down and potentially reduce how well they work. Even storing certain capsules and tablets together can cause moisture to transfer between them, potentially affecting their effectiveness.

“There's also a common misconception that many vitamins and supplements are harmless because they're natural or available over the counter. In reality, some can interfere with how prescribed medicines work, making it important to check what can safely be taken together."

‌
