The result means seventh-seeded Columbus, the 2023 champions, can eliminate Messi and Miami from the playoffs with a victory in Game 2 of the best-of-three series in Ohio next Friday.

“It was a game where nothing went right for us, and we effectively created their chances for them,” Miami coach Kily González said afterwards.

“We didn’t produce the great performance we had hoped for. Everything went wrong, but we have to learn from it because next time, if we don’t win, we’re out.

“There’s no better challenge for us as a team than this. It’s a test of character, and I know my team has that character.”

FC Dallas 3-0 Portland Timbers

Joaquín Valiente scored twice in the space of two minutes as FC Dallas beat the Portland Timbers 3-0 in the opening game of their best-of-three Western Conference first-round series.

The 25-year-old Uruguayan midfielder broke the deadlock in the 53rd minute, volleying home a rebound after Daniel Job’s shot was parried by Portland goalkeeper James Pantemis.

Valiente doubled the lead two minutes later, timing his run to meet another pass from Job before redirecting the ball between Pantemis’s legs.

Samuel Sarver completed the scoring in the fourth minute of stoppage time, finishing a cross from Logan Farrington on the counterattack.

Dallas goalkeeper Daniel de Sousa Britto, known simply as Daniel, made four saves, while Pantemis finished with five for Portland.

The Timbers also lost Ariel Lassiter to an apparent injury in the 33rd minute.

Second-seeded Dallas can advance to the Western Conference semi-finals with a victory in Portland next Saturday.

New England Revolution 2-0 Philadelphia Union

Teenager Peyton Miller scored one goal and helped create another as the New England Revolution beat the Philadelphia Union 2-0 in the opening game of their Eastern Conference first-round series.

The 19-year-old Miller became the fifth-youngest goalscorer in MLS Cup playoffs history when he volleyed home a cross from Jack Harrison in the 73rd minute, his effort bouncing off the crossbar and into the net.

New England had taken the lead in the 10th minute when Miller’s shot from the edge of the penalty area deflected off Philadelphia defender Nathan Harriel for an own goal.

Harrison, who came on as a substitute in the 62nd minute, was making his first appearance since 9 September after missing more than two months with a quadriceps injury.

Philadelphia nearly equalized in the 37th minute when Cavan Sullivan turned and fired a shot from outside the penalty area that struck the left post.

The Union fielded the youngest starting lineup in MLS Cup playoffs history, with an average age of 23 years and 207 days, breaking the record set by the New York Red Bulls in 2022.

Matt Turner made two saves to preserve the shutout for New England, who can advance to the Eastern Conference semi-finals with a victory in Philadelphia next Saturday.

Sports.title: European football: Doué carried off for PSG while Kane vows to return fresh
Sports.content:
Désiré Doué was carried off in tears after suffering what looked like a nasty knee injury as Paris Saint-Germain beat Nice 3-2 in Ligue 1.

Doué went down after twisting awkwardly late in the first half as he tried to control the ball, shortly after scoring to put PSG 2-1 ahead. The match was stopped for five minutes to allow Doué to receive treatment to his right knee before he was carried off to a backdrop of applause from the crowd at the Allianz Riviera stadium.

PSG will now be dreading discovering the extent of the injury, having lost Khvicha Kvaratskhelia to a ruptured anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee playing against Barcelona last month. The Georgian winger is unlikely to return this season, and Doué looks set for a significant spell on the sidelines too.

“We will need to wait until tomorrow for the test results, but it is obviously a serious injury,” PSG’s coach, Luis Enrique, told the broadcaster Ligue 1+.

Mohamed Amoura had given Nice the lead only for Senny Mayulu to equalise with a penalty awarded after a video assistant referee (VAR) check for a handball.

Doué – who was wearing a mouthguard after one of his teeth became dislodged while playing for France against Italy during the international break – put PSG ahead a minute later, turning in at the back post from an Achraf Hakimi assist for his sixth of the season in all competitions.

His replacement, Ferran Torres, scored PSG’s third in the 85th minute, controlling in the box before finishing on the turn for his eighth goal of the season – but first in two months. Ali Abdi pulled one back for Nice in stoppage time, but their run of three straight wins was ended as PSG made it 12 victories on the bounce.

Lazio will continue their surprise stay at the top of Serie A for at least another week after thumping Lecce 3-0, while a red-hot Donyell Malen scored four at Parma to lift Roma up to second.

Gennaro Gattuso’s Lazio are two points ahead of their local rivals thanks to goals in each half from Tijjani Noslin and a late Davide Frattesi strike. Inter would close to within a point of Lazio with a win at struggling Atalanta on Sunday.

“I am proud of the mentality and the hunger shown today,” said Gattuso to Dazn. “It’s all down to the players, they have the right mentality, hunger and team spirit. What they are doing is incredible.”

Malen took his tally in all competitions for Roma this season to 16 before Wednesday’s daunting Champions League clash at Paris Saint-Germain. The Netherlands forward opened the scoring six minutes before half-time with a brilliant touch and finish, and put Roma, also unbeaten in the league, back in the lead in the 68th minute. Rodrigo Mora added Roma’s third moments later and then Malen capped another superb display with two more expert finishes.

Scott McTominay’s second-half strike gave Napoli a hard-earned 1-0 win over Torino to ease the pressure on manager Massimiliano Allegri, while Como stayed six points behind the leaders in fourth with a 2-0 home win over Cagliari.

In Spain, Kylian Mbappé’s third miss in his last six penalty attempts for club and country did not prove costly as ⁠Carlos Espi’s late winner helped Real Madrid to a 2-1 home victory over Celta Vigo. Real have 33 points from ⁠13 La Liga games, level ⁠with leaders Barcelona, ​but have now played a game more. The Catalans are in action on Sunday at home to Villarreal.

View image in fullscreen Kylian Mbappé reacts after he misses from the penalty spot. Photograph: Susana Vera/Reuters

Mbappé’s wastefulness from 12 yards had already ⁠cost Real a point earlier in the season and this time it was almost two as he lifted his effort well over the crossbar. He also ⁠missed a penalty when the Madrid side lost 1-0 at Real Betis in September, and for France ​against Morocco in the World Cup. On both ‌those occasions he shot ‌low and saw his effort saved, which perhaps might explain why he tried to go high ‌this time.

Celta took the lead inside six minutes when Pablo Durán scored from close range as he turned in Williot Swedberg’s low cross. Real had the chance to pull level when Mbappé had his arm pulled by Celta defender Javier Rodriguez and the referee pointed to the spot, but the Frenchman could not convert.

Real were level on 66 minutes when Jude ‌Bellingham drilled the ball low into the net from just inside box. It looked as though they would be frustrated before Espi’s initial header was saved by ​goalkeeper Ionut Radu, but he turned in the rebound.

Kike Salas equalised in added time at the end of the game as Sevilla earned a 1-1 draw with Real Betis in the Seville derby. Antony netted for the visitors early in the second half with his first goal of the season ⁠but Betis were denied a place in the top three by the equaliser.

Deportivo ​Alaves ended an eight-game winless ​streak with a 3-1 home victory ​over Deportivo La Coruna. Angel Perez opened the scoring for the hosts, but ​they were pegged back ‌to 1-1 by ​an own goal from ​Nahuel Tenaglia. Lucas Boye, who earlier missed a penalty, scored Alaves’ second and the points were made safe when Denis Suarez netted in added time. Valencia moved out of the bottom three with a 1-0 away win at Rayo Vallecano thanks to Jose Copete’s first half headed goal.

In Germany, Borussia Dortmund’s Felix Nmecha fired his side to the top of ⁠the Bundesliga table as they won 1-0 at bottom side Borussia Mönchengladbach. After Bayern Munich ⁠were held to ⁠a ​1-1 draw at home by Cologne on Friday, Dortmund capitalised to take a two-point lead at the summit.

The home side played far better ⁠than their position would suggest, ​withstanding waves of pressure ‌from the visitors, ‌but Gladbach finally cracked in the 80th minute when Nmecha picked ‌up the ball on the edge of a packed penalty area and let fly. Unsighted by the thicket of bodies in front of him, the goalkeeper Daniel Batz misjudged the trajectory of the ball, and it flew over his right shoulder ‌and into the net.

View image in fullscreen Felix Nmecha fires home Borussia Dortmund’s winner against Borussia Mönchengladbach. Photograph: Christopher Neundorf/EPA

Gladbach created a number of chances, but Gregor Kobel came to the rescue ​with several fine saves for Dortmund, and once the goal went in, there was no way back for the hosts. Dortmund have 24 points after 10 games, two ahead of Bayern and third-placed Freiburg, who ⁠beat Elversberg 1-0.

Meanwhile, FifPro said it was “deeply concerned” by public comments from Bayern’s leadership about Jamal Musiala’s contract, accusing the German ⁠champions of putting pressure on the midfielder while he recovers from health problems. The global players’ union was responding to recent remarks by senior Bayern officials, including ⁠honorary president Uli Hoeness, ⁠chief executive Jan-Christian Dreesen ​and supervisory board member Karl-Heinz Rummenigge, about Musiala’s future at the club.

Hoeness this month questioned whether the 23-year-old Germany international could return to his ⁠previous level after being diagnosed with a neurological disorder. Dreesen later backed those remarks, saying Bayern would evaluate Musiala’s progress and discuss his future with his representatives. Rummenigge subsequently defended ⁠the comments, saying the club’s consideration of Musiala’s health and contract situation was both responsible and normal.

“Bayern’s honorary ​president, chief executive and former chief executive ‌have all publicly questioned Musiala’s contract ‌in quick succession,” Fifpro said in a statement. “In FifPro’s view, this is a coordinated strategy to put ‌pressure on Musiala and his representatives ahead of any negotiations. A club of Bayern’s standing should know better.”

Musiala signed a contract extension with Bayern until 2030 in February last year. He has endured a difficult run of injuries and health setbacks in recent months. He broke his leg at the Club World Cup in July 2025, missed half of last season and collapsed twice within a ‌few days in August before being diagnosed with a neurological disorder. In September, he suffered a hamstring injury.

After September’s injury, Musiala returned as a substitute in Bayern’s 1-1 home draw with Cologne in the Bundesliga on Friday in which Harry Kane sustained an injury that may mean months of rehabilitation. On Saturday, Kane said he was looking to come back improved for “the business end of the season”. Kane tore a ligament in his left ankle and Bayern said the Ballon d’Or winner had undergone “successful surgery overnight” having earlier said that Kane would be out for “the next few months”.

Kane posted a photo on Instagram of himself smiling broadly, while sitting on a hospital bed after the surgery, with his leg encased in a medical boot. “The highs and lows of life!” the 33-year-old wrote. “Obviously very disappointed to get this injury but as always it’s an opportunity to show resilience and improvement going into 2027. I’ll be back fresh and ready to go for the business end of the season.”

Sports.title: Champion’s corner: KC Current win first NWSL Championship with 2-1 stunner over Spirit
Sports.content:
It took five years, 90 minutes and a goal for the ages, but the Kansas City Current have their first-ever NWSL championship.

Riding a wave of momentum created by a 54th-minute Olimpico from midfielder Vanessa DiBernardo, and capping it off with an all-important breakaway winner from Debinha, the Current silenced the partisan, sellout crowd at the heavily-favored Washington Spirit’s home ground with a 2-1 victory on Saturday.

The Spirit, heartbroken at the final whistle, have now lost three consecutive NWSL Championships.

“Obviously this one hates way worse than any of the other ones,” forward Trinity Rodman said afterward. “I don’t even think you have words in this moment — it is too fresh.”

DiBernardo’s goal was stunning, a driven, bent corner kick played to the far post that eluded Spirit goalkeeper Sandy MacIver, her defenders and Current forward Haley Hopkins, potentially DiBernardo’s intended target. The Spirit’s players and fans alike pleaded with center referee Joshua Encarnación, suggesting he examine the play on VAR for obstruction, as MacIver had potentially been screened. The review never came.

Whether played directly on goal intentionally or otherwise, the effort will go down as one of the most memorable in NWSL Championship history. At 34, DiBernardo becomes the oldest player in league history to score in a final, and was later named the match’s MVP.

“I’ve been to the game a few times and haven’t won, but this one just felt a little lighter,” said DiBernardo, who gave birth to Charlie, her first child, in January and took time off before returning to the Current in March. “I think just having Charlie, it just brings a different perspective on life. I knew the game was big and it was a big moment, but just kinda having her, just spending the day with her, it just felt really special.”

The game’s early phases were forgettable save for one incident which would go on to affect the remainder of the match: a bruising, high-speed tackle on Rodman by Current defender Laney Rouse in the fifth minute. The challenge sent Rodman flying and appeared to injure her left elbow; the Spirit forward, nearing tears, spent much of the first half in visible pain and seemingly never fully recovered. Rouse was not cautioned for the challenge.

“[It helped set the tone] in the sense that it hurt really bad, yes,” Rodman said. “As a team, you always want to put the first hit in. You’re taught to do that. Credit to them. I wish I was the one who put her on the ground. They did a really good job at setting the tone and controlling the first half.”

It was far from the game’s only physical moment. Neither team managed to settle into any meaningful rhythm during an opening 45 that felt at times more like a title fight than a title match. Encarnación, involved in his first NWSL final, called a very tight match and the near-constant stoppages in play were the defining characteristic of a sometimes ugly opening phase. In many ways it was not entirely his fault: the message-sending start from KC and the Spirit’s subsequent response often compelled him to act. The 19 combined first-half fouls between both sides were the most in any half of any NWSL title match in league history.

“It felt like we couldn’t play more than two minutes without a whistle,” Rodman said. “We were fouling, they were true calls for sure — but I think you lose control of the game really quickly that way ... It definitely messed with our rhythm a little bit.”

Paradoxically, though, the match was won with speed. Deep into second-half stoppage time, the Current found their eventual match-winner on a breakaway. After doggedly winning back possession after a Spirit free kick late on, Kansas City forward Debinha streaked upfield from just beyond the center stripe, looking off a wide-open Temwa Chawinga and rounding MacIver who looked on hopelessly as the Brazilian slotted it home.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Moments later, Rodman – somehow still in the match after not only the early challenge but a later high-speed collision with Current goalkeeper Lorena – pulled one back for the Spirit. Falling away from goal 10 yards out, Rodman got her head on the end of a Tara Rudd cross, placing it perfectly over Lorena’s outstretched arms and into the far-side netting. The ensuing five minutes – the game ended in the 102nd – were chaotic but the Spirit couldn’t quite find the equalizer.

After a slow start, the Current were well-managed by former Major League Soccer and US national team member Chris Armas. Armas was widely considered a controversial selection at the time of his appointment but proceeded to lead the club to their first championship in his first season, doing so by beating Gotham FC and now the Spirit, two sides picked by many as potential league-winners.

“I think from the front to the back we made it a point that every person on this team defends and if somebody is going to make a mistake the other person is going to have their back,” Current defender Izzy Rodriguez said. “We try and turn every 1v1 situation into a 1v2 for us, and I think that showed up today. We were winning our duels and second balls and those are things that win games.”

For the Spirit, the loss is devastating. They become the first American professional club – men’s or women’s – to lose three consecutive finals since the New England Revolution of Major League Soccer, who did so in the mid 2000s. In their five Championship appearances, the Spirit have won just one time, in 2021.

Sports.title: talkSPORT tips – Best football bets and expert advice for Sunday 22 November
Sports.content:
All eyes will be on Anfield on Sunday afternoon as Mauricio Pochettino takes charge of Manchester United for the first time, hoping to spark a response away at old foes Liverpool.

The Red Devils have been in complete disarray this season and are in the relegation places after ten matches, so are in need of a positive display on Merseyside.

High-flying Brighton head to Hull for Sunday’s supporting fixture in the Premier League, while there is also top-flight action in France, Germany, Italy and Spain.

Sports.title: Matthias Jaissle instantly apologises for X-rated Arsenal gaffe
Sports.content:
Matthias Jaissle gave an explicit assessment of Arsenal during a post-match gaffe after his Newcastle United side drew 2-2 with them.

The Magpies restricted the Premier League holders to just one point at St. James' Park on Saturday evening in an entertaining affair.



2 Jaissle was quick to apologise for the language he used when describing how good Arsenal are Credit: Getty

Harvey Barnes and Malick Thiaw hit back after Eberechi Eze opened the scoring, although Noni Madueke salvaged a draw for the champions late on.

Arsenal managed to avoid losing a league match for just the second time this season and remain at the summit with 11 played.

They also have the joint-best defence with Brighton having conceded just seven goals, and Jaissle is clearly impressed by their quality.



Jaissle apologises for swearing

During his post-match press conference, the Newcastle head coach was asked about how good this Arsenal team are.

"F****** good," he replied, before swiftly apologising for his coarse language as members of the press laughed at the comment.



Newcastle have only one league win from their last five, but the draw has taken them four points clear of the bottom three.

Arsenal on the other hand missed the chance to go eight points clear of Brighton at the top of the table with the Seagulls in action against Hull City on Sunday.



They will also be concerned over goalkeeper David Raya, who went off injured during the second half.

Raya went down holding his arm after an accidental collision with William Osula inside his area.

Kepa Arrizabalaga was brought on as his replacement in the 70th minute of play.

2 Arsenal were unable to beat Newcastle, but are still top of the league and on course for another title Credit: Getty



"We don't know, unfortunately," manager Mikel Arteta Arteta said on the severity of Raya's injury.

"Obviously he had to come off. We are worried, but we don't know. Tomorrow [Sunday], he will have an MRI."

The injury has come three days before Arsenal return to Champions League action with a home clash against Borussia Dortmund.

As it stands, Arrizabalaga looks set to start between the sticks on Tuesday night.



He has featured in the competition on just one occasion for Arsenal since signing from rivals Chelsea in 2025.

That appearance came in their last league phase match at home to Kazakhstan-based FC Kairat last season, which ended in a 3-2 win for Arsenal.

Sports.title: ‘Deeply concerned’ – Bayern Munich accused of ‘coordinated strategy’ against Jamal Musiala
Sports.content:
FIFPRO has criticised members of the Bayern Munich hierarchy after their comments on Jamal Musiala and his contract situation.

Musiala was diagnosed with temporary episodes of absence, caused by a neurological condition, this summer after fainting twice during matches.



3 Bayern chiefs have come under fire for their comments on Musiala and his contract amid his health issue Credit: Getty

The 23-year-old came off the bench for Bayern on Friday night in the 1-1 Bundesliga draw with FC Koln as he returned from a muscle injury.

However, former club chief Karl-Heinz Rummenigge expressed their concerns over his contract, which runs until 2030.

Rummenigge claimed that financial aspects of his deal are 'no longer feasible' amid Musiala's health issue.



Honorary president Uli Hoeness also previously questioned whether Musiala can 'regain the performance level he once had', whilst chief executive Jan-Christian Dreesen warned of talks over his future.

Musiala backed in FIFPRO statement

FIFPRO, the international representative body of professional players, have now hit back at their comments in a strong statement.



"FIFPRO is deeply concerned by the repeated public statements from FC Bayern Munich's leadership calling into question the contract of Jamal Musiala as he returns from injury," it read.

"Bayern's honorary president, chief executive and former chief executive have all publicly questioned Musiala's contract in quick succession.



"In FIFPRO's view, this is a coordinated strategy to put pressure on Musiala and his representatives ahead of any negotiations. A club of Bayern's standing should know better.

"Bayern has a duty of care to Musiala. Across professional football, uncertainty about a player's future can take a toll on their mental health, particularly when they are recovering from injury. Making Musiala's health and future a matter of public debate adds to that pressure.

"Any concerns about his contract should be raised privately with him and his representatives.

3 Bayern boss Vincent Kompany returned to the dugout during their 1-1 draw with FC Koln on Friday after his collapse last month Credit: Getty



"Contracts are there to be respected. An injury or a dip in form gives a club no grounds to reopen terms it agreed to, just as a run of outstanding performances gives a player no automatic right to a pay rise.

"Clubs, leagues and player unions have agreed at FIFA level that contractual stability is a core principle of the game. It protects clubs as much as it protects players.

"FIFPRO stands with Jamal Musiala and with all players who honour their commitments. We expect their employers to do the same."

What next for Musiala?

According to reports in Germany, Musiala's contract includes a release clause that becomes active next year.



This opens the door for a possible move away from Bayern and to the Premier League.

Liverpool have previously been interested in a move, with rivals Manchester City also being a speculated destination in the past.

3 FIFPRO reminded Bayern of their duty of care with Musiala and sided with the player in a strong-worded statement Credit: Getty

Chelsea, where the attacking star played academy football from 2011 to 2019, are another club to have had links.



Musiala has scored two goals and assisted one other in five matches this season.

This has come in just 233 minutes of action amid his fitness issues.

Sports.title: Manchester United-linked Calvin Bassey responds to rumours as Fulham boss compares him to all-time great
Sports.content:
Manchester United-linked Calvin Bassey responds to rumours as Fulham boss compares him to all-time great

Fulham captain Calvin Bassey has confirmed he is in negotiations over extending his contract at the club.

Bassey's current deal with the Cottagers is set to expire at the end of the season.

2 Bassey has been with Fulham since July 2023 Credit: Getty

However, Fulham hold the option to extend it for an additional 12 months.

What has Calvin Bassey said about his Fulham future?

But Bassey looks poised to remain in the capital.

"We are negotiating, we are still talking," Bassey told TNT Sports after Fulham's 1-1 draw with Manchester City.

"It's an amazing place to be, I have settled in nicely and the manager has put a lot of faith and trust in me.

"It's nice to be here and hopefully we will see what happens with the negotiations."

Talks of a new contract to remain at Fulham comes amid rumours linking Bassey with a surprise switch to Manchester United.

The Red Devils are reported to be in the market for a centre-back in January after heavily investing in their midfield during the summer.

And Bassey, who has stepped up his game under Cottagers boss Alvaro Arbeloa, is reportedly being monitored by United.

Fulham boss Alvaro Arbeloa likens Calvin Bassey to Paolo Maldini

But Arbeloa will be extremely reluctant to lose his skipper, especially after a commanding display against City on Saturday.

"I told Calvin and David [Affengruber], 'You were like Maldini and Baresi today,'" Arbeloa told talkSPORT.

2 Arbeloa has Fulham on a five-match unbeaten run in the league Credit: Getty

"They are leaders and they are performing so well.

"We wanted to take the victory, but not a bad point."

Manchester City 1-1 Fulham

Rodrigo Muniz sparked hope of an unlikely victory at the Etihad Stadium when he struck in the 16th minute.

However, Elliot Anderson's goal just before the hour mark ensured the spoils were shared.

City thought they'd gone level earlier in the contest when Erling Haaland pounced on what appeared to be an error from Bernd Leno.

However, VAR decided Leno was in control of the ball, sparking a furious reaction from Haaland.

The result marked the first time Fulham avoided a loss to City in all competitions since September 2011.

As for City, they slumped to a fourth consecutive match without a win, leaving them six points behind league leaders Arsenal.

Sports.title: Mauricio Pochettino dealt blow with key Man United player to miss Liverpool clash
Sports.content:
Marcus Rashford is not fit enough to play for Manchester United this weekend against Liverpool, talkSPORT understands.

The winger has not played since October 13 due to a hip injury and is not expected to return to action at Anfield on Sunday.

2 Rashford will not feature for United against Liverpool due to injury in a blow to Pochettino ahead of his first match Credit: Getty

This comes as a blow to new United head coach Mauricio Pochettino as their injury list remains packed.

Manuel Ugarte, Benjamin Sesko, Luke Shaw and Carlos Baleba are all set to be sidelined for the match as well.

Rashford first sustained his injury during the 2026 World Cup with England and struggled to shake it off since.

His last appearance came in the 2-0 Champions League defeat away at Atletico Madrid.

The 29-year-old was then benched for the 1-1 Premier League draw with Leeds United.

Rashford struggles at United continue

With his latest setback, Rashford continues to endure a difficult first season back at United following his loan spell in Barcelona.

He hit 14 goals and 15 assists in a campaign that saw him return to his best form and win LaLiga at Camp Nou.

Barcelona had the option to buy him permanently for £26million, but they did not activate it and instead brought in Anthony Gordon.

This is despite Rashford revealing that he wanted to stay at the club given his success on loan.

United welcomed him back for the 2026/27 campaign and now wears the no. 9 shirt, having previously donned 39, 19 and 10.

2 Pochettino faces a gruelling start to life on the United touchline with a trip to their historic rivals Credit: Getty

However, he is yet to score or assist in any eight matches across all competitions this season.

Rashford has started six of those fixtures, four of which have come in the Premier League.

A January move to Everton has been speculated as he continues to refind his feet.

It would see him follow a similar path to Jack Grealish, who has done well for the Toffees after a dip at Manchester City.

Rashford has also missed the last two England camps despite being part of their World Cup squad.

He is on 78 caps and 19 goals with the Three Lions since making his debut in May 2016.

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta worried about David Raya as update on Arsenal star’s injury given
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta worried about David Raya as update on Arsenal star’s injury given

Mikel Arteta confirmed David Raya will undergo an MRI after he sustained an arm injury in Arsenal's 2-2 draw with Newcastle.

Raya exited the contest midway through the second half after what appeared to be an innocuous collision with Magpies striker Will Osula.

3 Raya's teammates were quick to console him following his arm injury Credit: Getty

The Spaniard briefly fell to the turf and then quickly got back to his feet, only to clutch his arm in serious pain.

It quickly became clear Raya could not continue and he made his way off with his left arm placed in a makeshift sling.

Raya was replaced by Kepa Arrizabalaga.

Mikel Arteta gives update on David Raya injury

Arteta now faces a nervy wait as to whether Raya will be fit to feature for the Gunners against Borussia Dortmund in the Champions League on Tuesday.

Speaking to media following the contest, the Arsenal boss admitted he was unsure how serious Raya's injury was.

"We don't know, unfortunately," Arteta said.

"Obviously we had to come off. We are worried, but we don't know.

"Tomorrow, he will have an MRI."

How Arsenal's draw with Newcastle unfolded

It was far from a vintage performance for the Gunners, who took the lead courtesy of Eberechi Eze.

Eze was slipped in behind Newcastle's defensive line and coolly slotted home with a first-time effort from close range.

3 Arteta's side will finish the weekend with a minimum three-point buffer to second-placed Brighton Credit: Getty

But a rare mistake from Martin Odegaard allowed the hosts back into the contest.

The Norwegian mis-kicked a throw-in from the left and sent the ball straight to Osula, who drove towards goal from the right before he laid it to Harvey Barnes.

Barnes, who was in plenty of space, gratefully slid the ball home past a diving Raya.

Newcastle then took the lead in bizarre fashion courtesy of Malick Thiaw.

3 Thiaw thought he'd scored the winner, but it was not to be Credit: Getty

A Dan Burn header towards goal landed into Joe Willock, who was being closely marked by Gabriel on the goal-line.

Thiaw was first to the loose ball and lashed it into the net, sparking wild scenes from the Toon faithful.

A VAR check for offside followed, but Thiaw's goal remained.

However, the hosts could not hang on for just their fourth league win of the season as Noni Madueke rescued a point for the Gunners in the 78th minute.

The winger capped off a blistering counter-attack when he cut in from the right flank onto his left foot and unleashed a strike that squirmed under Newcastle goalkeeper Lukas Hornicek.

Sports.title: Premier League player leaves stadium on crutches after freak injury coming out of tunnel
Sports.content:
Premier League player leaves stadium on crutches after freak injury coming out of tunnel

Coventry City were dealt a blow when Taiwo Awoniyi picked up a bizarre injury just before the second half.

The striker was on the score sheet for the Sky Blues in their impressive 3-2 win over Crystal Palace on Saturday.

2 Awoniyi got the Sky Blues on their way to a huge three points Credit: Getty

And Awoniyi may have scored more, only to hurt himself when he re-emerged for the final 45 minutes.

As he ran out of the tunnel, Awoniyi fell to the turf and clutched his leg, with two Palace players helping him off the ground.

The strange incident prompted Coventry boss Frank Lampard into an unplanned substitution as Sidiki Cherif was brought on in place of Awoniyi.

After the game, Awoniyi was filmed leaving the CBS Arena wearing a protective boot round his right foot and on crutches.

Frank Lampard gives update on Taiwo Awoniyi's injury

Lampard then confirmed following the match Awoniyi had felt his ankle in the first half, with the club to now fully assess the extent of the damage in the coming days.

"He hurt his ankle," Lampard said. "I don't know what the diagnosis is of that yet.

"He felt he could go and give it a try. Quite clearly, straight away he felt he couldn't."

How Coventry's win over Palace unfolded

Awoniyi got Coventry off to a dream start when he slotted home from close range in the fifth minute.

Sky Blues ace Jack Rudoni drove into the box on the left side and squared it to Awoniyi, who directed his effort past a diving Dean Henderson.

It was Awoniyi's second league goal this term for Coventry following his summer switch from Nottingham Forest.

2 Lampard has Coventry slowly creeping up the table after a difficult start Credit: Getty

Palace's Yeremy Pino equalised just eight minutes later, only for Tatsuhiro Sakamoto to restore the hosts' advantage on the half-hour mark.

But the two sides went into the break at 2-2 courtesy of Jorgen Strand Larsen, who lashed home from close range.

Yet there was one final twist to come in the 89th minute.

A long Coventry throw eventually found Brandon Thomas-Asante, who powered a header straight at Dean Henderson.

However, his save rebounded into a retreating Dwight McNeil and into the back of the net, sparking wild scenes among Sky Blues supporters.

The result marked Coventry's fourth league win this season and moved them up to 13th with 12 points.

As for Palace, who had Thomas Frank at the helm for the first time following his appointment, they remain rooted to the bottom of the ladder following their eighth defeat from 11 league games.

Sports.title: ‘Rotten’ – Shell-shocked Jason Cundy gives Xabi Alonso Chelsea sack warning as fans turn on manager
Sports.content:
Jason Cundy was a despondent man on the talkSPORT airwaves after watching his beloved Chelsea get thumped by Leeds United.

Leeds were 4-1 winners on Saturday in what was their first victory at Stamford Bridge in the Premier League since December 1999.



3 Leeds ended their 27-year wait to win at Stamford Bridge with a deserved victory against a dreadful Chelsea Credit: Getty

Noah Okafor scored two for the visitors, with Dominic Calvert-Lewin and Brenden Aaronson also netting against a woeful Chelsea side.

Cundy was at the Bridge and rushed to talkSPORT towers at the full-time whistle to join a gleeful Jamie O'Hara on the GameDay Phone-In.

'Disgusting' Chelsea leave Cundy worried

"We are rotten," he explained. "We were so bad, it was so bad... I'm in disbelief at what I've just witnessed."



The former Blues defender also expressed his concerns for manager Xabi Alonso amid a run of one win in five across all competitions.

A handful of fans were also heard chanting 'You don't know what you're doing!' to the Spaniard once Malo Gusto came on in the second half.



"That was a worrying performance, worrying. If that carries on, Alonso won't keep his job, I'm telling you that for nothing," Cundy added.

"You can't do what you did against Sunderland (1-0 loss), you can't do what you did against Leeds today and lose those two games."



"We were disgusting today, absolutely disgusting," Cundy continued. "I'm still trying to find the words... as every minute ticked by, we got worse, and Leeds got better."

Chelsea have dropped to eighth in the Premier League after losing for the fifth time this season, and Cundy thinks the next few months look bleak.

"It's almost disbelief at how bad we were, seriously, I'm not even joking. I'm worried... I'm worried about how this season is going to go," he said.

3 Cundy looked a broken man on the GameDay Phone-In and raised his concerns over how Chelsea will fare this season Credit: talkSPORT



3 He also warned Alonso that he could face the sack if their dismal run of form continues across the next few weeks Credit: Getty

"Genuinely now, I'm worried... I am worried about what this season looks like for us.

"I'm being completely honest here, I don't know whether we're going to finish... we look like bottom half fodder, easily bottom half fodder."

Later in the show, Cundy stated that Chelsea would have lost against Championship opposition with a similar performance.



"I actually think Lincoln could've beaten us today… anyone could've beaten us, we were that bad," Cundy said.

"I'm really struggling to work out how we could've been that bad."

Leeds also poked fun at Cundy on social media by giving him a taste of his own medicine with his famous 'Has anyone seen?' joke.

Alonso: Chelsea in a 'fragile moment'

Speaking to talkSPORT afterwards, Alonso detailed how Chelsea, who saw Moises Caicedo go off injured in the first half, struggle to bounce back from adversity.

"It was a tough one, a tough game, tough result to deal with," Alonso said. "My feeling is that we are in a fragile moment, when we get a setback, we are not able to recover quick enough to this competitive level required against a team as Leeds.



"The first half an hour we were good, we conceded the 1-1, and after that, the substitution, we lost total momentum. Leeds started believing more than us and we were not able to turn it our way."

Alonso added: "Leeds have their qualities and they do good. There are more reasons than just the physicality of the duels.

"I think that we could have done better, even that we lost a little bit of confidence to do the right things, how to keep the ball, how to be able to go through this first pressure of Leeds.

"The first half an hour we were able to play much more on the half, but the rest of the game we didn't progress that well."

Sports.title: Why Tom Brady, LeBron James, Will Smith and Didier Drogba are all buying into motorsport's new James Bond-like craze: Inside the glitzy world of powerboat racing's E1 Series
Sports.content:
Why Tom Brady, LeBron James, Will Smith and Didier Drogba are all buying into motorsport's new James Bond-like craze: Inside the glitzy world of powerboat racing's E1 Series

Floating in the media boat on the glorious, crisp blue waters of Biscayne Bay, a sunshine-filled backdrop befitting an episode of Miami Vice, we set up shop in anticipation of the E1 Series Championship finale.

Little did we know that the next boat around the course would not be one of the ten racebirds lined up on the water, ready to do battle, but rather the 500-horsepower, zero-emission Arc Sport passenger speedboat that was hosting much of the world’s media.

The captain whacked on AC/DC’s Shoot to Thrill, put his metaphorical foot on the pedal, and showed us the true meaning of powerboat racing. This was the moment I realised that E1 was the next big thing in motorsport.

We are on the waterfront of ‘The Magic City’ for the race boat championship’s first-ever double-header, and the final stop of the third season of this electrifying, glamorous, up-and-coming sport.

The E1 World Championship is the very first of its kind, the only all-electric powerboat competition on the planet. It’s led by a swathe of celebrities, some of the biggest names not only in sport, but in the film and music industries too.

Seven-time Super Bowl-winning quarterback Tom Brady, NBA legend LeBron James, Oscar-winning actor Will Smith, and football stars Thibaut Courtois and Didier Drogba are just a handful of the superstars who own teams in what has been dubbed the ‘Formula One of the water’.

The eco-friendly powerboat racing E1 Series wrapped up its third season in Miami last week

NFL legend Tom Brady is one of 10 celebrity team owners, which include the likes of Lebron James and Will Smith

International DJ Steve Aoki, who is best known for a remix of Kid Cudi's ‘Pursuit of Happiness’ – used in the chaotic teen-party comedy Project X – and for throwing cakes in the faces of his fans, is also one of the owners, and was repping the cohort in his hometown of Miami alongside Brady and Latin pop icon Marc Anthony.

The musical duo within the trio could be seen 'digging' at each other on occasion in the affluent VIP Ocean Club, an area filled with distinguished and well-dressed guests, which has become common practice among A-list stars behind the teams.

‘I have never seen another sport [that] was led by prominent figures in culture,’ Aoki tells Daily Mail Sport during a media roundtable. 'I’m sure it’s happened before, but it’s never crossed my radar.

‘They are doing it successfully and are really thinking about the global reach; we are getting different people from different parts of the world that have an impact on culture, that have an impact on visibility.

‘It’s a fun, healthy competition and it drives a lot of different kinds of attention. As it gets bigger, people will take notes and do the same thing. The idea was incredible, but how do you get it on its legs? By doing what it's doing, it’s growing; it's spreading. I hear conversations about E1 far more than a few years ago.’

In what is yet another product of Alejandro Agag’s boundless imagination, following on from Formula E and Extreme E, ten teams – nine of which are owned by celebrity owners such as Aoki – fiercely compete over seven rounds in waters all across the world, in a bid to become ‘Champions of the Water’.

Brady's team, piloted by Emma Kimilainen and Sam Coleman won a third E1 Series title on the spin in the Magic City

Each team has both a male and female pilot who will alternate across qualifying, group stage races and finals. All 20 racers drive a stock 200 hp electric propulsion boat, which is called a racebird but looks more like a blend between an F1 car, a fighter jet in Star Wars and the speedboat Pierce Brosnan’s James Bond rips through the Thames in the opening scene of The World Is Not Enough.

Both the men and women race against each other; it is not split by gender, in these 7.5m-long magnificent machines that can ramp up to 60mph, otherwise known as 50 knots, and glide slightly above the water with an elegance not seen in many other motorsports.

Now, the top speed may not seem crazy quick, but as the pilots made clear, and as was evident during our chaotic media lap, racing on water feels doubly quick to the road. Oh, and of course, it isn’t exactly flat or solid either. When the boats aren’t gliding, they are crashing through the chop.

Team Brady were back-to-back champions coming into the finale in Miami, and were looking to add their third crown on the bounce as they build the sport’s first dynasty. And come the end of the gruelling but enthralling successive race days, they achieved just that.

Some rip-roaring racing from Finnish driver Emma Kimilainen, whose fame in her homeland led to appearances on both Dancing with the Stars and The Masked Singer, sealed the deal in the final round. Kimilainen and fellow pilot Sam Coleman had achieved something their big boss Brady never managed during his trophy-laden career in the NFL: a three-peat.

On what sets them apart from the rest, Kimilainen tells Daily Mail Sport: ‘Our team works together and our mindset. Also, Tom is absolutely insanely involved; he is supporting us, he is pushing us.

Both male and female pilots across 10 teams race a stock 200 hp electric propulsion boat called a racebird that floats above the water at up to 60mph

The finale took place the crisp waters of Biscayne Bay, a backdrop befitting of a James Bond film

International DJ Steve Aoki owns his own team and told Daily Mail Sport that the celebirties have healthy competition at the races

‘He loves data, strategy; he loves everything about sports. He wants us to find our best performance everywhere we can. We are so grateful for Tom.’

Brady’s ability to win has followed him to almost every sports team he has been a part of during his career – which Chelsea fans will be hopeful it continues in the Premier League following his alleged minor stake purchase in the club – and it’s clear his mentality has had a monumental effect on the pilots.

‘Something that Tom said last week is that you always go to work on a Monday,’ Coleman tells Daily Mail Sport. ‘Win on a Sunday, go to work on a Monday. Lose on a Sunday, go to work on a Monday. It’s that mentality that really helps us.

‘He has had his fair share of losses and he says that failure is something to learn from; he’s had his fair share of failures and adversity. It’s how he responded and what he did next, and that’s something that runs through the team.

‘Three on the bounce is really challenging but we only have Tom’s seven Super Bowl titles to aspire to. We have a bit more work to do to build that dynasty.’

E1 Series is clearly still in its infancy. While it’s growing by the year, and many a celebrity is taking a keen interest – as was shown by the attendance of two-time Champions League winning PSG star Achraf Hakimi at the Jeddah, Saudi Arabia round earlier this year – they are still yet to truly crack the casual motorsport fanbase.

The VIP Ocean Club where fans watch the action in luxury is a staple of the E1 experience

The championship’s next aim is to start building areas for casual fans that don’t feel the need to dress like they are attending one of Jay Gatsby’s West Egg soirees, sipping champagne – however delightful that sounds, and is.

‘What I say is watch this space,' E1 Series CEO Jamie Copas tells Daily Mail Sport during a roundtable. ‘We have these incredible celebrities, but we also need to realise just how busy they are.’

He adds: ‘The development moving forward is about fan zones because we have Ocean Club. Ocean Club is fantastic and it's a great place for people to come experience the racing, but also experience the lifestyle element of E1 Series.

‘But what's really important for us for the future is how do we build out the fan zones? And the reality of that is that where we race, we need to make sure there's enough space for it.

‘The more people that come and see the races, the more they're going to interact with the stories that we're telling and the more we can talk about sustainability, the more we can talk about men and women racing against each other.’

The eco-friendly sport may already be worldwide, with races across Europe, North America and Africa, but it’s still early on in its inception and is riding the start of a swell that could see it surf to the top of its realm.

Sports.title: Cool Palmer has turned into Complaining Cole... his sulking as his club lurches into crisis doesn't say a lot for Chelsea's cultural reset, writes KIERAN GILL
Sports.content:
Cool Palmer has turned into Complaining Cole... his sulking as his club lurches into crisis doesn't say a lot for Chelsea's cultural reset, writes KIERAN GILL

We do not know why Cole Palmer headed for the tunnel in a huff after full-time while others in the same Chelsea side paraded the pitch to thank those supporters who had stayed to the end.

Perhaps he was frustrated with himself after a performance in which he did not score, assist, or even test James Trafford in Leeds United’s goal. Maybe he did not fancy thanking those who had been booing as Chelsea trailed 4-1. It is possible he simply does not like losing.

Most superstars can feel the same, and they can show their stroppy side when the game is not going their way.

An extreme example is Bruno Fernandes. Manchester United fans have long accepted his reputation as the Premier League’s temperamental nonpareil because of the numbers he can produce with the whingeing, albeit not so much this season during their downturn.

Such names can get away with petulance when their performances are proper, though Palmer has no such justification currently. The 24-year-old Englishman, unfortunately for Chelsea, put up another anonymous 90 minutes.

We could see he was frustrated even while on the pitch towards the end, with the way he was performatively kicking passes backwards as if to tell everyone else he had no other option. We have seen that before when Chelsea are losing, and it can be somewhat unhelpful when the pressure is being piled on the manager. It indicates the tactical set-up is not to his liking.

Cole Palmer and Joao Pedro were involved in a frosty exchange following Chelsea's 4-1 home defeat by Leeds. Source: Instagram/farihaxchels

As the biggest name within this Chelsea team and a player whose profile transcends his team-mates’, like it or not, he is the totem when it is all going wrong.

We wax lyrical when he is at his brilliant best. It can be as if there has been an explosion at a praise factory when he is dropping that shoulder to down a helpless defender. We know how terrifically talented he is. He is still compared to that 2023-24 season when his statistics were, in a wonderful way, stupid.

But when he is not performing, so too does he need to take the medicine of disapproval, which came in the form of a chorus of boos aimed at all those in Chelsea shirts at Stamford Bridge.

Leeds had not won at this ground since 1999. They corrected history, then Complaining Cole showed up at full-time.

His reaction did not speak to the cultural reset which Chelsea hoped they had orchestrated in the summer when they finally signed some experience for the changing room, bringing in Danny Welbeck, the 35-year-old whom Palmer has nominated as their new ‘Unc’ after Tosin Adarabioyo’s departure, and Jordan Henderson, 36.

Cole Palmer

It was a poor show from someone who, in his fourth season at a club that gave him his chance when spending £42.5million to sign him from Manchester City in 2023, should be seen as a leader by now.

Palmer is, probably, still undroppable. Alonso would create an almighty problem for himself if he suddenly relegated his No10 to the substitutes’ bench when playing Nottingham Forest next week. But he is in danger of such conversations cropping up at a time when he should want to be impressing enough to get back into Thomas Tuchel’s England squad at the next opportunity.

We are told both Palmer and Levi Colwill are desperate to represent their country again, but neither are performing to that standard of late. Colwill is a defender devoid of confidence, questioning himself and making mistakes. There was one moment during this demoralising defeat by Leeds when he booted a long ball straight out of play and reprimanded himself for it.

Colwill is perfectly capable of playing a good game. You do not have multiple clubs including Bayern Munich making enquiries with Chelsea without being considered elite. He is in a bad spell, and can come back from it, just like Palmer.

Sack Alonso? Patience is the name of the game

Inevitably, the response of some on social media was to say that Alonso’s time should be up.

For clarity, he is not under threat of suddenly being sacked by those at the top of Chelsea. He is 11 Premier League games into his career, and, clearly, deserves time.

The tactics are on him, absolutely. But he is also dealing with a few issues outside of his control, such as holes in his squad and injuries inflicted, like his highly-influential vice captain Moises Caicedo having to be substituted after 22 minutes in this match.

Xabi Alonso has made errors but was rightly considered a huge coup when Chelsea landed him

When appointed head coach of Bayer Leverkusen in October 2022, they went through patches in the Bundesliga. First, they beat Schalke 4-0, which was good. Then they failed to win any of their next three fixtures, which was bad.

Then they won five in a row – happy days. Then they won only one of their following five – bad days. Then they won five in a row again – perfect. Then they won only one of their next seven – pitiful.

But the following season, Leverkusen won the Bundesliga without losing a single game. Alonso was considered an almighty coup when secured in the summer. A little patience is deserved from my perspective, even if Chelsea are currently in a dismal spell.

It's not worth it for Gusto

It is hard not to think Malo Gusto’s time at Chelsea is almost at an end.

He was priced out of a move in the summer when the club asked for £75million, with Liverpool, Manchester City and others across Europe indicating their interest in that window.

Malo Gusto cut a lonely figure after being beaten for Leeds's fourth goal

But the 23-year-old Frenchman has shown little worth as the season has progressed.

Gusto started in five of Alonso’s first six games in all competitions at the beginning of the campaign.

Since then, he has been handed one start in eight, and that was in the Carabao Cup at Liverpool. Coming on as a substitute in this loss to Leeds, he tried and failed to play Brenden Aaronson offside and was then beaten by his man as the visitors made it 4-1.

We should expect to hear more on Gusto’s situation as January approaches.

Sports.title: Why Liverpool have a point to prove against Man United: Andoni Iraola's side must end rotten run against 'Big Six' rivals - and Florian Wirtz and Alexander Isak have to finally step up when it matters
Sports.content:
Why Liverpool have a point to prove against Man United: Andoni Iraola's side must end rotten run against 'Big Six' rivals - and Florian Wirtz and Alexander Isak have to finally step up when it matters

Given the carousel of chaos and never-ending crises at Old Trafford, it is easy to forget there are football storylines away from the headline-generating machine of Manchester United and Mauricio Pochettino.

Lo and behold, there is – and Liverpool also enter Sunday’s clash against the old enemy with a point to prove.

One problem for Andoni Iraola is his side's frailties in the bigger games, which comes into focus this weekend with United in town – despite the desire to make an easy joke about how this is a clash against relegation fodder.

Since thrashing United 7-0 in 2023, Liverpool have beaten their friends in Manchester just once in seven meetings, including two draws and a defeat at Anfield.

To use a cliche, form seems to go out of the window for this fixture. In the last two Anfield meetings, Liverpool have been first and second in the table, United 14th and then tenth. This weekend, it is fourth against 18th, though Pochettino’s side could be bottom by kick-off.

Liverpool’s struggles in bigger games stretch further. Against the so-called 'Big Six’, the Reds have won just two of 12 games since winning the Premier League title. In a ‘mini league’ of those six sides, Liverpool are bottom in the aforementioned period.

Andoni Iraola's Liverpool side must prove on Sunday they can deliver in the biggest matches

Manchester United did the double over Liverpool in the Premier League last season

United did the double over Liverpool last season, Manchester City have beaten them four times in little over 12 months, Arsenal won on Merseyside a month ago.

So why has this team gone from looking formidable 18 months ago to rather flappable whenever the historic big boys are in town? Casual neutrals who only tune in for the showpiece Sunday 4.30pm may joke that they have not seen Liverpool play well for a good year.

A lot of the answer to that question comes back to Arne Slot and the issues we documented every week last season, when his side were dull and boring to watch, naked in defence and would capitulate in an instant.

Maybe players like Isak, Florian Wirtz and Bradley Barcola thrive more in intricate spaces rather than the gaping gaps left behind by the attack-minded bigger teams.

Another reason could be the simple fact that these sides are more likely to expose Liverpool’s vulnerabilities, such as the lack of a true defensive midfielder, the poor full backs or the frailties at defending set-pieces.

Anfield has lost its fear factor somewhat, too. Liverpool are top of the Premier League away table with 13 points from 15, but 18th in the home table with just one win in five games.

City had not won in front of a crowd there since 2003, now they have done it two seasons running. Arsenal had not triumphed at the stadium for 14 years until last month.

Iraola is aware of all this and said on Friday: ‘United finished third in the table last season. You are looking at a squad with exactly the same players. They had very, very good results, especially in the second half of the season.

Liverpool bemoaned Ryan Gravenberch’s red card in their home defeat to Manchester City

The Reds spurned a number of chances when they were beaten 1-0 by Arsenal last month

‘Now we have just started, this is just 10 games. So, for sure, they will be a lot higher in the table (soon). We have to rate them like this and the truth is the reference we have is that they finished third.

‘We have to look at ourselves because we need the points. We need to improve our home form. It is also a big game in terms of relevance. It’s Liverpool v Manchester United, so we want to play well and we want to win.’

Asked if he understands the importance of the fixture to fans, Iraola – who spent the weekend off taking in grassroots football and netball games following his kids – said: ‘I am very aware! This is the biggest one in English football. In this country, this is the one.’

In Iraola’s first two bigger games, a theme threatened to emerge. Against Manchester City, Liverpool were well in the contest until Ryan Gravenberch’s red card but were toothless when it came to putting their chances away, lacking bite in attack.

The game was there to be won at 0-0, with the Anfield crowd roaring, but the Reds did not have the killer instinct to do so.

Against Arsenal, there were plenty of chances to equalise after the Gunners’ early goal but, again, goalkeeper David Raya could have put his feet up and had a cigar. A lot of territory but nothing to make the defence seriously sweat.

In both cases, Liverpool were on the receiving end of refereeing howlers. Gravenberch’s red was not a red – the first yellow should never be a booking – and Alexander Isak had a stonewall penalty turned down. ProRef has admitted errors.

To take a cynical view, though: in the title-winning campaign, we were rarely sat talking about referees or moaning about narrow misses or unfair results. Liverpool found ways to win and had no excuses.

Liverpool need Florian Wirtz and Alexander Isak to step up against the league's big boys

And that brings us nicely on to Sunday. It feels like the script has been written for weeks.

Indeed, after United lost 3-0 to Bournemouth and the score was read out to huge cheers at Anfield, Daily Mail Sport wrote: ‘Everyone is looking forward to United sacking Michael Carrick and then rocking up at Anfield to win 1-0 with their new manager in a few weeks.’

It always seems to happen and it feels like United get results against rivals Liverpool and City even when they have felt close to their lowest ebb.

But Liverpool and Iraola must not allow that to happen. There can be no excuses of ‘new manager bounce’, refereeing calls or fine margins come Sunday tea time.

Isak and Wirtz simply must step up. It feels harsh that the pair, Wirtz especially, are always in the spotlight but the £125million and £116million signings have flattered to deceive against the big boys.

Both have been spectacular at times this term but need to show up when it really matters, while £123million addition Barcola is still waiting for his first Premier League goal.

Iraola has history with United. As a player, his Athletic Club side beat Sir Alex Ferguson’s great side 5-3 over two legs in Europe.

‘I said at the time, it was one of the best wins of my career,’ he said. 'United, I remember, were champions of the Premier League, got to the Champions League final and lost to Barcelona the year before. We honestly played much better than them.’

Iraola has remained unbeaten against United into his managerial career, winning two and drawing four of his six meetings with them.

Overall, the former Bournemouth boss has played 38 games against ‘Big Six’ teams in the league: winning ten, drawing ten, losing 18.

But a win is all that matters on Sunday and it is a chance for Liverpool to set the tempo ahead of a busy festive schedule. After already taking on the current top three, Iraola now contests two rivalries with a trip across the city to Everton next week.

Six of nine pre-Christmas games are at Anfield so there is a real chance to build a head of steam in the league, qualify for the next stage of Europe and get to the Carabao Cup semi-final.

Iraola would welcome those festive gifts but, for Liverpool fans, nothing will be sweeter than giving their old foes a good old walloping on Sunday.

Sports.title: Revealed: Just two Man United stars are selected in combined XI with Liverpool by stats boffins as Andoni Iraola's defence dominates... but is the Liverpool boss missing a hidden gem?
Sports.content:
Revealed: Just two Man United stars are selected in combined XI with Liverpool by stats boffins as Andoni Iraola's defence dominates... but is the Liverpool boss missing a hidden gem?

All eyes will be on Manchester United's new head coach Mauricio Pochettino when they take on Liverpool at Anfield this afternoon.

Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola has freshened up the squad since joining in the summer, including the £123million purchase of Bradley Barcola from Paris Saint-Germain, while blending in young emerging talent. They have made a solid start across all four competitions, knocking Chelsea out of the League Cup on penalties, and they currently sit in fourth place in the Premier League.

United have had a dire start to the season, with only one win in 10 games leading to the axeing of head coach Michael Carrick. Will his replacement be able to save the season and galvanise a group of talented but dispirited players?

So, who from United’s struggling side have done enough to break into Sofascore's combined XI based on their performances throughout the 2026-27 season so far?

Manchester United's new head coach Mauricio Pochettino will face his first test against Liverpool on Sunday

United currently sit at 18th in the Premier League after a disappointing start to the season

Goalkeeper – Alisson Becker (Liverpool)

Between the sticks is Liverpool’s No 1, who since signing for a record fee in 2018, has established himself as one of the best shot-stoppers in the world.

Rated for his positioning, distribution and consistency, Alisson has an impressive record, especially in one-on-one situations.

The 34-year-old Brazilian goalkeeper has kept four clean sheets in 10 league appearances this season, averaging 2.5 saves per game. He has conceded 10 goals, including a brutal 3-0 loss to Manchester City at Anfield last month.

Alisson was poor in Liverpool's 3-2 defeat by Fenerbahce but responded with a fine display in the Reds' 3-1 win over Crystal Palace when back in league action days later.

Sofascore rating: 6.86

Right back – Ronald Araujo (Liverpool)

At right back is Liverpool’s Ronald Araujo, on loan from Barcelona this season, and there are already cries from Liverpool fans to sign him permanently.

The 27-year-old is a natural centre back, but he has done wonders to ease Liverpool’s problems in the right-back position. Jeremie Frimpong started the season in that position but the Liverpool backline were far too exposed. Araujo has helped Liverpool tighten up defensively.

The Uruguayan defender has featured in all of Liverpool’s league matches so far this season, with his defensive actions helping him contribute inside his own penalty box. He has averaged six clearances per game and has won 30 aerial duels so far this season, behind only Virgil van Dijk in the Liverpool squad.

Sofascore rating: 7.16

Ronald Araujo (right) has impressed this season for Liverpool, on loan from Barcelona

Centre back - Jeremy Jacquet (Liverpool)

Jeremy Jacquet is a young player to watch this season after joining Liverpool this summer.

The 21-year-old has a 95 per cent accurate pass rate, including long balls. He had a standout performance against Fulham early on in the season, winning five aerial duels, five recoveries and making a clearance off the line to keep his team in the game.

Despite playing in France's second division just two seasons ago, Jacquet has fitted seamlessly into Iraola's style of play at Liverpool and there are suggestions he is an upgrade on the man he replaced, fellow France international Ibrahima Konate.

Sofascore rating: 7.12

Centre back - Virgil van Dijk (Liverpool)

It is no surprise that Liverpool and Netherlands team captain Virgil van Dijk makes it into the XI.

Known for his strength, leadership, speed and aerial ability, he is the only defender to win the UEFA Men's Player of the Year Award, and finished runner-up for both the Ballon d'Or and Best FIFA Men's Player in 2019.

This season, he has shown his aerial ability with 3.8 duels won in the air (79 per cent) per game and 4.8 total duels won per game.

The team struggled against Manchester City, however. In the game at Anfield that ended their unbeaten run, Van Dijk only made four defensive contributions and picked up a yellow card for a frustrated foul on Rayan Cherki in added time.

Van Dijk's contract expires next summer, and the 35-year-old has a big decision to make.

Sofascore rating: 6.96

Left back – Kostas Tsimikas (Liverpool)

Is Iraola missing a hidden gem? Tsimikas is very much understudy to Milos Kerkez after acting as a reliable deputy to Andy Robertson.

But across all competitions this season he is statistically rated higher than the man who's ahead of him in the pecking order. Kerkez is rated at 6.67 – so it is tight.

Nicknamed 'Greek Scouser' by Reds fans, Tsimikas has only started five games but has produced three assists with 1.78 key passes and 1.56 accurate crosses.

Manchester United, on the other hand, have struggled to fill this position. They were unable to recruit in the summer, and now rely on Luke Shaw – who has been sidelined with a muscular issue since limping off during their 1-1 draw with Tottenham Hotspur in October – and are adapting with makeshift alternatives.

Sofascore rating: 6.71

Liverpool captain Virgil van Dijk celebrates with the fans after beating Crystal Palace

Centre midfield – Dominik Szoboszlai (Liverpool)

Versatile vice-captain Dominik Szoboszlai signed a new five-year contract with Liverpool this summer, and has proven his worth after scoring a stoppage-time penalty to level the score in their first game of the season against Newcastle.

With his ability to go forward and send crosses into the box and drop back to defend, Szoboszlai has been crucial for ball recovery, key passes and creating big chances.

It is a testament to his creative ability, including registering four big chances and one assist in the Premier League this season, that he makes the XI despite being sidelined with a hamstring injury for three games.

However, the Hungary midfielder has received backlash from fans for playing 90 minutes for his country in a 2-0 win against Georgia in the UEFA Nations League despite early withdrawal against Palace, and injury concerns remain ahead of this afternoon's clash.

Sofascore rating: 7.25

Centre midfield – Kobbie Mainoo (Manchester United)

Only one of two Manchester United players in this line-up, Kobbie Mainoo deserves recognition for his creative efforts this season, which have earned him the second highest Sofascore rating in this XI.

The 21-year-old England midfielder is known for his high pressing and long balls to create chances up the pitch. He has also registered four shots from outside the box.

He has been through some turbulent times at Old Trafford but Michael Carrick turned to him regularly this season.

A product of Manchester United's youth system and there is plenty of potential, especially with new manager Mauricio Pochettino’s penchant for developing young players. A chance to refresh and discover his best form.

Sofascore rating: 7.27

Kobbie Mainoo is one of only two United players to make the combined XI this weekend

Centre midfield – Alexis Mac Allister (Liverpool)

After his public revelation that he nearly left Liverpool, Alexis Mac Allister has been in form and pulling the strings in midfield and played an important role in Liverpool's season so far.

He headed in Liverpool’s second goal in their 3-1 away win over Crystal Palace and his passing and playmaking abilities have been key for their attacking chances this season.

He has scored five goals in 16 appearances across all competitions this season.

Sofascore rating: 7.36

Right forward – Bruno Fernandes (Manchester United)

The Portugal forward was named the PFA Players' Player of the Year last season, but he has divided United fans this season.

Inconsistent performances and publicly questioning Carrick's tactics after defeat in Como.

In the 1-1 draw against Spurs at Old Trafford, the skipper did not record his first successful pass until the 23rd minute, and he missed a big chance against Chelsea.

He has bagged four goals and two assists in the Premier League so far, but this is largely owing to his hat-trick against Ipswich, which earned him a perfect 10 Sofascore rating.

United fans will hope he can get back to his old ways under Pochettino.

Sofascore rating: 7.14

United fans will be desperate to see Bruno Fernandes find consistent performances again

Centre-forward – Alexander Isak (Liverpool)

Liverpool’s star striker, transferred for a British record-breaking fee of £125million last summer, has scored eight goals in 14 games this season, showing just how clinical he can be.

Reds fans are finally seeing the form that earned him the big-money move from Newcastle.

Isak edges out United's Bryan Mbeumo to lead the line in this team. He has a 55.6 per cent big chance conversion, scoring a goal every 113 minutes.

Sofascore rating: 7.14

Left forward – Cody Gakpo (Liverpool)

The Dutchman is establishing himself as Liverpool's go-to wideman among Iraola's plethora of options. His rapid pace and direct approach proves a massive threat.

This season his end product has improved, notching three goals and supplying six assists in 12 appearances across all competitions.

He is proving to be a reliable outlet while summer signings Bradley Barcola and Victor Munoz continue to settle into life in England.

His stunning long-range strike to equalise against Newcastle United shows just how clinical he can be in front of goal.

He averages 1.9 key passes and one big chance per game, which lands him a spot in this XI.

Sofascore rating: 7.15

Sports.title: The untold story of Mauricio Pochettino's move to Man United: When club decided he was the right man, the moment it became 'real', emotional talks with US staff and whirlwind first days in charge
Sports.content:
When Mauricio Pochettino boarded a flight from London to Atlanta a little over two weeks ago, there was little indication that by the time he landed back in the UK it would be as the new head coach of Manchester United.

The club were aware of the £7.5million buyout clause in his contract with the US national team as they began to consider potential replacements for Michael Carrick, but it hadn’t gone any further than that.

However, United’s 3-0 defeat to Bournemouth on October 25 left Carrick’s job hanging by a thread. He was given a two-week stay of execution that also allowed United time to step up their search for a suitable replacement.

At a meeting of the club’s executive committee on November 5 – after United had lost to Chelsea and staged a chaotic Champions League win against Roma – it was decided that Pochettino would be the No.1 choice if Carrick was sacked.

By the time the Argentine caught that flight to Atlanta 24 hours later to take charge of the USA's two-legged CONCACAF Nations League quarter-final against Haiti, United were preparing to make their move.

This is the story of the whirlwind two weeks that will end with Pochettino taking charge of his first game as United boss against Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday following the dramatic events on both sides of the Atlantic.

Sunday November 8

Patrick Dorgu’s injury-time header rescued United from another defeat as they snatched a 4-4 draw against Aston Villa at Old Trafford, but it wasn’t enough to save Carrick. His fate was effectively sealed and the first contact was made with Pochettino’s camp.

There is a five-hour time difference between Manchester and Georgia, so it was late afternoon when Pochettino first learned of United’s interest at the Trilith Guesthouse – close to the US national team’s training base in Fayetteville south-west of Atlanta – as the players began to report there for duty.

Michael Carrick's fate was effectively sealed and the first contact was made with Pochettino’s camp after the 4-4 draw with Aston Villa at Old Trafford

Monday November 9

As speculation raged over Carrick’s future, the odds on Pochettino replacing him at Old Trafford were slashed after some big money was placed on the 54-year-old overnight.

Preliminary talks continued with his representatives who made the US Soccer Federation aware of the situation. Pochettino discussed it over dinner at the team hotel with chief executive JT Batson and chief operating officer Dan Helfrich who knew it was pointless trying to change his mind.

Tuesday November 10

‘That was the big day,’ says a source close to Pochettino, who took US team training in Fayetteville. ‘It became real and the optimism grew.’

As talks accelerated between United and their prospective new head coach, Carrick returned to Carrington to work with the United players not on international duty while chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox flew to Monaco to meet minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe and rubber-stamp the change.

Wednesday November 11

United reached verbal agreement with Pochettino over a two-and-a-half-year deal, and agreed to pay US Soccer around £10million to buy the 54-year-old and his staff – No 2 Jesus Perez, first-team coach Miguel D’Agostino, goalkeeper coach Toni Jimenez, fitness coach Sebastiano Pochettino (Mauricio’s son), strength and conditioning coach Silvia Tuya and analyst Alec Scott – out of their contracts.

There was never any question of him leaving before the two Haiti ties, even though it left little time before his first game against Liverpool. Pochettino is said to have been respectful of the USA’s position and felt an obligation to see the job through.

As a compromise, it was agreed that Perez, Jimenez and Pochettino Jnr would be allowed to leave for Manchester after the first leg regardless of the result.

Media in the US were informed that access to the players had been cancelled out of respect for Veterans Day. It also meant that they don’t have to answer questions about Pochettino’s future.

Thursday November 12

Carrick returned to Carrington at 7.50am for the last time as United head coach and was sacked in a meeting with Berrada and Wilcox.

By the time Pochettino woke up in Fayetteville, United officially had a managerial vacancy and he gathered the players together for a scheduled team briefing at 10am.

Pochettino went through the usual pre-match preparation, and then invited staff into the room for the second half of the meeting.

There was some emotion but no surprise when he informed them of his decision to take the United job. ‘As you’d expect, he spoke from the heart,’ says a source. ‘He loved being here but United was a dream opportunity. It was too hard to say no, but hard to say goodbye.’

Friday November 13

United officially announced Pochettino’s appointment and confirmed that he would stay in charge for the USA’s two games against Haiti before starting work the following Wednesday.

Pochettino conducted his pre-match press conference in Fayetteville, flanked by CEO chief JT Batson and president Cindy Parlow Cone, and broke down in tears as he thanked them for their support over the last 26 months.

Otherwise, the preparation is said to have gone according to plan as the US squad flew to Miami.

The Argentine broke down in tears as he thanked the USA for their support over the last 26 months

Saturday November 14

The US smashed Haiti 6-0 to all but guarantee their place in the semi-finals. Even so the message from Pochettino to his players after the game was: ‘This tie isn’t over.’

The players learned for the first time that Perez, Jimenez and Pochettino Jnr were leaving camp, and they headed straight to Manchester.

Sunday November 15

Pochettino flew with the players from Miami to Cincinnati for the second leg at the TQL Stadium.

On a visit to the Kenwood Towne Centre shopping mall, a man whose profile had risen in the US during his two years in charge of the national team was approached by even more fans than normal.

When Pochettino appeared as a guest of honour at the NFL game between the Cincinnati Bengals and Pittsburgh Steelers at Paycor Stadium that night, a number of Bengals’ players and staff congratulated him on his new job claiming to be United fans.

Monday November 16

It emerged that United had provided a private jet for Pochettino and the remainder of his staff to fly straight from Cincinnati to Manchester through the night after the second leg.

In his pre-match press conference, he confirmed the departure of his three coaches over the weekend, and it was no surprise to learn that he was in constant contact over several days as he prepared to join them at Carrington.

Tuesday November 17

The US beat Haiti by two goals to complete an 8-0 aggregate win. Afterwards, they played Take Me Home, Country Roads by John Denver over the stadium PA, which has been a tradition since the US hosted the World Cup last summer but carried particular poignance given that it has also been adopted as an anthem at United.

Pochettino invited all the staff onto the pitch for a team photo as he led a chant of U-S-A, and there was a tearful send-off in the dressing-room as he was presented with a signed shirt and a special hand-painted bottle of Clase Azul tequila.

It’s a favourite tipple of Pochettino’s and staff also ordered food from Chick-fil-A, which Pochettino regrets won’t be available in Manchester.

He never had a permanent residence in America, so he left the stadium at 10.30pm with the same suitcase he had brought from London and headed for Cincinnati/Northern Kentucky International Airport for the flight to Manchester.

Wednesday November 18

Pochettino had a poor night’s sleep before landing shortly before noon aboard the grey Gulfstream G700 jet with D’Agostino, Scott and Tuya.
