He posted a picture from the skies above Manchester and was then driven to Carrington, changing into an official United tracksuit en route.

Pochettino was too late for training but met with some of the players and club executives before being given a tour of the training ground and conducting an interview with MUTV which wrapped up about 7pm. He stayed at the training ground long into the evening to catch up on his preparation for Liverpool.

The plane believed to be carrying Pochettino and his staff was hired by Manchester United

Thursday November 19

More players returned from international duty, but Pochettino’s first training session with them at Carrington was ambushed by a drone shooting video footage that was posted online. It was proof – if he needed it – that the former Tottenham and Chelsea boss will be under even greater scrutiny at United.

Responding, Pochettino said: 'We have young guys training with us. It’s not nice. It’s not good.

'What do they want to show? Yes, we were working on shape. We were very organised. What is the point of doing something that can be very dangerous?

'I don't want to be upset, but I think it's a process the club is caring a lot about.'

Pochettino’s first training session with them at Carrington was ambushed by a drone shooting video footage that was posted online

Friday November 20

Having only trained for a couple of hours on Thursday, Pochettino worked with the players between 11.30am and 2pm on Friday.

‘The training session was a little bit longer than it normally is in (match day) minus two,’ said Pochettino at his opening pre-match press conference, admitting that he had not even had a chance to shower beforehand.

Pochettino worked with his new players between 11.30am and 2pm on Friday

Saturday November 21

Pochettino took training for the third day running at Carrington on Saturday morning, before United travelled on the team bus to their hotel where they had dinner and a pre-match meeting last night.

On Sunday he faces a massive first game as United boss in front of the cameras at Anfield at the end of a dizzying fortnight.

Sports.title: 'I've got a bitterness towards English cricket and how I was spat out': Former Yorkshire coach ANDREW GALE on the county's racism 'witch hunt', Azeem Rafiq and his new life in Tasmania
Sports.content:
'I've got a bitterness towards English cricket and how I was spat out': Former Yorkshire coach ANDREW GALE on the county's racism 'witch hunt', Azeem Rafiq and his new life in Tasmania

A bright morning down by Hobart’s glimmering waterfront feels a world away from drizzly Dewsbury, but it is where Andrew Gale – once a proud Yorkshireman, now an honorary Tasmanian – calls home.

‘It’s funny how things work out, and everything sort of happens for a reason,’ he says, relief trumping regret. ‘But my three kids are very settled here. So is my wife. I’m forever grateful to Cricket Australia.’

Staff at the Mures cafe have barely opened up for the day, but the 42-year-old Gale is already deep into a story that might well have reached a darker conclusion. It is a remarkable journey, until now only partially told.

Yorkshire to his core, he captained his county to Championship titles in 2014 and 2015, before coaching them for five years until 2021. It was at this point that the wheels fell off.

The club suspended Gale that November for an 11-year-old tweet that included the word ‘yid’. He said he didn’t realise the term was offensive, and deleted the tweet as soon as he had. Worse was to come: a month later, he was among 16 Yorkshire employees sacked amid accusations of racial discrimination and abuse by Azeem Rafiq, whose 11 years at the club overlapped with Gale.

Gale was stunned to find himself among the accused, so when he heard the ECB were launching an investigation, he says he ‘welcomed it with open arms’.

Andrew Gale lifts the 2014 County Championship trophy, his first of back-to-back titles as captain of his beloved Yorkshire, with Azeem Rafiq and Alex Lees in the background

In 2021 while head coach, Gale was suspended for a historic tweet, and then was one of 16 staff sacked following Rafiq's allegations of racism at the club

‘I sent them all the stuff we’d gone through with Yorkshire,' he tells me over coffee, 'all the transcripts, hundreds and hundreds of pages. I was training as a joiner at the time, and I was digging a hole when the phone rang. I said, “If you tell me where and when, I’ll come at any time, any day, anywhere in the country, and I’ll tell you the story”.’

But no interview took place. The next thing he knew, he was being charged by the ECB in June 2022 for a breach of their anti-discrimination code, by which point he said he had ‘no faith’ in a ‘tainted process’, and declined to engage with it.

The following May, he was one of six former Yorkshire cricketers found guilty by the Cricket Discipline Commission, with Gale said to have called Rafiq ‘Rafa the Kaffir’ (a slur that is deemed hate speech in southern Africa) and a ‘P***’ – charges he denied. He was fined £7,500, and told the only route back into cricket was to undergo an education course at his own expense.

Rafiq said he felt ‘vindicated’ by the CDC’s verdict, and finally had ‘closure’.

In the intervening months, to less fanfare, Yorkshire admitted Gale’s sacking had been ‘procedurally unfair’, and agreed a financial settlement. He said at the time: ‘I will always be unhappy with how my career ended, but I refuse to have my life defined by unsubstantiated allegations by an embittered former colleague and by a YCCC/ECB witch hunt.’

Looking back now, he says: ‘I was caught up in something that was gathering momentum, and a lot of it was out of my control. There were things that should or shouldn’t have happened, and the people in power, I’m sure, carry some guilt over the way they were handled.

‘The advice was that it would cost £200,000 to fight it, and you’ve got a 20 per cent chance of winning – whether we’ve got a good story or not. That was a big risk with a young family. I just couldn’t afford to take it on.

‘I was very low, and wondering: “What’s the point?” I gave my heart and soul to Yorkshire. Anyone who’s been a head coach knows there’s no such thing as a day off. I probably made choices where I sacrificed my family for the club and the players.

‘When you go through that, and you think what was it all for, and you get spat out… it’s just how quickly everything happened.’

Rafiq said he felt ‘vindicated’ by the verdict, and finally had ‘closure’. In the intervening months, to less fanfare, Yorkshire admitted Gale’s sacking had been ‘procedurally unfair’

‘I was very low, and wondering: “What’s the point?” I gave my heart and soul to Yorkshire,' says Gale (left, with Michael Vaughan), having spent his entire career with the club

Rafiq (left) with Gale (right) and Jack Brooks during their Yorkshire days

Gale recalls a family trip to the Dominican Republic, during which he learned of his sacking. ‘At nights, I sat at the bar crying, but my kids remember that as their best holiday. I always look at that period as a parent and think: we actually did all right.

‘But I also thought: what am I going to do with the rest of my life? I don’t think I’ll ever get as low as that, but it has made me resilient and probably a bit soulless. I don’t ride the wave like I used to. If we lose, it’s a game of cricket. The sun will come up tomorrow and we crack on.’

The scandal had already cost Gale a coaching role with Hobart Hurricanes in Australia’s T20 Big Bash League. And so, unwanted by the only world he had ever known, he spent two years training and working as a joiner. ‘As a 40-year-old bloke turning up at people’s houses, they must have thought I’d just got out of prison on work experience,’ he chuckles.

But a job came up as Tasmania’s head of male performance pathway. Gale’s wife, Kate, told him: ‘You have to go for this. I can see it in your eyes. There’s something missing from your life. I don’t think you’re ever going to be happy unless you get back into cricket.’

Gale was interviewed in 2023, Cricket Australia’s integrity unit did their due diligence, and he turned up for work in September. ‘When I got back throwing balls and working in cricket, it just felt like I’d arrived back home,’ he says.

Kate and their children – Ada, Beatrice and Jack, then 11, eight and seven – joined him three months later to embark on a new life, more than 10,000 miles away on the other side of the world, and they have approached it with gusto. Kate works for Leap Health, which runs physio practices around Tasmania, and Jack now supports Australia, turning up for Wednesday’s third ODI at Bellerive Oval in the gold shirt of his adopted country.

‘When he asked for an Australia shirt for Christmas, I thought this is a bit weird,’ says Gale, his own vowels still very much northern England. ‘But we’ve got a fantastic life here. It’s almost like the childhood we had. It’s very safe. The kids ride bikes to school, and they’ve got a bit more freedom. It’s slow-paced in Hobart, very stress-free.

‘There aren’t many English coaches working in Australian cricket, so I’ve certainly had to prove myself. I think I’m a more rounded coach. I was probably too attached to Yorkshire.

'There was a period where I couldn’t even look at Yorkshire’s scores. But I don’t think I ever wanted them to do badly, and I still watch out for the players'

‘I’ve probably got a bitterness towards English cricket for what happened,' says Gale

‘I can’t speak more highly of Cricket Tasmania, and what they’ve done for me and the family. Coming out the other side of all that, you think, "Yeah, I can handle anything life throws at me now". It showed what resilience I had. I probably always had that as a player, and then it shone through in my personal life.

‘I’ve probably got a bitterness towards English cricket for what happened, and there was a period where I couldn’t even look at Yorkshire’s scores. But I don’t think I ever wanted them to do badly, and I still watch out for the players. I still watch for Harry (Brook)’s results, and text him when he’s done well. That gives me a lot of pride, because we gave that young kid his debut at 16, saying he’s going to be the next big thing, and he has gone on to achieve that.’

Gale’s stock here is high enough to have been involved in the Australia A set-up, and he was among the backroom staff when a Cricket Australia XI hosted England Lions at Lilac Hill, near Perth, a year ago. So who will he be cheering for in next summer’s Ashes?

He laughs. ‘I don’t know. I’m probably going to cheer for the Yorkshire boys. I just enjoy watching it now, I think because I’m not that close to it.’ Does he have anything to say to Rafiq? ‘No, nothing. I’ve not seen or heard from the bloke since the day he walked out of Yorkshire.’

Cricket has pushed Gale away and welcomed him back, via a route so tortured and circuitous it’s almost a surprise he still cares. But Tasmania took a chance on him, and he has repaid the faith. ‘It’s strange that something terrible had to happen,’ he says. ‘But it’s brought the best out of me.’

Sports.title: DAN BIGGAR: Here's how Ben Earl delivered one of the best displays I've ever seen from an England forward... and why mastering the art of deception could be crucial in the nation's bid for World Cup glory
Sports.content:
DAN BIGGAR: Here's how Ben Earl delivered one of the best displays I've ever seen from an England forward... and why mastering the art of deception could be crucial in the nation's bid for World Cup glory

I never thought I’d say this as a passionate Welshman, but I’m so, so pleased for England. Some might think that is a tongue-in-cheek comment. It genuinely isn’t.

There is, admittedly, a personal element to it. I played with a lot of England’s players at Northampton – guys like George Furbank and Tommy Freeman. They’re friends of mine. I know how good they are.

That’s why when I’ve seen England struggle, it’s been a bit confusing. They’re a team packed with talent. They showed that against New Zealand. But it wasn’t a one-off performance.

Across the autumn so far, England have showed that at their best, they can be a hugely powerful side. They are still a team that has strides to make up on South Africa and France, but on the evidence of the November Tests we've seen to date, they are a team capable of being there or thereabouts at next year’s World Cup – especially given their favourable draw.

Ahead of their first game with Australia, a newspaper report questioned the belief the players have in Borthwick and intimated that the environment was poor. I’ve been pretty clear already that the article and its timing unimpressed me.

But, whatever you think of it, England’s response has been mightily impressive. They have shown through the strength of their performances that they are together as a group.

To me, they are clearly a team who believe in their direction of travel under Borthwick. England are ticking a lot of boxes this month. I played against many England teams who had forward power. Their current team has that too and plenty of it.

George Furbank is a friend from my Northampton days and I'm so pleased for him and England

But, crucially, they are now developing into a side which can move the ball to the wide channels. They can bludgeon down the front door with a sledgehammer but wield the scalpel with dexterity too.

That’s a pretty good combination. New Zealand were poor. I knew within the first five minutes England weren’t going to lose. They started well, dominating possession and territory, and it was almost instantly clear to me the All Blacks still looked shell-shocked from their first defeat by Wales in 73 years.

Their big-name players were back for England, but the collective performance was poor. New Zealand made lots of errors.

But this result was not about the paucity of the All Blacks. It was about English excellence. I thought Freeman’s late withdrawal was going to be a big blow. But Cadan Murley was brilliant in his place. Lewis Moody helping lead England’s haka response was a really, really powerful moment.

It set the tone for a brilliant team performance, in a very similar, though still slightly different way to Wales had done in Cardiff the week before. England copped a lot of criticism after their first defeat by Italy and worst ever Six Nations finish.

That was entirely justified because no English team should ever win just one game in any Championship. The response has been impressive. England have an outstanding pack. Ben Earl and Ollie Chessum were world class against the All Blacks. England’s line-out was superb.

Cadan Murley excelled after stepping in for Tommy Freeman, who pulled out with a thigh issue

Former captain Lewis Moody leading England's response to the haka, having been diagnosed with MND last year, was a powerful moment at Twickenham

Their forwards carried hard, putting the team on the front foot. The way Borthwick and his coaches have evolved England’s attack deserves praise too. Against New Zealand, I thought they did two things really well.

The first was that they had a lot of hidden runners as carrying options off Fin Smith as No10, either from the short side or behind the first receiver.

That’s the sort of deception England have needed in their game for a long time, but that hasn’t always been there. Smith’s 10-12 partnership with Seb Atkinson is really developing nicely and you can add in the classy Henry Slade at No13 to that too.

The second aspect of the England performance that stood out for me was that they did not overplay in the middle of the pitch.

New Zealand have so many jackal threats that if a team goes through multiple phases against them, they risk a turnover or conceding a penalty at the breakdown. England played sensibly, going through phases in the opposition 22 but not looking to do that too much in areas that could cost them.

By playing for one or two phases and then going to width or kicking, they negated New Zealand’s breakdown threat. The fact England were also so physically dominant and had the upper hand on possession and territory was also significant. At No8, Earl was ridiculously good.

Ben Earl bulldozed through for the third try before half-time in a superb performance

It was one of the best performances from an England forward I have ever seen. Chessum was outstanding too on the flank.

With Chessum, who is normally a lock, playing at No6, England have the ability to destroy opposition at line-outs with Maro Itoje and either Alex Coles or George Martin alongside him in the second row.

That’s exactly what happened against New Zealand. You can give England no greater praise other than to say they made the All Blacks look pretty average.

That’s now back-to-back defeats for Dave Rennie’s side against Wales and England which is something you don’t often say – probably only every 70-odd years!

For Rennie and his players, it’s back to the drawing board. Don't write them off. The All Blacks will certainly still be World Cup contenders this time next year. But as they continue on an upward curve, so too can England.

Sports.title: Frustrated Cole Palmer shares frosty exchange with Joao Pedro after upsetting Chelsea staff member before walking off down the tunnel after 4-1 drubbing by Leeds
Sports.content:
Cole Palmer was involved in a frustrated exchange with team-mate Joao Pedro after Chelsea crashed to a 4-1 home defeat against Leeds.

The Blues were beaten by Leeds at Stamford Bridge for the first time since 1999, despite having taken the lead through Emmanuel Emegha's first goal for the club.

Noah Okafor scored twice for Leeds either side of a Dominic Calvert-Lewin penalty, with Brenden Aaronson adding a fourth in stoppage time.

Palmer, who opted against going around the pitch applauding the remaining fans at full-time, was captured approaching Joao Pedro following the match.

The Chelsea star could be seen covering his mouth while speaking to his team-mate, who had been left to watch from the sidelines as he continues his recovery from injury.

Joao Pedro put his hand on Palmer's shoulder as he responded to his team-mate, with the Brazilian then shrugging his shoulders as a frustrated Palmer went to walk down the tunnel.

Cole Palmer and Joao Pedro were involved in a frosty exchange following Chelsea's 4-1 home defeat by Leeds. Source: Instagram/farihaxchels

Joao Pedro shrugged his shoulders as a frustrated Palmer headed down the tunnel after their exchange. Source: Instagram/farihaxchels

Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso was asked post-match about the exchange, amid a suggestion Joao Pedro and Willie Isa, Chelsea's player support and development officer, had attempted to persuade Palmer to applaud the fans.

‘No, we were disappointed, the fans were disappointed because the expectations from them are high,' Alonso responded.

'We feel sorry for them and we need to go through together and to find solutions to that and now, as I said, for sure it’s not the easiest moment.

‘It’s a fragile moment but we need to work together and stick together because there is still such a long way to go.'

Alonso's side have now lost three of their last four Premier League matches, having been beaten at home by rivals Tottenham and falling to defeat at Sunderland prior to the international break.

The Blues have now dropped to eighth in the table, with Alonso's side having won five, drawn one and lost five of their 11 matches to date.

Palmer had begun the season brightly under Alonso by scoring in their opening two fixtures but has only scored one league goal since, netting with a penalty in a 2-0 win over Man United.

Chelsea will look to bounce back when they face struggling Nottingham Forest and Crystal Palace in their next two matches, before blockbuster clashes with Liverpool and Man City.

Sports.title: Andoni Iraola has two players that can beat Man Utd and change the mood at Liverpool
Sports.content:
Fortress Anfield is in need of some renovation. And there's nothing quite like the visit of Manchester United to focus the collective minds of the Liverpool fanbase.

The Reds entertain their bitter North West rivals this afternoon aiming to land another blow on the suffering Old Trafford outfit, who go into the game in 19th place after only one win from 10 Premier League games.

But for former Liverpool midfielder Paul Ince, Andoni Iraola's embryonic side are yet to fully feel the benefit of the famed sense of togetherness from an Anfield crowd still disgruntled by last season's dreadful title defence that ultimately saw Arne Slot sacked.

"It is very strange," said Ince. "I still feel that it’s an intimidating place to go to. But it takes time.

‌

Ismaila Sarr opens up on failed Liverpool transfer and reveals fresh talks READ MORE :

Make sure you don't miss the best Liverpool coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

"Liverpool need to get a big win at Anfield to just get that intimidation back, to get that fear factor back. Whether that’s on Sunday, I don’t know. But that’s what they need.

"I love the Liverpool fans. I still live in the Wirral so that says a lot. But I think last year Liverpool fans got a bit despondent, got a bit impatient with their players. And they never do that. They never, ever do that.

"It’s a family club. And they look after their own. But last year, I sensed they weren’t really all together. So that needs to come back.

‌



"I think there’s a 'what’s going to happen today?' type of attitude. Liverpool fans are a bit apprehensive about what they’re going to get at home."

While there have been signs of Anfield stirring into life on Champions League and Carabao Cup nights this season, Ince believes the raft of players signed in the wake of the title triumph 18 months ago have yet experienced a Liverpool crowd at its most rousing.

View 4 Images Paul Ince knows plenty about the Liverpool and Man Utd rivalry

"But that comes with getting results, doesn’t it?" said Ince, speaking to our sister title the ECHO through free bets. "That comes with performing. And at the moment, they’re not doing that consistently.

‌



"I don’t think Liverpool have performed badly at any stage this season. But they are still a work in progress. They’ve got a lot of players to click. If you think about Alexander Isak, Bradley Barcola, Florian Wirtz, I think all these players can start clicking."

Ince spent six years at United before later in his career spending two seasons at Liverpool. And the now 59-year-old is in no doubt about which of the two venues he found the most difficult.

"When I played for United, going to Anfield was always intimidating," he said. "It was electric. The fans were right on top of you. The Kop’s in full voice. And the Kop’s the best place in football. When the Kop’s got all the flags flying, it’s the best place to be.

"So, when you’re playing for United and you’re going there, you knew it was going to be tough. As a Man United player, that was the most daunting place to go.

‌



"As a Liverpool player, going to Old Trafford wasn’t as daunting. And I found that pretty strange."

View 4 Images Iraola has enjoyed a steady start as Liverpool boss

So to Sunday's showdown, which will be United's first game since Mauricio Pochettino replaced the sacked Michael Carrick during the international break. Pochettino has won only three times in 19 previous games as a manager against Liverpool, and has a worse record against only Real Madrid.

And Ince said: "It’s become a bigger game now with the signing of Pochettino, it puts a bit of juice into the game.

‌



"When you look at both teams this season, there are still a lot of questions to be answered. When United are struggling, it’s the biggest story in the world. It’s front and back pages.

"And Liverpool, they’re not quite there yet. When you think about the goals, even the Crystal Palace game the other week, Palace could have scored really four or five goals. Defensively, they’re giving teams so many chances. And that’s a worry.

"Maybe they should have kept Andy Robertson. I don’t think Milos Kerkez is a bad player, but I’m not sure he’s there yet. You’ve got Ronald Araujo playing right-back. Well, he’s a centre-half.

View 4 Images Ince is backing Bradley Barcola and Cody Gakpo to be the difference today

‌



"I love Jeremy Jacquet. I think he’s going to be great. But I just kind of think, when I look at that back four and I look for the spine of the team, I’m not sure they’ve got that quite right yet."

Despite his obvious midfield leanings, Ince doesn't believe the engine room will prove decisive at Anfield. Instead, the wide areas are where he regards the greatest attention should be paid.

"You always try to win the midfield battle," said Ince. "If you win the midfield, nine times out of 10 you win the game. You’ve got to win your duels, you’ve got to win your one-v-ones, make your tackles, and you’ve got to set teams on the way forward.

"But I think if you’re talking about actually where the danger is going to come from, I think it’d be wide, the full-backs and the wingers. When you look at Barcola, you look at Cody Gakpo, I think that they can win Liverpool the game. I really believe that.

‌



"Both teams are struggling with the full-backs. The danger is going to come from those wide areas."

Sports.title: How Fantasy Premier League's rapid growth gives managers an ‘unethical’ headache
Sports.content:
Fantasy Premier League is not just a bit of fun for football fans. It's a big business in its own right.

The Premier League's official fantasy game has over 11 million users, spanning 150 countries, and, according to its maker, has generated 1.4 billion page views. It's spawned and sustained countless content creators, podcasts and newsletters, with engaged communities willing to part with hard-earned cash in an effort to get ahead in their mini-league.

FPL started way back in the 2002/03 season, when Ruud van Nistelrooy fired Manchester United to the title, and has grown so big that it now interferes with the real-life football it is based upon.

Chelsea recently felt the need to warn their staff about inadvertently leaking teams news by using their insider info to tweak their FPL teams. It came after eagle-eyed fans spotted that Morgan Rogers' brother had sold in-form striker Joao Pedro before his injury became public knowledge.

‌



Meanwhile, Mikel Arteta has told his players to get rid of any Arsenal players from their FPL teams to avoid any risk of privileged information escaping the dressing room and giving rivals a heads-up. It comes after Christos Tzolis brought himself back into his own FPL team as captain following a period out injured, signalling he was fit again.

"Obviously the confidentiality is something critical because it's about trust and what you're trying to do and that should be kept as a huge secret," Arteta said on Friday. "And we will take measures to make sure that doesn't happen."

While it has become heightened recently due to the increased number of eyeballs and the higher stakes, it is not a new problem.

‌



'U nethical and unprofessional'

The phenomenon was first noticed back in January 2021 thanks to former Liverpool defender Andy Robertson. The Scot's FPL team was called 'Show Me the Mane' and he wasn't exactly trying to hide it from the public.

So when Robertson transferred out Sadio Mane - his teammate and the inspiration for his name - for Tottenham's Son Heung-min Liverpool fans knew something was afoot.

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

View 4 Images Andy Robertson left Sadio Mane out of his fantasy team, alerting FPL managers to his injury (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Low and behold, Mane was then left out of Jurgen Klopp's starting line-up that weekend, with an injury to blame. Robertson had used his own privileged information to change his fantasy team - and while it didn't do him much good, with his team sitting 1,656,552nd out of 7,919,731 players at the time - it did spark some developments.

A Twitter account called 'FPL Insider' was set up with a bot which scanned the FPL accounts of staff and players and posted their transfers. It was by this method that an injury to Jack Grealish, then of Aston Villa, was picked up before it was public knowledge thanks to Villa's Matt Targett, Conor Hourihane and Neil Taylor, as well as two Villa staff members, transferring Grealish out.

View 4 Images The FPL Insider account caused a lot of headaches for Premier League managers at its height in 2021 (Image: X/@insider_fpl)

"I've been made aware that on social media there'd been rumours that he wasn't going to play," Aston Villa manager Dean Smith said after his side lost 2-1 to Leicester without Grealish.

‌



"If it's coming out of our training ground then I will find out where that's coming from and reprimand where it's coming from." Smith reportedly banned his players and staff from playing FPL in response.

"Sometimes you make a team selection and players speak to friends on other teams and talk about what you do," was how Manchester City boss Pep Guardiola responded. "Sometimes it happens and it is incredibly unethical and unprofessional but you cannot control it."

'Concerned about integrity'

The FPL Insider Twitter account stopped posting at the end of the 2021/22 season, but leaks have continued to pop up on social media every now and then.

Interestingly, it's not just Premier League managers who are worried. It seems it is a two-way street, as a well-connected FPL source told Mirror Football: “The general consensus among the FPL managers we've spoken to is that the Premier League is interfering with the FPL product, rather than the other way around.

‌



View 4 Images Fantasy Premier League is serious business for millions worldwide (Image: Fantasy Premier League)

"FPL managers are concerned that the integrity of the game might be somehow harmed by the clear advantage that Premier League players - and seemingly everyone on their Christmas card lists - have over the civilians who play the game.

“Ultimately, FPL is a game of information, and the privileged information that these players have access to - injuries, rotation, how a player performs in training etc - means that FPL is no longer a level playing field. It's one of those bumpy playing fields, like the one your local Sunday league team has to play on, in which knowing where the key divots and bobbles are might be the difference between winning and losing.”

Whether FPL 2026/27 will be won by a Premier League player, a staff member or one of their relatives remains to be seen. But as the game keeps developing, it seems likely that more controversy is to come.

Sports.title: How Mauricio Pochettino was reinvigorated by the USMNT and finally landed Man Utd job
Sports.content:
It was behind closed doors two years ago that Mauricio Pochettino and Manchester United's drawn out public flirtation almost culminated in the Argentine landing the job he craved long before he finally stepped out at Carrington earlier this week.

After being pipped to the post by Erik ten Hag two years prior, Pochettino was sounded out about replacing the Dutchman in the summer of 2024. Though previous courtships had been played out in the public eye, this was very much the opposite. Pochettino had not long left Chelsea, while Ten Hag, though heavily scrutinised, was still officially in his post as manager.

In the end, Ineos and Pochettino would decide against taking things further. It's understood that United felt Pochettino was still bruised by the year he spent in charge at Chelsea; a body of work which has only got better with age.

Though he has had to wait that big longer, Pochettino has now been deemed ready and rejuvenated to a point where he is suitable to tackle the gargantuan task of rehabilitating a Manchester United side who have endured their worst start to a season in 40 years.

‌



Getting to this point has not been without its complications, though through no fault of Pochettino's own. On paper, the job he did at Chelsea was not dissatisfactory; the Argentine guided Chelsea to a sixth-place finish, which represented a commendable recovery considering the turbulent start to his reign.

During his time at the helm, Pochettino had to juggle an inflated squad assembled for grand outlays in an environment where the expectations were perhaps, even grander.

Mauricio Pochettino wants to scrap Man Utd system from Michael Carrick reign READ MORE :

Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



The manner of his exit, which was mutually agreed with the Blues' ownership, was swift. It was no surprise, either, given the rumblings of discontent between Pochettino and the club hierarchy which had been present for months.

That, coupled with a similarly taxing but rewarding spell at Paris Saint-Germain which culminated in Pochettino's first major honours as a manager, was enough to put United off the idea of finally giving Pochettino the keys to the Old Trafford kingdom.

There were no such reservations, however, at U.S Soccer. Pochettino was exactly the type of high-profile coach they craved ahead of a much anticipated home World Cup.

While few would have predicted Pochettino to transition to international management with a nation like the US back at the peak of his powers when he was coveted by Europe's elite, his decision to embark on an unexpected career arc with the United States men's national team, following talks with former Southampton ally Matt Crocker in his role as technical director of the U.S. Soccer Federation, appears to have paid dividends.

‌



Pochettino's stint in America has re-energised a coach who long appeared to have the required charisma and drive to manage in the figurehead role of a footballing institution like Manchester United.

View 4 Images Pochettino is finally in place at Manchester United (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images)

That is despite the fact that the USMNT's exploits at the World Cup, much like Pochettino's stints at Chelsea and PSG, were steady rather than spectacular.

Success at a home World Cup was always the ultimate goal; a prize which would trump anything that preceded it. But their campaign was preceded by a turbulent 2025 which saw Pochettino's credentials questioned. The team regrouped and started the tournament in spectacular fashion, romping to a 4-1 victory in the opener over Paraguay. That dazzling show in Los Angeles was followed up by the USMNT's first victory in a World Cup knockout game since 2002. Pochettino's men rode the crest of a wave until it crashed in the last 16, their journey coming full circle with a bludgeoning 4-1 defeat at the hands of Belgium.

‌



Pochettino's impact in the role transcended that last 16 finish and he was subsequently offered an extension. With the twinkle back in his eye and whispers of a Premier League return, the decision to extend until 2030 raised eyebrows.

But unlike at PSG and Chelsea, Pochettino had unearthed the right cultural fit for the first time since those halcyon days at Tottenham.

View 4 Images Pochettino encountered good and bad times with the USMNT (Image: Getty)

JT Batson, the chief executive of U.S. Soccer, expressed how important that element had been when they decided to offer Pochettino the job back in 2024. Speaking to The Athletic prior to the World Cup, he said: “Just because someone is a big name, doesn’t mean they’re the right fit for what you’re trying to do.

‌



“(The coach) needed to be a good cultural fit, a good strategic fit for U.S. Soccer, as well as for the men’s national team. That was, first and foremost, the most important thing.”

Though not the expected - or orthodox - environment for Pochettino to rediscover his mojo, Manchester United stand to benefit from his odyssey across the Atlantic.

Just as he leaves U.S. Soccer in an emboldened position, Pochettino looks, sounds and feels re-energised.

View 4 Images Pochettino departed the USMNT not long after signing a contract extension to join United (Image: Matthew Huang/Icon Sportswire)

‌



The most obvious threat to his renaissance is the fact that he is once again about to embark into the pressure cooker of an elite club.

But this is also the club, and the job, that Pochettino has long wanted. Manchester United feel he is ready for it. Crucially, suggestions that he instructed his representatives to make United aware of the release clause in his USMNT contract would indicate he feels he is, too.

That he referenced culture in his first message to supporters is telling. Building it from the beleaguered foundations inherited is another matter altogether.

But Pochettino has done it before. Famously on these shores. And after experiencing it with the US, there is reason enough to suggest he can do it once again.

Sports.title: Bruno Guimaraes shows true colours with behaviour at full-time after brutal Newcastle boos
Sports.content:
Bruno Guimaraes shows true colours with behaviour at full-time after brutal Newcastle boos

Arsenal star Bruno Guimaraes left Newcastle United in the summer and was playing at St James' Park for the first time since his exit as the Gunners were held to a draw

View 3 Images Bruno Guimaraes was booed on his return to St James' Park (Image: Serena Taylor/Newcastle United via Getty Images)

There was no hero's welcome for Arsenal star Bruno Guimaraes as he returned to Newcastle for the first time since his summer transfer. The Magpies held the Premier League leaders to a draw at St James' Park on an occasion when the Toon Army expressed exactly how they felt.

‌



‌



Guimaraes was booed on his way into the ground, when he warmed up and during the match, but nevertheless took the time to complete a lap of the ground, waving to the crowd, following the full-time whistle. The midfielder received a few rounds of applause but was still met with a negative response from many of those remaining in the ground in the North East.

‌



Such was the sustained hostility, Guimaraes could only show a glum expression as he made his way back to the tunnel to head towards the dressing room. The 29-year-old, who captained Newcastle to their first domestic trophy in 70 years, was, however, offered a warmer greeting by his former teammates.

‌



Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Guimaraes was embraced by figures such as Malick Thiaw and Tino Livramento as he was crowded in the centre of the field following the game. The Brazilian could be seen having positive interactions with members of Newcastle's backroom team too.

‌



The former Newcastle star could not help his new team to three points on his old stomping ground. The Gunners took the lead in a commanding first-half performance when Eberechi Eze opened the scoring.

Matthias Jaissle's side fought back after the break as Harvey Barnes and Thiaw turned the game on its head. David Raya was forced off the field with an injury, while Guimaraes was replaced by Myles Lewis-Skelly as Mikel Arteta attempted to get his side back in the clash.

‌



View 3 Images Arsenal's Bruno Guimaraes applauds the Newcastle United fans (Image: Lee Parker - CameraSport via Getty Images)

View 3 Images Arsenal player Bruno Guimaraes with Malick Thiaw (Image: Stu Forster/Getty Images)

‌

Sports.title: Enzo Maresca reveals exactly what Erling Haaland said during Man City VAR controversy
Sports.content:
Enzo Maresca reveals exactly what Erling Haaland said during Man City VAR controversy

Manchester City were forced to settle for a point against Fulham but only after Erling Haaland saw a first-half goal controversially ruled out by the officials

View 2 Images Erling Haaland reacts after his goal vs Fulham was disallowed

Enzo Maresca insists Erling Haaland was ‘absolutely sure’ his disallowed goal vs Fulham was going to stand.

‌



‌



City’s winless run in the Premier League extended to four matches as the Cottagers earned an impressive point at the Etihad. Fulham had taken the lead through Rodrigo Muniz, before Haaland thought he had equalised in the 25th minute.

‌



The Norwegian fluffed his lines after a brilliant Phil Foden cross, but bundled the ball across the line when Bernd Leno appeared to spill it. However, referee Thomas Bramall disallowed the goal, before VAR officials in Stockley Park defended his decision.

‌



A statement from the Premier League Match Centre said: “The referee’s call of free-kick to Fulham and no goal to Manchester City was checked and confirmed by VAR – with the goalkeeper deemed to be in control of the ball.”

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



During discussions between Bramall and his VAR, he was told: “The ball is in control between both hands and then is played out of that possession by the attacker, and then into the back of the net.”

City eventually found an equaliser through Elliot Anderson but had to settle for a point as they failed to beat Fulham for the first time in 15 years.

‌



However, Maresca was adamant the goal should have stood, with Haaland similarly convinced that the decision would be overturned in his favour.

“I reviewed the goal after the game,” Maresca explained. “It is quite clear that it’s not a foul. But I’m not the guy who decides unfortunately.

‌



View 2 Images Bernd Leno was adjudged to be in possession of the ball when Haaland scored

“He [Haaland] was absolutely sure. Even when they were reviewing the VAR, he was absolutely sure that it was a goal. I asked from the touchline and he was completely sure it was a goal, but again the referee decided for different things.”

‌



City have now gone four games either side of the international break without a win as their hopes of a sustained title change continue to fade.

Maresca added: "It's a tough moment in terms of results. We don't like these moments. It's also normal when you are trying to build something new."

‌



"It's something we are doing wrong. After going behind you do things, you rush, and that's not good for us. We need to find a way to keep a clean sheet. All the Premier League games are in this way [with opposition having a go]."

Sports.title: Bayern chief admits Jamal Musiala could be sold months after collpasing on pitch
Sports.content:
Bayern chief admits Jamal Musiala could be sold months after collpasing on pitch

Bayern Munich star Jamal Musiala returned to action on Friday night, but there are growing fears he may not return to his best after a number of health issues

View 2 Images Jamal Musiala collapsed on the pitch twice during pre-season

Bayern Munich chief Karl-Heinz Rummenigge has admitted they could be forced to sell Jamal Musiala due to his ongoing health issues.

‌



‌



Musiala collapsed twice on the pitch in a matter of days and was subsequently diagnosed with a ‘neurological dysfunction’. The 24-year-old was insistent that there was no additional health risk and suggested that the condition would not impact his career moving forward.

‌



However, Rumenigge has now revealed that Bayern will have to make a decision on his future due to his bumper contract and fears he will never return to his previous levels.

‌



Rummenigge told Sky Germany: “He has a health-related issue. It's also well known that he has a contract involving very substantial sums of money. As a club, we have to consider how to deal with that situation. I think that's responsible and perfectly normal.

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



“What we know unfortunately suggests it will be difficult for him to get back to the level he has often shown here in this stadium.”

Rumenigge said discussions will take place over the player’s future, but worryingly warned he will be difficult to sell in his current condition.

‌



He added: “We need to talk to the family, the player, and the agency, because then these sums of money, sorry, with all due respect, are no longer feasible. I cannot imagine that Jamal wants to leave the club or that any other club would buy him under these conditions.

“We are all interested in his return, ideally in top form. But what happens if that isn’t the case? Then we still have to think about the finances. The discussion hasn’t taken place yet. These are just ideas at this stage.”

‌



View 2 Images Musiala returned to action for Bayern on Friday night

Bayern signed Musiala from Chelsea in 2019, before the winger made his breakthrough at senior level in the 2020/21 season.

‌



In 2025, he signed a new deal at the Allianz, which saw him become the highest-paid player at the club. A position he held until Harry Kane recently extended his own deal with the German champions.

Musiala has struggled to get going this season, but after collapsing for the second time in August, he issued a statement on his social media explaining how his diagnosis was affecting him.

‌



"I've been diagnosed with temporary, brief, but easily treatable absence seizures, which are due to a neurological dysfunction," he said.

Sports.title: Lewis Moody, 48, stares down New Zealand Haka with England as ITV viewers brought to tears
Sports.content:
Lewis Moody, 48, stares down New Zealand Haka with England as ITV viewers brought to tears

England legend Lewis Moody, who was diagnosed with motor neurone disease in September 2025, joined Steve Borthwick's players on the pitch to face the New Zealand haka ahead of Saturday's clash at Twickenham

View 3 Images Lewis Moody faced down the haka (Image: David Rogers, Getty Images)

Former England captain Lewis Moody joined Steve Borthwick's squad on the pitch to confront the New Zealand haka in an extraordinary moment before Saturday's encounter at the Allianz Stadium. The 2003 Rugby World Cup champion stood beside the current England team as they formed an arrow formation in answer to the traditional Maori challenge, with Moody positioned at the head of the arrangement in a gesture that touched spectators watching globally.

‌



‌



Moody, who received his motor neurone disease (MND) diagnosis in September 2025, was also afforded the privilege of presenting the England players with their jerseys before kick-off. The venue erupted as Moody appeared from the tunnel to be greeted by skipper Maro Itoje before taking his position to face the New Zealanders.

‌



Every England player embraced Moody before he departed the pitch to a standing ovation. The 48-year-old's participation created a particularly moving occasion, with England's choice to invite one of their former icons into their haka response attracting widespread acclaim.

‌



Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

It proved a stirring sight as Moody stood alongside the players, with the ex-flanker once more confronting the All Blacks' renowned pre-match ritual.

‌



Co-commentator Ben Kay, who played alongside Moody, said: "It's very, very difficult to talk about that. I don't think there's anyone I played with that that would have meant more to. He was so pumped up for games. Loved facing the haka."

The response from viewers was instantaneous, with social media awash with messages from fans who confessed they had been brought to tears by the scenes. Television presenter Sonja McLaughlin was amongst those expressing her feelings, posting: "OMG what a brilliant idea to have Lewis Moody face the Haka. That's hit right in the feels."

‌



View 3 Images Lewis Moody faces the haka (Image: 2026 The RFU)

View 3 Images Lewis Moody stands at the tip of England's arrow to face the haka

‌



Another spectator commented: "Emotional scenes at Twickenham. Lewis Moody one of the greats."

The England setup also received recognition for including the former skipper in their response, with one fan posting: "A superb gesture from @EnglandRugby inviting @LewisMoody7 into the response."

‌



Someone else remarked: "Brilliant to see Lewis Moody on the pitch with England to face the Haka."

‌



The emotional weight of the occasion was evident in numerous other messages, with one viewer confessing: "Might be crying here a tiny bit watching Lewis Moody on pitch for the Haka."

A further supporter contributed: "Lewis Moody faces the Haka once again. That was a special moment. Now, let's bring it ABs."

‌



Another shared: "In tears already seeing Lewis Moody with the England Rugby team! Face the Haka! Of New Zealand.."

The moment formed part of the unveiling of Moody's new 'Front Up to MND' campaign, in partnership with the My Name'5 Doddie Foundation.

The project seeks to generate over £1million for research into the devastating disease, with its inaugural major fundraising event, 'Front Up: Walk the Coast', scheduled for June 12, 2027. Thousands of participants are being urged to complete 26-mile sections of coastline throughout England, Scotland and Wales, with over 175 routes on offer.

Moody has been resolute in using his platform to assist others living with the condition since announcing his diagnosis, and Saturday's occasion provided a platform to bring the campaign to a massive rugby audience.

Sports.title: Parrott fires Republic of Ireland into Nations League play-offs
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott fired the Republic of Ireland into a Nations League play-off berth with two penalties in their 3-0 victory over 10-man Kosovo at the Aviva Stadium in Dublin.

The result ensured the Republic finished runners-up in group B3, and also propelled the Euro 2028 co-hosts into a coveted pot-two seeding for next month's qualifying draw for that competition.

Tuesday night's contest turned on its head in the 26th minute, when Kreshnik Hajrizi was sent off for handling the ball off the line, and Parrott took advantage with a top-corner finish.

The Real Betis striker doubled the Republic's lead from the spot five minutes after the restart, and Jack Moylan added a 75th-minute cushion to keep alive the hosts' hopes of booking a place in League A for the first time through the March play-off.

Image: Parrot struck twice from the penalty spot

Heimir Hallgrimsson's lone change from Saturday's defeat to group winners Austria was the insertion of John Egan into the line-up, replacing injured captain Nathan Collins.

How Ireland finished as group runners-up...

It was a contest that lacked fluidity in the opening 10 minutes, before the Republic found a foothold and Finn Azaz looked to pick out Parrott, but was blocked.

Kosovo then twice missed chances to take the lead. Lindon Emerllahu fired just wide in the 17th minute, and Caoimhin Kelleher was called into action for the first time a minute later to deny Vedat Muriqi.

What had been a largely uneventful encounter suddenly took a dramatic twist in the 26th minute, a red-card incident sparked by Moylan's cross, glanced on by Liam Scales to Parrott.

His effort - clearly goalbound - was cleared off the line by Hajrizi, who extended his arm like a goalkeeper, and was immediately shown a red card by Latvian referee Edgars Malcevs.

Parrott stepped up and gave Arijanet Muric no chance when he rifled into the top right corner to set the Republic on their way.

It remained just a one-goal advantage at the break despite a handful of chances falling the Republic's way, while the visitors created one when Kelleher denied Ilir Krasniqi with 10 minutes remaining to ensure there would be no first-half equaliser.

There was a flurry of Republic chances immediately after the second half kicked off before Parrott added his second penalty.

Muric had just denied Jayson Molumby's effort from range and Parrott was rushing forward to meet the loose ball when he was taken down by the Kosovo keeper.

This time he dove in the right direction, but failed to stop Parrott from doubling the hosts' lead.

The Republic were less successful from open play, unable to put the game away from a string of subsequent chances despite finding themselves in plenty of space, and should have added a third before the hour.

Moylan's persistence finally paid off with 15 minutes remaining, nodding home substitute Liam Kitching's cross in off the post.

The Republic nearly added a late fourth when Adam Idah stung the palms of Muric with two minutes left.

Parrott dreaming of home Euros

Republic of Ireland striker Troy Parrott speaking to RTÉ about the 2028 Euros:

"I've been thinking about it since I was a kid, I think everyone has.

"Look, it's not a guarantee that we are going to qualify for that tournament, so I think tonight was very important to get into pot two so that we have a better draw.

"We'll be going into the qualifiers now, trying to make sure that we qualify for the tournament.

"A tournament that's one of the host nations being Ireland, without Ireland it would be heartbreaking for all of us, so I think it's a mission now to make sure that we're there.

"It was disappointing that we didn't win the group because that's what we all wanted to do at the start.

"There's been so many nearly matches where we've nearly won, we've played really well and haven't won, and I think tonight we went out there with the mindset that no matter what we have to win.

"Obviously the red card helped us, but I have no doubt in my mind that group of players who were out on that pitch would have won that game."

'We want to play the top teams'

Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson speaking at his post-match press conference:

"Everybody, and especially us, likes to play the top teams. To compare yourself with the best teams, that's one thing.

"Second is those teams will expose your weaknesses, and that helps you in your growth to play these teams, so we can continue our growth.

"We're already looking forward to March. Tough teams in the pot. Whoever we draw is going to be a tough two games, and it's good for this team at this time to play these matches instead of friendlies.

"We're really excited for March, and looking forward to meeting the players again."

Sports.title: Kalajdzic scores late as Republic of Ireland taste defeat in Austria
Sports.content:
Sasa Kalajdzic dealt the Republic of Ireland a late blow in Linz with the only goal in Austria's 1-0 Nations League victory at the Raiffeisen Arena.

The result ensured that, no matter how the closing contests in Group B play out, Austria sealed promotion to League A.

Ireland enter Tuesday's critical home clash at the Aviva Stadium in third place, with one point fewer than their final opponents, Kosovo.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's men were not without chances, but only Kalajdzic made one count when he broke the deadlock in the 79th minute.

Sports.title: Hallgrimsson urges UEFA to keep Ireland and Israel apart in future
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland drew 1-1 with Israel in a behind-closed-doors contest in Serbia; there were allegations of spitting by an Israeli player at half-time, while the Israeli government criticised the Irish players for bowing their heads during the national anthem

Republic of Ireland: Heimir Hallgrimsson calls on UEFA to keep Ireland and Israel apart in future after tense draw

Ireland's head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson has called for UEFA to keep his team and Israel separate in future

Heimir Hallgrimsson has called on UEFA to keep Ireland and Israel apart in future.

The Ireland boss was speaking following his side's 1-1 UEFA Nations League draw with Israel behind closed doors in Serbia.

The games between the two nations this international break were overshadowed by politics, with the Football Association of Ireland (FAI) urged to boycott the internationals amid ongoing conflict in the Israel-Gaza War.

This continued in Serbia, as Ireland fitness coach Damien Doyle was allegedly spat on by an Israeli player at half-time, according to reports in the stadium.

Irish media reported that the incident took place as the teams went down the tunnel. Ireland boss Hallgrimsson confirmed there was an allegation, but he admitted he didn't see it and declined to comment further on it.

However, when asked if the two countries should be playing each other again, he told RTE Sport: "No, they shouldn't. That's not ours to decide - that's UEFA who decides that. Obviously, there's a big support for Palestine in Ireland. There's not many countries that support Palestine as much as Ireland does.

"I wouldn't wish any national team to go through what we've gone through in these two weeks, so maybe UEFA just needs to step in and do something."

Sky Sports News has contacted UEFA for comment.

Israeli Government accuses ROI of 'moral blindness'

The Israeli Government have accused the Ireland football team of "moral blindness" for bowing their heads during their national anthem.

For the second time in a week, the Irish players, coaching team and FAI all bowed their heads while the Israeli national anthem was played pre-match.

Image: Republic of Ireland players bowed their heads during the national anthem

The official Israeli Government X account posted: "While some use the football field as their political theatre, for us this is personal.

"1939: Irish players raised their arms in salute to Nazi Germany.

"2026: Irish players bowed their heads during Israel's anthem.

"Different generations. The same moral blindness.

"Today, Israel's players wear black armbands to remember those brutally massacred by Hamas on October 7 - including former professional footballer Lior Asulin.

"Some of us have skin in the game. Others just make a show of it."

Sky Sports News has contacted the FAI for comment.

Two Israeli journalists banned for post-match press conferences

Meanwhile, prior to the match, UEFA confirmed that two Israeli journalists were banned from the post-match press conferences, after Saturday's pre-match Ireland press conference descended into chaos.

The media access for Ireland was cut short after an Israeli journalist alleged that Israeli players had claimed Irish players had racially abused them during the match in Hungary last weekend.

The journalist alleged that a derogatory term had been used, which Sky Sports has chosen not to repeat. The term is not associated with antisemitic or anti-Israeli abuse.

An Irish press officer refuted the allegation, saying: "That's completely untrue," before bringing the news conference to a premature close.

After the press conference ended abruptly, Serbian police were called following an allegation of assault by an Israeli journalist, who said a microphone had been taken from them by an FAI press officer.

Sky Sports News understands that no further action was taken by police.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland draw with Israel in second Nations League meeting
Sports.content:
Match report and reaction as Republic of Ireland drew 1-1 with Israel in behind-closed-doors contest in Serbia; Troy Parrott's first-half penalty was cancelled out after the break; sides clashed at half-time

Republic of Ireland 1-1 Israel: Troy Parrott scores again as sides draw second controversial Nations League meeting

The Republic of Ireland drew 1-1 with Israel in the second controversial Nations League fixture between the sides.

Troy Parrott's first-half penalty was cancelled out by Dor Peretz after the break in the behind-closed-doors game in Serbia.

The Republic's 'home' fixture was held on neutral territory at the 4,500-seat TSC arena in Backa Topola, due to "operational challenges that could impact on the delivery of the game on home soil" according to a June Football Association of Ireland (FAI) statement.

Both sides wore black armbands. The Republic's, the same as in Hungary to acknowledge - as the Football Association of Ireland chief David Courrell explained before that contest - "all lives lost" in the ongoing Israel-Hamas conflict.

Israel's armbands - which read "7.10" - were to commemorate the October 7, 2023 Hamas-led attack on southern Israel, their official X account confirmed.

The pitch featured no sponsored content or branding, just UEFA graphics with slogans like "football for all", a decision taken by the FAI.

Image: The referee pleads with the benches in Serbia

Tensions rose at half-time after a fracas broke out in front of the tunnel and players from both sides engaged in a heated argument, with the Israeli Government later accusing Irish players of "moral blindness" for bowing their heads during Israel's national anthem, as they did in Monday's first match.

Officials broke up a second altercation in three minutes of added time, and there were more heated words exchanged after the final whistle.

On the pitch Parrott, who has now scored 10 times in his last seven competitive internationals, fired the Republic in front from the spot in the 39th minute before Dor Peretz drew the sides level two minutes after the restart.

The result puts Ireland third in Nations League Group B3, level on points with second-placed Kosovo.

Hallgrimsson calls on UEFA to keep Ireland and Israel apart in future

Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson has called on UEFA to keep Ireland and Israel apart in future.

Speaking after the 1-1 draw, Hallgrimsson also declined to comment on the half-time fracas between the two sides.

When asked if the two countries should be playing each other again, he told RTE Sport: "No, they shouldn't. That's not ours to decide - that's UEFA who decides that. Obviously, there's a big support for Palestine in Ireland. There's not many countries that support Palestine as much as Ireland does.

"I wouldn't wish any national team to go through what we've gone through in these two weeks, so maybe UEFA just needs to step in and do something."

On the half-time incident, he said in his post-match press conference: "I was there. I'm not going to comment on it. It's something that a disciplinary committee is probably going to look at."

Sky Sports News has contacted UEFA for comment.

Two Israeli journalists banned for post-match press conferences

Meanwhile, prior to the match, UEFA confirmed that two Israeli journalists were banned from the post-match press conferences, after Saturday's pre-match Ireland press conference descended into chaos.

The media access for Ireland was cut short after an Israeli journalist alleged that Israeli players had claimed Irish players had racially abused them during the match in Hungary last weekend.

The journalist alleged a derogatory term was used - which Sky Sports has chosen not to repeat. It is not a term associated with being antisemitic or anti-Israeli.

An Irish press officer refuted the allegation, saying "that's completely untrue", and brought the news conference to a premature close.

After the press conference ended abruptly, Serbian police were called due to an allegation of assault by an Israeli journalist who had the microphone taken from them by an FAI press officer.

Sky Sports News understands there was no further action was taken by police.

Sports.title: Ireland news conference cut short after tense exchanges with Israeli media
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland vs Israel is being played in Serbia as the FAI moved the game to a neutral venue for "operational reasons" in June following widespread calls for a boycott; protests briefly halted Ireland's draw with Austria on Thursday over opposition to Sunday's Israel fixture

Republic of Ireland vs Israel: Heimir Hallgrimsson's press conference cut short after tense exchanges with Israeli media

Republic of Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson's pre-match press conference ahead of Sunday's match against Israel in Serbia ended abruptly after a tense exchange with Israeli media.

The media access was cut short after an Israeli journalist alleged that Israeli players had claimed they were racially abused by Irish players during their match in Hungary last Sunday.

The journalist alleged a derogatory term was used - which Sky Sports has chosen not to repeat. It is not a term associated with being antisemitic or anti-Israeli.

An Irish press officer refuted the allegation, saying "that's completely untrue", and brought the news conference to a premature close as one of his colleagues remonstrated with the reporter.

Image: Ireland's players bowed their heads before facing Israel in the reverse fixture last week

Hallgrimsson later labelled the accusation a "verbal attack" during a separate briefing for members of the Irish press.

The exchange in the main press conference took place after Hallgrimsson was also asked a question about a co-pilot who attacked a pilot and tried to hijack a flight travelling from Dubai to Tel Aviv earlier this week.

The reporter's question was shut down by the FAI press officer.

Sky Sports News understands there are no open UEFA investigations at this stage from the previous meeting between Israel and Ireland last weekend.

The FAI are conducting their own investigation into whether striker Adam Idah was racially abused by Israeli supporters during their 3-0 UEFA Nations League win but have yet to make an official complaint to UEFA.

Image: Protesters interrupted Ireland's draw with Austria by throwing tennis balls onto the pitch with Palestine flags on them

Despite the high-profile nature of the fixture, members of the Irish media later reported that there was no UEFA delegate present at the news conference.

Sky Sports News was told a UEFA match delegate does not have to attend press conferences. The duty is left to the venue media manager, whose job it is to report anything if there is an incident.

Sunday's match is being played in Backa Topola, Serbia, as the FAI moved the game to a neutral venue for "operational reasons" in June following widespread calls for a boycott.

Sky Sports News has approached the FAI for comment.

Sports.title: Ireland held by Austria despite Parrott double as protests interrupt game
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott scored twice but the Republic of Ireland were forced to settle for a 2-2 draw after Austria came back in the second half of their Nations League encounter at the Aviva Stadium in Dublin.

The contest was twice interrupted in the opening 45 minutes, first due to what campaign group Stop the Game later referred to in a statement as a "limited tennis ball protest", when - around the 20th minute - tennis balls wrapped in stickers featuring the Palestinian flag and the text '#StopTheGame' were launched onto the pitch.

The match paused a second time when an invader carrying what appeared to be a Palestine flag entered the pitch and was promptly tackled and carried off by security.

The protests came after Ireland's decision not to boycott their game against Israel last week - although goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu did make himself unavailable.

Ireland are due to face Israel again on Sunday.

Image: Tennis balls with Palestine flags were throw onto the pitch

Before the protests, Parrott scored a sensational 12th-minute opener, and then added a penalty on the stroke of half-time.

A pair of substitutes proved Ireland's undoing after Alexander Prass halved the deficit in the 71st minute and Michael Gregoritsch drew the sides level six minutes later.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had a chance to top Group B3 with a victory, but they sit third behind Austria and Kosovo at the halfway point of the group stage.

Hallgrimsson made three changes, including the reintroduction of Finn Azaz, who was greeted warmly when his name was announced over the PA system before the match.

Bazunu was back in the squad, while Liam Scales and John Egan were awarded starts.

There was a significant security and police presence outside the stadium, where a small group of protesters also gathered before kick-off.

There was an audacious early effort from Sasa Kalajdzic, who tried to catch Caoimhin Kelleher off his line with a lob from midfield, before Ireland enjoyed a couple of attacking spells deep in the visitors' half.

Image: Parrott is congratulated after scoring his second goal against Austria

It was a brilliant opener from Parrott, who realised he was on his own after bringing down Adam Idah's glanced-on header from a goal kick.

The Real Betis striker was sandwiched in a triangle of white shirts, before nutmegging Philipp Lienhardt and evading every other challenger with a mazy run before planting the ball past Florian Wiegele and into the bottom corner.

Image: A protestor was carried off the pitch during the game

Kelleher denied Patrick Wimmer and there were a few more promising spells for Austria before Parrott doubled their lead.

Ryan Manning won the penalty after he was clipped in the box by Nicolas Seiwald. Parrott stepped up after a VAR check and blasted it past the Austria 'keeper.

Austria cut the deficit after Liam Kitching was caught out and Austria worked the ball to the unmarked Prass, who blasted the ball beyond Kelleher. The offside flag was initially raised, but the decision was reversed after a VAR check.

The Brentford goalkeeper then failed to stop Gregoritsch's free-kick as Ralf Rangnick's side fought back for a point.

Ireland captain Dara O'Shea was denied by an excellent leaping Wiegele save, Gregoritsch directed a shot over the crossbar and both sides fended off attempts at a late winner.

Sports.title: Hallgrimsson admits 'toughest days' of career after Ireland beat Israel
Sports.content:
The Republic of Ireland beat Israel 3-0 in their controversial Nations League fixture at a neutral venue in Hungary.

Players did not shake hands with each other before their meeting at the Nagyerdei Stadion in Debrecen and there was no exchange between Ireland captain Dara O'Shea and Israel's Manor Solomon.

Ireland players also appeared to bow their heads while Israel's national anthem was played out before kick-off.

Black armbands were worn by Ireland players, which Football Association of Ireland (FAI) chief executive David Courell said was a gesture to recognise "all lives lost" in the Israel-Gaza conflict.

Goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu was the only player who chose not to play after the squad voted to proceed with the match on Saturday amid calls for the game not to go ahead.

Goals from Troy Parrott, Adam Idah and Jack Moylan sealed the victory for Heimir Hallgrimsson's side.

Moylan celebrated his goal by kissing and raising his black armband before kissing his badge.

Hallgrimsson: I couldn't be more proud of the players

Republic of Ireland manager Heimir Hallgrimsson:

"It has been some of the toughest days of my coaching career, but its not about me.

"The game, the desire the players showed to make a statement on the pitch - they are football players, they wanted to show on the pitch, make that talking with their feet.

"What they did was impressive. In tough times that's when you find your leaders, there were so many players that stepped up in these tough times. The energy levels they showed was impressive.

"The performance was good given all the preparation, the lack of training, all of our meetings were about something other than football.

"I couldn't be more proud of the players.

"By playing I know we are making some people unhappy. By playing we are making others happy. Winning probably pleases everyone, but there will still be people angry that we played the game.

"I hope we can settle that slowly down and stay together as a team. I wish people in Ireland continue supporting these boys, because they certainly deserve it."

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland slip to deserved defeat in Kosovo
Sports.content:
The Republic of Ireland slipped to a 1-0 defeat away to Kosovo in their Nations League opener in Pristina.

The build-up to the League B3 encounter had been overshadowed by the controversy around upcoming fixtures against Israel, which Republic boss Heimir Hallgrimsson had admitted many of his squad members were uncomfortable about playing.

Chiedozie Ogbene had fired an early chance over before Kosovo responded to finish the first half strongly at the Fadil Vokrri Stadium.

The home side saw two shots cleared off the line and Ireland goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher then clawed away a header from Vedat Muriqi as Hallgrimsson's side got to the break on level terms.

Ireland - who are scheduled to play Israel in Hungary on Sunday and then again in a 'home' tie at another neutral venue in Serbia seven days later - dug in for the second half but were eventually undone with seven minutes left when Kosovo captain Muriqi bundled the ball in from close range.

Udinese defender James Abankwah was handed a first competitive start as part of a back five, with in-form Real Betis striker Troy Parrott the lone forward and Dara O'Shea taking the captain's armband.

Image: The Republic of Ireland have won two of their six games in 2026 so far

Ireland created what ended up being their only real clear chance in the 22nd minute. Abankwah got away down the right and ran into the Kosovo penalty area before cutting the ball back to Ogbene, who sent a curling effort over the crossbar.

Kosovo, who are in League B for the first time, went close on the half-hour mark when a cross from the left found its way through to Muriqi, whose angled shot was cleared off the line by Jayson Molumby.

Veldin Hodza then saw his 10-yard strike blocked in front of goal by O'Shea before Kelleher got up to claw away a looping header from Muriqi, which was set for the top corner.

Ireland made a positive start to the second half, with a deep cross from the right by Abankwah finding Parrott at the far post and his header was gathered by Kosovo goalkeeper Arijanet Muric.

Image: Vedat Muriqi scored the winner for Kosovo

Kosovo, though, continued to carry a threat themselves. Baton Zabergja sent a 20-yard effort just wide of the top corner, which again got the home supporters into full voice.

Muriqi forced Kelleher into another smart reaction save from an angled shot at the near post before Kosovo eventually made the breakthrough in the 83rd minute.

Ermal Krasniqi's shot was deflected onto the crossbar and Muriqi reacted quickest in a crowded six-yard box to nod the ball over the line.

Kosovo should have got a second late on when substitute Krasniqi dragged his shot wide after being set up by Muriqi following a break onto a long ball.

Ireland pay price for 'off day'

Ireland manager Heimir Hallgrimsson told RTE:

"[Kosovo are] a good team, momentum with them, crowd with them, and to be honest they deserve the win.

"There was nothing that we didn't know about how they would play, where their threats would be, but [it was] an off day for a lot of our players and [it is] a tough place to come to if you have an off day, so a deserved win for Kosovo."

Hallgrimsson added: "We were the team that needed to defend today and didn't connect in possession or passes, not as sharp as we have done.

"We have to quickly find out the reason that we had an off day. We can all do better than we did today.

"It is a two-day turnaround for the next one, so we better be quick…and do better than this versus Israel. They are probably in the same position as us [having lost to Austria]."

Asked if the controversy from playing the fixtures against Israel had impacted on his team's performance against Kosovo, Hallgrimsson said: "I couldn't say now. It is difficult to measure that one."

He added: "This is the situation, we have to cope with it. And like I said before the game, this camp is a test of character.

"We need to do better in that area than we did here today. We knew that we needed to win the duels, win the one-vs-ones, but sadly they had the upper hand on all the basics."

What it means and next fixtures

Sports.title: Huge crowd gathers for funeral of Irish boxer Lee Reeves after he passed away following knockout in the ring and three-month coma
Sports.content:
Huge crowd gathers for funeral of Irish boxer Lee Reeves after he passed away following knockout in the ring and three-month coma

Huge crowds have gathered today for the funeral of Irish boxer Lee Reeves who died this week.

The 31-year-old died in hospital on Monday after being placed in a medically induced coma following a fight in August.

After being knocked down twice in the 10th round, the Irish southpaw was carried from the ring on a stretcher following his defeat to fellow countryman Gary Cully and taken to hospital.

His promoters, Queensberry, later revealed he was in a 'critical but stable' condition before undergoing surgery.

Reeves was then placed in an induced coma, where he remained until his death three months later, surrounded by his family.

Along with being a professional boxer, Reeves was a serving member of the 12th Infantry Battalion out of Sarsfield Barracks, an ambassador for Limerick Treaty Suicide Prevention and a model.

A large crowd gathered at the Church of Our Lady, Queen of Peace for the funeral mass in Roxboro, Limerick, on Friday, with thousands also tuning in to a livestream of the service.

Dreams by The Cranberries played in the church as the coffin carrying Reeves' body, draped in the Irish tricolour, was carried inside.

Irish boxer Lee Reeves died on Monday after spending three months in a medically-induced coma

Family members accompanied the hearse carrying the coffin of boxer Lee Reeves arriving at Our Lady Queen Of Peace Church, Limerick, for his funeral with full military honours on Friday

Members of the Irish Defence Forces carry the coffin of boxer Reeves out of Our Lady Queen Of Peace Church, Limerick, on Friday

It had been brought to the church on an adapted gun carriage, as part of the military honours for the service.

His Defence Forces cap was also placed on the coffin.

Reeves' boxing gloves and belt, his Bible, and a pizza box were among items placed at the altar to represent his interests including his love of his religion – along with photographs of the Limerick-born boxer.

The mass heard tributes from some of his four sisters: Louise, Shannon, Jodie and Jessie, who described him as 'one of the greatest men on this earth' and 'an inspiration to everyone he met'.

Jodie told the funeral mass that Reeves was a family man who 'did everything' for his sisters.

'He was my mother's whole life, and she was his. He dedicated every fight to her, and no doubt made her proud.

'She was his number one supporter from day one.

'You were a father to us all, and that even includes Dad.'

She added: 'Nothing is going to be the same without you around, but I promise you'll never be forgotten.'

Jodie, also reading a tribute from Reeves' father, said: 'You had a heart and a presence that touched so many lives.'

Continuing that tribute, she added: 'God knows how much we will miss you, and how much of a piece of our hearts will go with you. Rest easy, son.'

Reeves had been carried out of the ring on a stretcher after his defeat to his countryman Gary Cully and taken to hospital (Source: Instagram/Lee Reeves)

A car is pictured following the funeral cortege of Reeves as it leaves Our Lady Queen Of Peace Church, Limerick, after his funeral mass on Friday

Wreaths and tributes are seen on display before the funeral of boxer Lee Reeves at Our Lady Queen Of Peace Church, Limerick,on Friday

Shannon said: 'I will miss you every day that I'm on this earth.'

She added: 'You never deserved this, brother, but it's not the end.

'Your story will live on, and your legacy will live on.'
