Sports.title: Verstappen leads parade of position-swapping to win in Las Vegas | 2026 Las Vegas Grand Prix report
Sports.content:
Max Verstappen scored his third grand prix victory of the season in a Las Vegas Grand Prix which was dominated by ‘yo-yo’ position swaps.

As he and other drivers predicted, the race saw constant changes of position from the start as drivers quickly exhausted their batteries on the Las Vegas Strip Circuit’s long straights. Positions swapped repeatedly as drivers varied their deployment strategies, or gained the use of Overtake Mode by drawing within a second of each other.

Verstappen exchanged the lead with George Russell several times in the opening laps of the race. One Mercedes replaced the other in the closing stages as Andrea Kimi Antonelli, who started on pole position, used soft tyres to get within range of the leader.

With 10 laps to go, Verstappen warned his Red Bull team that he felt Mercedes had found a deployment setting which would allow one of their cars to beat him to the finishing line. But his concern was never put to the test as the Mercedes pair dropped out of contention.

First Russell skidded off at turn five trying to regain second place from Antonelli. He appeared to run over some debris – possibly left by Isack Hadjar’s front wing failure several laps earlier. “Well done,” remarked Verstappen after apparently seeing Russell’s error on a video screen.”

Then Antonelli abruptly slowed as the penultimate lap began, letting the two McLaren drivers through into final podium positions. Lando Norris took second place ahead of Oscar Piastri, the latter being cleared by the stewards after an investigation for a potential yellow flag infringement.

Verstappen led home five Mercedes-powered cars, Alpine capitalising on a bad day for Racing Bulls to take fifth and sixth places. The two pink-and-blue cars were split by Charles Leclerc’s Ferrari as they crossed the line, but a 10-second penalty dropped him to 10th.

Both Ferrari drivers collected penalties on a grim Saturday for the Scuderia. Leclerc knocked team mate Lewis Hamilton into a spin at turn seven on lap 38.

Hamilton had already served a 10-second time penalty for cutting the track at the same point while gaining a position from Norris. He served the penalty during a mid-race Safety Car period which briefly dropped him to 14th place.

Leclerc’s penalty promoted Hamilton to seventh ahead of Carlos Sainz Jnr, who brought home a rare strong result for Williams. Team mate Alexander Albon was unable to start after a pre-race brake problem caused severe overheating on his car. Russell and Leclerc completed the points scorers.

Sergio Perez became the race’s second retirement when he tangled with Rafael Camara at turn 14 and crashed out, prompting the Safety Car’s appearance. Hadjar had been in the mix at the front until that point, but his front wing failed immediately after the restart. The stewards are looking into an incident between him and Russell, but cleared Hadjar of leaving the pits unsafely during the Safety Car period.

The Audi drivers finished outside the points in 11th and 12th. Hadjar recovered to 13th behind Bortoleto.

The race was a huge missed opportunity for Racing Bulls. Liam Lawson had to forfeit his seventh place on the grid and start from the pit lane due to a pre-race fuel leak. He came in 15th.

Arvid Lindblad showed what could have been possible for the team. He ran close to the leaders in the early stages and was holding fifth place when he spun into retirement during the Safety Car period.

Sports.title: Liam Paro Sets 24-Hour VADA Deadline For Devin Haney
Sports.content:
IBF welterweight champion Liam Paro has given WBO champion Devin Haney 24 hours to enroll in VADA testing, or he will walk away from their December 20 unification fight in San Francisco. That is a pretty bold ultimatum from a guy entering the biggest payday of his career, especially when Haney is the A-side drawing the crowd at the Chase Center.

No Limit promoter Matt Rose confirmed the deadline on Sunday morning after Paro called Haney out on social media over the delay.

“We’re very disappointed they [Team Haney] have failed to enroll in VADA testing,” Rose told Fox Sports Australia. “One of the first things we agreed to when negotiating this fight was that VADA testing would take place. So now we’re giving them 24 hours …”

Paro already went after Haney on X over the weekend, questioning why the three-division titleholder hadn’t signed the paperwork yet despite preaching about clean boxing for the past two years.

“@realdevinhaney you preach serious boxing and speak out against PEDS, yet we’re still waiting for you to agree to VADA testing to begin. What’s the hold up???” wrote Paro.

Haney fired back quickly, reminding everyone about his testing track record and taking another shot at Ryan Garcia, who tested positive for ostarine after their April 2024 bout.

“This is will be my 14th consecutive fight using VADA testing,” Haney wrote. “Over 65 clean tests. Thanks for tagging the cheater.. the one that got popped for PEDS.”

The Problem With The Paperwork

If Haney has already gone through more than 65 VADA tests without a single issue, what is taking so long to get the forms signed for December 20? You can understand why Paro (25-1, 15 KOs) is suspicious. Haney spent all of 2024 and 2025 demanding 24/7 year-round testing, filing lawsuits against Garcia, and lecturing everyone about drug cheats. Now that he is moving up to 147 pounds to face a tough Australian southpaw, the enrollment is suddenly dragging out less than a month before fight night.

Paro already got under Haney’s skin at their launch press conference when Team Haney showed up nearly half an hour late.

“I don’t want any excuses or lawyers,” Paro said across the stage. “That’s what happened last time, isn’t it?”

Team Haney has until Monday to get the paperwork submitted. If they miss that deadline, Paro can pack his bags in Las Vegas and leave Haney scrambling for a replacement on December 20.

Sports.title: David Morrell Stops Julio Rodriguez in First Round
Sports.content:
David Morrell (13-2, 10 KOs) stopped Julio de Jesus Rodriguez (27-11, 24 KOs) by first-round TKO on Saturday night, November 21, at the Coliseo Carlos “Teo” Cruz in Santo Domingo, Dominican Republic.

The Cuban southpaw hurt Rodriguez with clean power shots and staggered him before the referee stepped in. Their light heavyweight bout was scheduled for 10 rounds on the Shuan Boxing card, though Morrell needed less than one in his first fight in over six months, getting his first win since edging Imam Khataev by split decision in July 2025.

The fight lasted less than a round, yet Morrell immediately fell into the same pattern. Rodriguez walked forward, and Morrell froze behind his shell guard rather than letting his hands go.

Rodriguez simply lacked the quality to make him pay for it. Once Morrell opened up, he clipped Rodriguez with a right hand to the back of the head that sent the 44-year-old backing toward a corner. Sensing Rodriguez was hurt, Morrell unloaded several hard punches until the referee stepped in and waved it off.

Rodriguez brought six straight defeats into Saturday’s fight, five of them inside the distance. The Dominican veteran had 24 knockouts on his record, but his recent form gave little reason to believe he could test Morrell or take him into the later rounds.

Morrell badly needed this victory after getting stopped in the tenth round by late replacement Zak Chelli in Manchester. That loss came on the heels of a unanimous decision defeat to David Benavidez in February 2025, plus a rough night five months later when Imam Khataev dropped him.

At 28, Morrell looks like he hasn’t improved or changed his fighting style at all. Whenever an opponent attacks, he still covers up behind a static shell and waits for them to stop throwing, the exact habit that caused him major trouble against Radivoje Kalajdzic, David Benavidez, and Imam Khataev before Chelli treated him like a heavy bag and stopped him.

Getting past an aging club fighter in Santo Domingo hides the flaw for one night, though against any durable light heavyweight who refuses to stop punching, Morrell will be right back in the same trouble.

Sports.title: Shakur Stevenson Hedges Ahead of Muratalla Purse Bid
Sports.content:
Shakur Stevenson is already building an escape route before the bids are even opened. Asked about his next move, the WBO light welterweight champion waved off talk of an Ashton Sylve bout as nonexistent and left a telling hedge on mandatory challenger Raymond Muratalla.

“To take over the sport of boxing and give the fans every fight they want to see, anybody can get it! If Muratalla has to be the first example, then so be it,” Stevenson told Mike Coppinger on X.

That word “if” does all the talking ahead of the November 30 purse bid, especially since Sylve’s promoter, Amer Abdallah, already went on record saying he hopes to get a deal done.

Stevenson enters the bid as a free agent after splitting with Zuffa Boxing. He has no house promoter with a reason to bid high to keep his belt and future fights in-house. If Matchroom or Top Rank sees this as a pay-per-view, it has to figure out how many buys the fight can generate against the cost of paying both men and putting on an undercard.

At a 75/25 split, a $2 million bid pays Shakur $1.5 million. A $2.5 million bid gets him $1.875 million. Would either figure get him to sign? Muratalla makes that a harder decision. Stevenson could pick off William Zepeda with clean counters as Zepeda came forward.

After enjoying huge purses at Turki Alalshikh’s table on Riyadh Season cards, Stevenson won’t be happy settling for table scraps in a standard U.S. purse bid. He could drop the WBO belt if the winning number comes in low, yet vacating it leaves him chasing deals with Devin Haney, Ryan Garcia, or Richardson Hitchins without a title to bring to the table.

None of those fighters have a reason to overpay a beltless free agent coming off a long layoff. If Stevenson turns down the November 30 bid, he will quickly learn how hard it is to demand Riyadh Season money when you no longer hold a title or a promotional deal.

Sports.title: Chase DeMoor Volunteers To  Step In And Face Deontay Wilder
Sports.content:
Since Jai Opetaia withdrew from his scheduled fight against former WBC world heavyweight champion Deontay Wilder, many well-known heavyweights have asked to fill the December 11th void.

Well-known heavyweights such as Derek Chisora, Jarrell Miller, Frazer Clarke, and Dillian Whyte are all willing to step in on short notice. In addition, a lesser-known heavyweight is also volunteering his services.

Chase DeMoor has thrown his name into the proverbial hat because he wants the opportunity to face Wilder. Some boxing fans are probably reading the name and thinking, who is Chase DeMoor?

A product of Eatonville, Washington, Chase DeMoor led the NCAA Division II in blocked kicks in 2018 as a defensive lineman for Central Washington University. In 2021, he appeared on the Netflix reality TV show Too Hot To Handle.

Soon after, DeMoor participated in an exhibition boxing match against Cory Wharton. In November 2022, DeMoor made his pro debut against Josh Brueckner, and He went viral for his comedic-looking punching technique.

After losing his first two professional fights, Chase DeMoor improved his technique and put together a winning streak. An already popular figure, DeMoor gained more notoriety when he defeated Andrew Tate in a Misfits Boxing bout in 2025.

Now, Chase DeMoor (7-2-1, 7 KOs) wants to reach new heights as he has volunteered to step in to face hard-hitting former WBC heavyweight world champion Deontay “The Bronze Bomber” Wilder (45-4-1, 43 KOs).

In his most recent ring appearance in August 2026, Chase DeMoor stopped Kevin Nagle in the fifth round and won the vacant WBC USA Silver heavyweight title. DeMoor has a solid fanbase, but skeptics also don’t view him as a legitimate boxer.

DeMoor is volunteering his services because he has a passion for boxing and he wants to silence the doubters. The odds of DeMoor getting the Wilder fight are slim, but if he gets it, does DeMoor have a path to victory?

The heavyweights who give Deontay Wilder trouble are 20 to 50 pounds bigger than him; they know how to neutralize his right hand, and they are very skilled. DeMoor has the size, but he doesn’t have the skills or the IQ to neutralize Wilder’s right hand.

Chase DeMoor wants a chance to prove he can be competitive against high-level competition. Hypothetically, if this match were made, DeMoor would bring in casual viewers, and Wilder could get an electrifying tune-up.

Sports.title: Granit Stein Stops Marius Antonietti in Five
Sports.content:
Granit Stein stopped Marius Antonietti 28 seconds into the fifth round to win the vacant IBO International super middleweight title Saturday at the Maritim Hotel in Ingolstadt, Germany. Referee Marco Morales halted the scheduled 10-round main event when Antonietti’s corner threw in the towel after a knockdown. Burim Syleyjmani’s Fides Sports Promotion presented the card, which aired on DAZN.

Stein (22-2-1, 12 KOs), fighting in his hometown, controlled the first three rounds before rocking Romania’s Antonietti (23-6, 19 KOs) with several lead right hands in the fourth. Another right to the chin sent Antonietti to the canvas early in the fifth.

Undercard Results

Heavyweight Luis “El Expreso” José Marín García (18-14-1, 13 KOs) stopped Albon Pervizaj (19-3, 14 KOs) for the second time, winning their scheduled 10-round rematch at 1:04 of the eighth. Pervizaj bloodied García’s nose in the third, and García lost a point for repeated holding in the fifth. Both fighters looked exhausted by the seventh. García dropped Pervizaj in the eighth, and Pervizaj got up but walked away and did not continue.

Kastriot “Super” Sopa (10-1, 5 KOs) knocked down southpaw Victor García (16-8, 13 KOs) three times in the third round, each time with a right hand. The scheduled 10-round bout ended at 1:28 of the third.

Chamseddine “Chamse” Lemjid (15-0, 11 KOs) stopped Michel “El Gallo de Oro” Marcano (43-17-1, 37 KOs) to win the German International title. Lemjid dropped Marcano with a right to the chin in the closing seconds of the fourth round. Marcano got up, but the fight was waved off at 2:59.

WBO European light heavyweight champion Nick Hannig (15-2-1, 8 KOs) outlanded Slavisa Simeunovic (42-97-1, 34 KOs) over the first two rounds of their scheduled six-round bout. Simeunovic retired with a nose injury, and the stoppage was recorded at 0:01 of the third.

Welterweight Rigon Demaku (1-0, 1 KO) dropped Dennis Neuer (2-43, 0 KOs) twice in the opening round to win his professional debut. The scheduled four-rounder ended at 2:27.

Super middleweight Bleron Gashi (1-0, 1 KO) also won his professional debut, dropping Alen Dozo (1-11, 0 KOs) twice in the first round. The scheduled four-round bout was stopped at 2:17.

Cruiserweight Mohammad “Montana” Gholami (1-0, 1 KO) won his professional debut after dropping Goran Panic (2-34, 1 KO) twice in the first round. A shoulder injury ended the scheduled four-round bout between rounds, with the stoppage recorded at 0:01 of the second.

Sports.title: Dillian Whyte Eyes Late Replacement Spot Against Deontay Wilder
Sports.content:
Dillian Whyte is trying to talk his way into a co-feature payday he hasn’t earned. The 38-year-old heavyweight has volunteered to replace Jai Opetaia against Deontay Wilder on the December 11 Tyson Fury vs. Anthony Joshua undercard at the Principality Stadium in Cardiff. Whyte hasn’t boxed since being stopped in the first round by 20-year-old prospect Moses Itauma in August 2025, yet he expects to walk straight into one of the biggest shows of the year.

“If they want it then they know where I am,” Whyte told Sky Sports News. “I’ve already waited 100 years for him, so if he wants it in December, then let’s go.”

Whyte Is Already In Camp

Whyte says he is already training for a December 18 return, seven days after the Cardiff show. Moving his date forward by a week is easy on paper. Taking on a heavy-handed former WBC champion on three weeks’ notice after a 15-month layoff is a different matter.

British fans remember Whyte sitting as Wilder’s WBC No. 1 contender for years without ever getting his shot. Fury ended up taking Wilder’s belt before Whyte finally got his title fight in 2022, where Fury stopped him in six rounds. That old history makes the matchup easy to sell on short notice, even if both men are well past their peak.

“He’s a big puncher, he’s wiry, and he’s fast and all that,” Whyte told Sky Sports News. “I just believe that I have the mentality and the style to beat him and cause him all sorts of problems.”

What Whyte Faces In Cardiff

Whyte’s plan has always been to crowd Wilder and take away the room he needs to unload his right hand. Getting inside against a live puncher requires sharp legs and timing. Whyte didn’t last three minutes against Itauma, and he hasn’t taken a punch in a real fight since.

Cardiff organizers have three weeks to fill the co-feature slot, and Whyte gives them a British name with a built-in backstory against Wilder. That doesn’t make him ready. Skipping a December 18 tune-up to jump straight in after 15 months out means his chin gets tested the first time Wilder’s right hand lands.

Sports.title: Andy Cruz Walks Into Another Judging Trap In Ufa Russia
Sports.content:
Andy Cruz is heading to Artur Subkhankulov’s hometown for his second shot at a world title. They meet for the vacant IBF lightweight belt on November 27 at the Wrestling Palace in Ufa, Russia. Cruz’s team agreed to the trip a day before a scheduled purse bid, according to promoter Peter Maniatis.

Cruz could have let the fight go to a bid to see who was willing to put up the money. That might have landed the bout on a card closer to home. It also could have sent him to Ufa anyway for less certainty. Taking the deal gets him a set date and a second title shot before the year is out.

The Judging Lesson From Las Vegas

Cruz (7-1, 4 KOs) knows how quickly a title fight can slip away on the scorecards. Officially, he lost a majority decision to Raymond Muratalla in January in Las Vegas before stopping Abraham Montoya in three rounds in July. Plenty of observers had Cruz winning that night. The official cards made it look like Muratalla had control of the fight, which didn’t match what happened in the ring. Muratalla had his moments when he trapped Cruz on the ropes, yet he was getting tagged coming forward and backing out all night.

Muratalla eventually moved up in weight and vacated the IBF strap, giving Cruz another crack at it. Still, Las Vegas was a reminder of how judges often reward forward pressure over clean countering.

Subkhankulov (12-0, 6 KOs) is 34 and faces a steep jump in class against an Olympic gold medalist who already beat him in the amateurs. He earned this spot by stopping Bakhodur Usmonov in the 12th round of an eliminator in April. Subkhankulov dropped Usmonov twice in the 10th, once in the 11th, and again in the 12th. Anyone assuming the Russian fades down the stretch hasn’t watched that tape.

The Trap In Ufa

Three amateur rounds against Subkhankulov won’t help Cruz much over 12 pro rounds in front of a Russian crowd. Cruz can make Subkhankulov miss and catch him on the way in, just as he did against Muratalla. He also leaves quiet stretches where the local fighter looks busy.

Subkhankulov already proved he can carry his offense into the championship rounds. If Cruz lets the hometown man march forward and work on the ropes in Ufa, he can’t expect the judges to bail him out with clean-punching credit.

Sports.title: Haney Still Wants Ryan Garcia Even If Mayweather Beats Him
Sports.content:
Devin Haney says he still wants a rematch with Ryan Garcia even if Floyd Mayweather beats him, a stance that makes Haney look desperate for a payday rather than a fighter chasing real competition.

If a 50-year-old Mayweather defeats Garcia, Garcia’s credibility at welterweight is finished. Chasing a fighter coming off a loss to a retired veteran does nothing for Haney’s standing in the sport, no matter how Haney tries to sell it.

Haney claimed he needs the second fight to settle unfinished business from their April 2024 bout.

“I think me and Ryan, we have to fight,” said Haney during Inside The Ring. “It’s just too much, you know. It’s too much question marks for that fight.”

Chasing Leftovers After a Mayweather Loss

Mario Lopez pressed Haney on whether the rematch still makes sense if Mayweather takes Garcia’s WBC welterweight title. Haney pointed out that Garcia has already lost since their first meeting and insisted fans would still want to see them run it back.

“I still want that fight just for me,” said Haney.

That excuse is empty. If Ryan loses to a 50-year-old man, nobody is demanding to see Haney fight him next, and claiming it is about personal pride does not hide the obvious financial motive. Haney knows Garcia still brings attention, even with his reputation damaged, and he wants that check regardless of how weak the matchup looks.

Haney did admit that a Mayweather win would change his immediate plans. If Mayweather ends up holding the WBC strap, Haney wants to fight him first for the undisputed championship.

“For me to be two-time undisputed and be fighting Floyd for undisputed, that would be crazy,” said Haney.

Before any of that can happen, both men have other business. Haney is scheduled to face Liam Paro, and Eddie Hearn has mentioned Jack Catterall as another option. Meanwhile, Mike Coppinger reported that Garcia and Teofimo Lopez have been working toward a deal for February 6, with talks for a Mayweather fight focused on a date after February.

Even if Ryan loses his belt and his credibility against Mayweather, Haney is still willing to line up for the leftovers. It is a bad look for a fighter who claims to care about legacy.

Ghana News.title: In Ghana, political principles fly economy until their owners enter government!
Ghana News.content:
By Jimmy Aglah

Once upon a time in the Republic of Uncommon Sense, there lived two political parties that agreed on almost everything except who should enjoy the privileges they so passionately condemned.

Whenever one party occupied the presidential palace, a presidential aircraft became an essential instrument of national security, diplomatic engagement and efficient governance. But the moment that party crossed into opposition, the same aircraft suddenly became an extravagant symbol of misplaced priorities, complete with luxurious seats, expensive fuel and a first-class ticket to political hypocrisy.

In this Republic, political principles behave like passengers at Kotoka International Airport. They arrive with impressive luggage, make solemn declarations at immigration and mysteriously disappear the moment their owners receive boarding passes to the presidential lounge.

The latest aircraft to enter this political drama is a Dassault Falcon 6X, acquired under a contract reported at approximately $60.68 million. It arrived in Accra on 16 November 2026, to a ceremonial water salute befitting a distinguished visitor.

The aircraft had barely settled on Ghanaian soil when the familiar engines of political controversy began roaring. The opposition demanded explanations. The government offered justifications. And the ordinary taxpayer, whose money helped finance the acquisition, watched the spectacle from a safe distance.

But the real entertainment began when the Republic opened its political archives.

In 2021, when the New Patriotic Party occupied the presidential palace, the National Democratic Congress was deeply concerned about presidential aviation expenditure. Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa and other NDC figures questioned the wisdom of acquiring another executive aircraft while ordinary Ghanaians struggled with economic hardship.

Their argument was straightforward. A country battling financial difficulties had no business shopping for expensive presidential aircraft while citizens were being asked to tighten their belts.

The NPP government, however, saw matters differently. Then Defence Minister Dominic Nitiwul defended consultations towards acquiring an additional aircraft, citing the demands of official travel and the limitations of existing arrangements.

Both sides spoke with the conviction of prophets who had personally received their instructions from heaven.

Then came the 2024 elections. The NDC returned to power, the NPP crossed into opposition, and something extraordinary happened at the Republic's political aviation school.

The parties exchanged boarding passes. Their arguments followed the luggage.

Suddenly, the NDC government discovered that presidential aviation was not necessarily an extravagant pastime for privileged politicians. It could also be a serious matter of national security, operational efficiency and responsible management of public resources.

The government explained that the ageing Falcon 900EX had developed technical problems, including reported fuel-tank corrosion, leaks, engine-related faults and increasingly expensive repairs. Government spokesperson Felix Kwakye Ofosu argued that maintaining the old aircraft had become financially burdensome and that replacing it was a practical necessity.

There may well be sound technical reasons for that decision. Aircraft maintenance is not a matter to be settled by political communicators armed with microphones and impressive vocabulary.

But the Republic had discovered something far more fascinating. The same political family that once questioned the wisdom of purchasing a presidential aircraft was now explaining why buying one was necessary.

In Ghana, it appears, the difference between a wasteful presidential jet and an essential national security asset is sometimes merely the distance between the Minority and Majority benches.

Just when Ghanaians thought they understood the argument, former Defence Minister Dominic Nitiwul introduced an interesting clarification.

Speaking on TV3's The KeyPoints on Saturday, 21 November, he explained that he was not opposed to acquiring a new presidential aircraft. Indeed, he supported the principle of purchasing one. His objection, he maintained, concerned the NDC's apparent change of position.

Apparently, Ghana's presidential jet has passed its aviation inspection, but the government's political memory is experiencing serious mechanical difficulties.

Then came another allegation capable of sending the Republic's political temperature soaring. Nitiwul claimed that an additional $9 million had been spent customising the new aircraft to President Mahama's specifications.

The allegation has not been independently established, and the government had not publicly responded to that specific claim when it was reported. It should therefore not be mistaken for a verified addition to the contract price.

Nevertheless, in the Republic of Uncommon Sense, the mere suggestion was sufficient to send political commentators scrambling for calculators.

One could almost imagine the presidential aircraft visiting an exclusive tailor before entering the palace. After all, even an expensive suit occasionally requires adjustments before its owner can wear it comfortably.

But $9 million for alleged alterations? At that price, the tailor should at least be capable of stitching Ghana's national budget back together.

Meanwhile, the debate over the old Falcon has developed into a remarkable medical examination. The government maintains that recurring technical problems and maintenance costs justified replacement. Nitiwul argues that the old Falcon remains serviceable following extensive repairs.

Both positions deserve careful examination. An aircraft may be technically airworthy while still being costly to maintain over time.

But in the Republic of Uncommon Sense, even the mechanical condition of an aeroplane has become a matter of political faith.

The Falcon 900EX has received so much public attention that one might mistake it for a distinguished patient at Korle Bu Teaching Hospital. Politicians are examining its fuel tanks, engines and maintenance records with the enthusiasm of specialist doctors conducting a national medical conference.

One side recommends retirement. The other insists the patient is fit to return to duty.

Then came the grand arrival of the Falcon 6X. According to the government, Ghana secured an earlier delivery opportunity after another customer agreed to transfer an existing aircraft order.

Water sprayed across its gleaming body as officials celebrated its arrival. It was a magnificent spectacle.

Somewhere in Ghana, a community still waiting for reliable running water might reasonably have wondered how an aeroplane could receive such an enthusiastic shower while its residents continued to struggle for a dependable supply from their taps.

Of course, the water salute was ceremonial. But satire requires no engineering qualification to recognise the irony.

As the controversy gathered momentum, private legal practitioner Martin Kpebu entered the discussion with a proposal that sounded almost revolutionary in Ghanaian politics. He suggested that the government should acknowledge that its earlier criticism of presidential aircraft expenditure had gone too far.

In other words, the government could simply admit that its position had changed.

But that would be asking for a political miracle. In Ghana, admitting that one's political opponents may have been right about something can be more difficult than securing a parking space at Kejetia during the Christmas rush.

An apology costs absolutely nothing, yet it remains one of the most expensive commodities in our political marketplace.

The controversy has also produced another intriguing argument. Some opposition voices believe Ghana should have acquired a larger aircraft.

Imagine that! While one group questions the cost of the new presidential jet, another argues that the aircraft should have been bigger.

Apparently, the debate is no longer simply about whether Ghana can afford to fly. It is also about whether the Republic's political disagreements can all fit comfortably inside the same cabin.

The government maintains that the Falcon 6X forms part of a broader programme to strengthen the Ghana Air Force's aviation capacity, including the acquisition of helicopters. Opposition figures have questioned the total expenditure and whether some of the helicopters should also be classified as VIP aircraft.

One side invokes national security. The other demands financial accountability. The taxpayer receives the bill.

And therein lies the enduring mystery of the Republic. Why does political concern for the suffering of ordinary Ghanaians become especially loud when a party occupies the opposition benches? Why does an aircraft acquire different moral qualities depending on who occupies its cabin?

Ghana certainly requires safe and reliable aircraft for legitimate state business. The safety of the President and other public officials must never be compromised merely to satisfy political sentiment. Equally, every major public expenditure deserves transparent justification, proper scrutiny and a clear demonstration of value for money.

These principles should survive changes of government.

Unfortunately, in the Republic of Uncommon Sense, political principles are frequently issued with return tickets. They travel into opposition as champions of financial discipline and return to government as ambassadors of executive necessity.

Perhaps the solution is to equip every future presidential aircraft with a special black box capable of recording the public statements of politicians before and after they enter government.

Whenever a new aircraft is proposed, the device could automatically replay yesterday's speeches.

Imagine the entertainment. A minister rises to defend the purchase of a presidential jet, only for the aircraft to announce, in his own recorded voice, that the country has more pressing priorities.

The embarrassed minister would probably demand an immediate parliamentary investigation into the activities of the black box.

Then an opposition spokesman rises to condemn the acquisition, and the same device reminds him of the passionate arguments his party once made in support of purchasing an executive aircraft.

At least the taxpayer would receive some entertainment in return for the investment.

And so, in the Republic of Uncommon Sense, the presidential jet has finally landed, but political consistency remains somewhere in transit.

Yesterday's critics have become today's defenders, while yesterday's defenders are now demanding explanations from yesterday's critics. The politicians have exchanged seats, but the ordinary Ghanaian continues to pay the bills.

Perhaps the next presidential aircraft should come with an additional safety feature: a political memory recorder.

For in this Republic, black boxes are recovered after aviation accidents, but the promises that crash after elections are rarely found.

Jimmy Aglah writes for the Republic of Uncommon Sense, where common sense is a scarce commodity, absurdity is government policy, and irony is the only thing that never goes on strike.

Ghana News.title: Tourism Ministry says Christmas events can boost Ghana’s December visitor appeal
Ghana News.content:
The Ministry of Tourism, Culture and Creative Arts says Christmas activities organised by churches and other institutions can strengthen Ghana’s appeal as a destination for visitors during the festive season.

Deputy Director for Finance and Administration at the Ministry, Charles Sedem Hottor, said such initiatives complement the government’s preparations for the influx of visitors expected in December.

He made the remarks at the Christmas celebration organised by The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints under the theme, “The Miracle of Christmas”.

Mr Hottor described the event as a valuable addition to efforts to position Ghana as a preferred destination in Africa.

He said the Ministry was working to improve the appearance of Accra and other major cities ahead of the festive season.

“The Ministry’s effort, through the Minister, is to ensure that the city of Accra and all our major cities are put in proper shape before they come,” he said.

He cited the installation of Christmas lights and other city beautification activities in Accra as part of the preparations to welcome visitors.

Mr Hottor also linked the activities to preparations for Ghana’s 70th Independence Day celebration next year, describing the Church’s initiative as complementary to the broader national effort.

“These programmes are all the preparatory programmes for such a very important independence celebration as well,” he said.

He added that the Ministry wanted Ghana to become “the destination that everybody prefers in the whole of Africa.”

Beyond its festive activities, the celebration provided an opportunity for the Church to share messages of love, peace and goodwill.

Elder Christian C. Chibundu said the theme reflected the message of Jesus Christ, which he described as one that transcends differences in people's backgrounds and circumstances.

“The Saviour Jesus Christ brings peace and goodwill to all of us. It goes beyond where we come from, our height, where we live. The message is the same,” he said.

He said the event was also an opportunity to bring people together through music, fellowship and messages centred on Christ.

“There's no other gift we can see more than what we are giving today, bringing people together, singing together, rejoicing together, hearing that peace and goodwill that our Saviour Jesus Christ brings,” he said.

Elder Chibundu encouraged people facing difficulties to seek comfort in Jesus Christ, noting that faith might not necessarily remove their challenges but could give them the strength to persevere.

“They might not be removed but the Saviour himself will help us to continue pushing even in the midst of troubles,” he said.

He urged Ghanaians to follow, love and trust Jesus Christ, saying that people could find peace, joy and happiness in Him.

Former Member of Parliament, Helen Adjoa Ntoso, also called on Ghanaians to make love for one another a priority during the Christmas season.

Quoting John 3:16, she said God's decision to give His only begotten Son demonstrated the depth of His love for humanity and should inspire people to show similar love to others.

“Christmas is all about love. Christmas is about the birth of Jesus Christ. So as the people of this country, our take-home is that we should love one another by the love of God,” she said.

Mrs Ntoso said the humble circumstances surrounding the birth of Jesus Christ also carried a lesson for Christians and society.

“I pray the birth of Christ was so simple, simple because He was born in a manger. This also means that when we humble ourselves, God will lift us up,” she said.

She urged Ghanaians to remain humble and ensure their actions bring glory to God.

The celebration formed part of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints' activities for the Christmas season, combining religious messages with a wider reflection on the contribution of festive events to Ghana's tourism ambitions.

Ghana News.title: One presidential jet, dishonest politicians, rented press and gullible citizens
Ghana News.content:
Kwaku Antwi-Boasiako

Imagine this: in today’s commercial aviation, airlines are required to submit advance passenger information to authorities at the destination airport. If the President of Ghana were to be flying on a commercial airline, the commercial airline that the President of Ghana is flying on to the United States, for example, would submit this information to the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA). What if this information gets into the hands of a terrorist organisation? Your guess is as good as mine, if your brains can help you to imagine the consequences.

There is a reason why most countries around the world would not subject the executive President or Prime Minister to commercial air travel. A few populist Presidents or Prime Ministers, once a while, would do it to make a name for themselves. But no national security agency would entertain the idea of having to make security arrangements to accommodate a presidential travel on a commercial flight. In actual fact, the cost of security arrangements alone would far outweigh the cost of making alternative private flight arrangements. Let me be clear: if a country hires a private jet to fly the President of the country, the overall cost will be lower than the cost of having the same President fly on a commercial flight, if the cost of security arrangements is factored into the cost-benefit analysis. What citizens don’t normally get to know is how expensive security arrangements have to be made in order to secure a President who decides to travel on a commercial flight.

During the presidency of President Nana Addo Dankwa Akufo-Addo, key figures of the current NDC government lambasted the former President for using private jets for foreign travels, claiming the presidential jet was serviceable and could have been used to save money and protect the public purse. The same persons criticised the attempt by the former government to acquire a new presidential jet for the presidency.

Since the NDC assumed office in January 2025, there has been a change of tone and a change of policy and approach. What has not changed is the lack of honesty, the hypocrisy and pure dishonesty of the political actors. President Mahama has been flying on the private jet of his wealthy brother, Ibrahim. The question is absolutely NOT whether Ghana is paying for the use of the private jet of Mr. Ibrahim Mahama. The question is, why would President Mahama not be asked to use the presidential jet that the NDC claimed was serviceable when they were in opposition? The short and simple answer is that, that presidential jet was not fit for President Akufo-Addo and is not fit for President John Mahama. The only difference now is that President Mahama, Okudzeto Ablakwa and all the NDC officials who said the old presidential jet was fit for President Akufo-Addo are dishonest and can’t tell the truth today.

Tell me, if President Mahama did not have a wealthy brother with a private jet, how was Ghana going to get our President to travel around the world, other than via private jets? Would a President Bawumia have been expected to fly on the unserviceable presidential jet, since he doesn’t have a wealthy brother with a private jet? Or would these same NDC officials have expected a President Bawumia to have used a commercial private jet and be constantly subjected to personal attacks by NDC officials?

What really shocks me is the fact that even veteran journalists are summersaulting to shield the NDC government from clear and legitimate accusations of hypocrisy and double-standards. What I have heard from key officials of the previous government is that they don’t oppose the acquisition of the new presidential jet in principle but criticise the hypocrisy and lack of honesty of government officials. How can any journalist, least of all a veteran journalist, not understand this logic and go on to ‘equalise’ by accusing both the NPP and the NDC of “inconsistency”? The media must hold our dishonest politicians accountable, without seeking to engage in ‘equalisation’ that provides comfort to these politicians who hurt the country by their conduct and actions, in government and in opposition.

As a person with an aviation background, I have remained quiet over the years when the needless political bickering has been raging. But the sad reality is that gullible citizens have been deceived and misled to support one political party or another. Citizens have been rendered zombies on social media, defending what they barely understand.

Ghana needed a new presidential jet under President Akufo-Addo. Ghana needs a new presidential jet under President Mahama. If you decided against having one under any of our two presidents, you have zero moral right to speak today - whether you are a politician, a journalist (even if you are a veteran) or a political footsoldier. You have absolutely no shame and you don’t deserve to continue to spew deception to gullible citizens!

Kwaku Antwi-Boasiako, Accra

November 19, 2026

Ghana News.title: COP 31: Africa expresses profound disappointment with outcomes, questions Presidency’s handling of negotiations
Ghana News.content:
The African Group of Negotiators (AGN) has expressed profound disappointment with the outcomes of key negotiations at the 31st UN Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Antalya, Türkiye, raising concerns over the substance of decisions and the process leading to their adoption.

Speaking at the closing plenary, Chair of the African Group of Negotiators, Nana Dr Antwi-Boasiako Amoah, said the outcomes on Action for Climate Empowerment (ACE) and long-term climate finance failed to adequately reflect Africa’s concerns and negotiating positions.

COP31 closing plenary travelled to midnight on Saturday as negotiators remained deadlocked over whether the final agreement should explicitly address the phase-out of fossil fuels and provide support for vulnerable countries to adapt to climate change.

In a statement on the outcome of negotiations on Action for Climate Empowerment, under agenda item 3(b) of COP31 and CMA 8, the African Group said it was disappointed with the proposed Action Plan for 2027–2031 under the Glasgow Work Programme.

The Group said the proposed text failed to address its substantive concerns and clearly communicated red lines, despite its constructive engagement throughout the negotiations.

It also questioned the role played by the COP31 Presidency, arguing that the process did not sufficiently reflect the responsibility of the Presidency to facilitate consensus among parties.

“The Presidency’s responsibility is to facilitate consensus among Parties, in accordance with the rules of procedure, not to determine or impose an outcome on their behalf,” the Group stated.

It insisted that the negotiations must remain party-driven, with the positions of all parties meaningfully considered in the development of final decisions.

The African Group also raised concerns over the handling of negotiations on long-term climate finance, arguing that the process did not provide sufficient opportunity for parties to engage with the proposed decision.

It said some paragraphs and provisions in the draft decision were not adequately negotiated, raising questions about the legitimacy and acceptability of the outcome.

The Group further questioned the evidence base used in the assessment of the US$100 billion climate finance goal, noting that the information and key findings relied on only two sources.

It said the consideration of Biennial Transparency Reports (BTRs) in the process was not given equal treatment by the Standing Committee on Finance (SCF).

The African negotiators called for the SCF to develop a more robust methodological approach that would promote greater understanding and trust among parties in the assessment of climate finance provision and mobilisation.

Despite its reservations, the Group indicated its willingness to adopt the decision on long-term finance if changes were made to paragraph three of the draft text to better reflect the realities of financial provision and mobilisation.

It proposed that the paragraph be revised to avoid relying on references to key messages that, in its view, did not accurately capture the financial realities under consideration.

The position reflects broader African concerns about the credibility of climate finance reporting, the fulfilment of commitments by developed countries and the need for decisions that translate into predictable support for developing countries.

For Africa, the effectiveness of the climate negotiations depends not only on the adoption of decisions but also on whether the process is inclusive, transparent and responsive to the concerns of parties, particularly those most vulnerable to climate change.

The African Group’s intervention at the closing plenary underscores its concern that consensus-building must not come at the expense of meaningful negotiations or the legitimate positions of developing countries.

Africa’s position at COP31 had remained firm: “Implementation needs means of implementation” bearing in mind the realities of climate impacts on the continent’s peoples.

Ghana News.title: Kisseman–Christian Village bridge to close for six months for reconstruction
Ghana News.content:
The bridge linking Kisseman and Christian Village in Accra will be closed to traffic for six months from the second week of December to allow for its reconstruction and elevation under the Greater Accra Resilient and Integrated Development (GARID) Project.

The works are intended to improve the flow of rainwater through the area and reduce the risk of flooding during periods of heavy rainfall.

GARID Project Communication Specialist, Philip Dunyo, said that alternative routes had been arranged to minimise the disruption to motorists who regularly use the busy road.

He said drivers travelling from Achimota would be directed onto a route near a mosque before reaching the bridge, while those coming from Dome would use an alternative route at BJ Junction.

“The road is a very busy road, and as a result, we have made alternative routes for motorists to use. As you can see the road is very busy. When you are coming from Achimota, there is a route leading to the mosque before you get here, so those coming from Achimota will use that side. Those coming from Dome, once they get to BJ junction, we have earmarked an alternative route there for them to use. We are blocking this road possibly by the second week of December,” he said.

Residents of Kisseman and Christian Village have experienced recurring floods over the years, with incidents resulting in loss of lives, destruction of property and the displacement of some households.

The existing bridge has been identified as one of the factors contributing to the flooding, as its narrow structure restricts the passage of water through the river during heavy downpours.

He spoke to Channel one TV.

The reconstruction and elevation are expected to address this bottleneck by improving water flow through the area.

Motorists who use the bridge have been advised to take note of the planned closure and use the designated alternative routes during the construction period.

Ghana News.title: Prof Nunoo calls for automated fisheries management to curb political interference
Ghana News.content:
Professor of Fisheries Science at the University of Ghana, Francis Kofi Ewusie Nunoo, has called for greater automation in Ghana’s fisheries sector, arguing that the use of modern technology could strengthen enforcement and reduce political interference in management decisions.

He said the sector’s reliance on human decisions had weakened the enforcement of regulations and made it difficult for scientists and regulators to implement measures based on research evidence.

Prof Nunoo believes technologies such as drones, satellites and artificial intelligence (AI) could improve monitoring, surveillance and enforcement, while reducing the scope for undue human influence.

He made the remarks at the launch of his memoir, Tides and Waves of Grace: A Memoir, in Accra.

He said fisheries management should be guided by scientific research, social considerations and economic data rather than political interests.

“We scientists believe that we do management with science. So, whatever the science tells us, whatever the social and economic situation tells us, we have to use that data to do the management,” he said.

Prof Nunoo noted that political interference had often undermined efforts by fisheries scientists to implement measures needed to protect fish stocks and ensure the long-term sustainability of the industry.

He urged scientists and young professionals to uphold professional integrity and resist pressures that could compromise their work.

He said researchers must have the courage to speak the truth and use evidence to influence national development, regardless of political or financial considerations.

Prof Nunoo, who has spent nearly 30 years in academia and more than three decades in the fisheries sector, said his 204-page memoir documents the experiences, challenges and lessons that have shaped his personal and professional journey.

Tides and Waves of Grace: A Memoir traces his childhood interest in fisheries, academic pursuits and professional experiences, including the difficulties he encountered on his path to becoming a professor.

He said growing up along the coast influenced his decision to pursue fisheries, despite his parents' initial preference for him to study medicine.

The memoir, he explained, is intended to encourage younger people to remain determined in the face of challenges and to recognise the value of perseverance and faith.

He also urged professionals and other individuals with meaningful experiences to document their stories to preserve knowledge and provide lessons for future generations.

Prof Nunoo expressed concern about what he described as a declining reading culture, particularly among young people, and encouraged Ghanaians to develop greater interest in reading and writing books.

He said the memoir was printed in Ghana as part of his commitment to supporting local industries and promoting locally produced goods and services.

The book launch also featured discussions on climate change, its causes and possible interventions to address its environmental and economic consequences.

Some senior lecturers and professors who participated in the discussions identified fossil fuel combustion, deforestation, industrial emissions, unsustainable agricultural practices and poor waste management as major contributors to climate change.

They said the destruction of forest cover, the use of fossil fuels for energy and transportation, and emissions from industrial activities increase greenhouse gas concentrations in the atmosphere, contributing to rising temperatures and changing weather patterns.

The academics called for greater investment in renewable energy sources, including solar and wind power, as well as afforestation and reforestation programmes, sustainable agriculture and improved waste management.

They also stressed the need for stronger environmental regulations, public education and climate-smart technologies to reduce emissions and improve communities' resilience to climate-related disasters.

The Head of the Department of Marine and Fisheries Sciences at the University of Ghana, Dr Benjamin Osei Botwe, described Prof Nunoo as an accomplished scholar, public servant, mentor and environmental advocate whose contributions extended beyond academia.

He said Prof Nunoo had served in several leadership positions, including Head of Department, Chief Director at the Ministry of Fisheries and Aquaculture Development, Director of Tertiary Education at the Ministry of Education and Chairman of the Fisheries Commission.

He had also served as Ghana's Commissioner to the International Whaling Commission and Acting Deputy Director-General of the Ghana Tertiary Education Commission.

Dr Botwe said Prof Nunoo's work in research, marine conservation, public administration and the mentoring of younger academics had contributed to Ghana's fisheries sector and higher education.

He added that the memoir would preserve institutional knowledge while offering younger generations lessons in leadership, perseverance, public service and professional commitment.

Ghana News.title: 22-year-old Ghanaian man dies after apartment fire in New York
Ghana News.content:
A 22-year-old Ghanaian man, identified as Zaidan Harun, has died after an apartment fire in the Soundview neighbourhood of the Bronx, New York.

The fire broke out shortly after 12:20 p.m. on Thursday, November 19, 2026, at a residential building on Metcalf Avenue, according to reports by 12 Westchester.

Fire officials said the blaze started on the second floor before spreading to the floor above.

Harun, who lived in an apartment on the second floor, was rescued by firefighters and taken to Jacobi Medical Center, where he later died.

Firefighters brought the blaze under control shortly after 1 p.m. Fire marshals have since begun investigations to establish what caused the fire.

Harun was a former student of Al-Azhariya Islamic Senior High School in Kumasi. He reportedly moved to the United States in 2021 to further his education.

Ghana News.title: Jospong subsidiary partners Turkish firm to test shrimp-shell-based farm products in Ghana
Ghana News.content:
The African Agribusiness Consortium Limited (AAC), a subsidiary of the Jospong Group of Companies, has signed a memorandum of understanding with Türkiye-based ChitoGlobal Biotechnology to test agricultural products derived from discarded shrimp and crab shells on farms in Ghana.

Signed on the sidelines of COP31 in Antalya, the agreement will begin with joint research and field trials to assess the products' suitability for Ghanaian farming conditions.

The products are based on chitosan, a substance derived from chitin, which is naturally found in the shells of crustaceans.

The trials will examine whether the products can protect seeds and plants, improve crop resilience during dry spells and strengthen plants' natural defences against fungal diseases.

They will also assess the products' effects on soil quality and crop yields, as well as their potential to provide farmers with a more affordable alternative to some conventional agricultural inputs.

After the signing, Jospong Group Chief Investment and Innovation Officer Noah Gyimah said the company would work with Ghana's environmental and standards authorities to ensure the products meet local regulatory requirements before introducing them for use on its farms.

“Our joint efforts will transition this technology from research and development to practical application. We will commence with collaborative research and field trials in Ghana, followed by technology transfer and full-scale commercial production,” he said.

Mr Gyimah said the pilot would also help AAC assess the commercial viability of the products, identify potential buyers and determine whether Ghana has sufficient raw materials to support local production.

He said the consortium intends to make the products available to smallholder farmers if the trials establish their suitability. AAC also plans to assess their potential use in growing its own crops and vegetables on a commercial scale for the Ghanaian market.

The agreement followed a visit by a four-member AAC delegation, led by the consortium's Coordinator, Dr Emmanuel Volsuuri, to ChitoGlobal's facility in Antalya.

Dr Volsuuri said he arranged the visit after meeting the company at its COP31 pavilion, where further discussions led to the opportunity to examine its operations and technology first-hand.

The delegation toured the facility to learn about the composition of the products and the operations of the company's laboratories.

Dr Volsuuri said the visit helped AAC assess the products' potential to support crop disease management and improve soil health in Ghana.

He also cited concerns about the widespread use of conventional chemical treatments in agriculture and the need to explore alternatives that could reduce farmers' reliance on them.

AAC Chief Executive, Dr Adelaide Araba Siaw Agyepong, leads the consortium, which grows rice, maize, vegetables and soybeans commercially in Ghana. The company also supports farmers with access to mechanisation services, financing and markets.

ChitoGlobal Biotechnology develops biopolymer products for agricultural and medical applications.

ChitoGlobal Sales and Technical Support Manager, Dana Abourahma, said the partnership would combine the expertise of both organisations.

“This collaboration brings together extensive local knowledge with cutting-edge scientific capabilities,” she said.

The proposed research and field trials will determine whether the chitosan-based products can be adapted for Ghanaian farms and whether local production could be commercially viable.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”
