World.title: Gukesh vs Sindarov: The youngest World Chess Championship in history
World.content:
India’s Gukesh defends his title against Uzbekistan’s Sindarov in up to 14 games in Geneva from November 22.

Share Gukesh vs Sindarov: The youngest World Chess Championship in history on social media

India’s Gukesh Dommaraju will defend his world chess title against Uzbekistan’s Javokhir Sindarov in Geneva, Switzerland, from November 22 to December 12.

The match, at the Fondation Martin Bodmer in Cologny on the outskirts of Geneva, will be played over a maximum of 14 classical games. The first player to reach 7½ points will be crowned world champion.

Both players will be 20 when the first game begins on November 24, making it the youngest world championship match in history.

The road to the crown

The official programme opens with a media day and opening ceremony on November 22. The first game is on November 24, and the 14th and final classical game is scheduled for December 11.

A win earns one point, a draw half a point and a loss none. Players have 120 minutes for their first 40 moves, then 30 minutes for the rest of the game, with 30 seconds added per move from move 41. Draw offers are not allowed before move 40.

If the score is tied at 7–7 after 14 games, the title will be decided on December 12 through tiebreaks at faster time controls, starting with four rapid games.

The players will share a $2.5m prize fund. Each earns $200,000 per game won, and the rest is split equally.

One will leave Geneva with the crown.

The contenders: India vs Uzbekistan

Gukesh made history in December 2024, when he defeated China’s Ding Liren in Singapore to become the youngest undisputed world champion, aged 18. Geneva will be his first title defence.

Sindarov won the 2025 FIDE World Cup, then the 2026 Candidates Tournament in Cyprus, where he went unbeaten and scored 10 points from 14 games. Victory in Geneva would make him the first undisputed world champion from Uzbekistan. His compatriot Rustam Kasimdzhanov won FIDE’s version of the title in 2004, when the crown was split.



Sindarov arrives with the stronger record against his opponent. He leads their classical head-to-head 2–0 with one draw, and Gukesh has never beaten him in a classical game.

World champions through history

Since Wilhelm Steinitz became the first recognised world chess champion in 1886, 21 players have held the title over 140 years.

The championship’s history reflects the changing balance of power in chess. European masters dominated its early decades, with Germany’s Emanuel Lasker holding the title for a record 27 years, from 1894 to 1921.

After the second world war, Soviet players took over. From 1948 until 1972, every world champion came from the Soviet Union, beginning with Mikhail Botvinnik.

That run ended in 1972, when American Bobby Fischer defeated Boris Spassky in a match that became a defining moment of the Cold War. The title returned to Soviet hands in 1975, starting the era of Anatoly Karpov and Garry Kasparov, whose rivalry shaped chess for the next two decades.

In 1993, Kasparov broke away from FIDE, chess’s governing body, to form the Professional Chess Association. Two rival world titles existed until they were reunified in 2006. Since then, the crown has passed to India’s Viswanathan Anand, Norway’s Magnus Carlsen, China’s Ding Liren and, in 2024, Gukesh Dommaraju.

The Soviet Union and Russia have produced nine of the 22 champions. India has produced two, Anand and Gukesh, and 11 other countries have each produced one.

In Geneva, either Gukesh will join the small group of players who have defended the title, or Sindarov will add Uzbekistan’s name to the list of undisputed champions.

World.title: Max Verstappen wins F1 Las Vegas Grand Prix for third time in four years
World.content:
Red Bull’s Verstappen dug deep to fend off Antonelli and Russell in a race that saw a jaw-dropping 35 lead changes.

Share ‘That was crazy’: Verstappen wins Las Vegas GP for third time in four years on social media

Red Bull’s Max Verstappen won a crazy, slipstreaming Las Vegas Grand Prix for the third time in four years, while Mercedes rival George Russell hit the barriers late on and finished ⁠ninth.

In a race featuring 35 lead changes over 50 laps, with drivers running nose-to-tail under the floodlights and track advantage swinging back and forth like a yo-yo, McLaren’s 2025 champion Lando Norris and teammate Oscar Piastri finished second and third behind the pole-sitter on Saturday.

Ferrari drivers Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc collided again in a ‌race in which both collected 10-second penalties for separate incidents and finished seventh and 10th, respectively.

“That was crazy. Really, really surreal and something I’ve never seen before in Formula One myself,” said Verstappen, who beat Norris by 0.639 seconds.

“It was a crazy amount of fighting, and the slipstream was so big that it was just impossible to drive off and it was just crazy how many people were just following.”

Mercedes have already won both titles, with 20-year-old Italian ⁠Kimi Antonelli this month becoming the youngest ever Formula One world champion, ⁠while Verstappen and Russell started the weekend scrapping to end the season as overall runner-up.

Verstappen’s fourth win in six races sent him 37 points clear of Ferrari’s Hamilton, with Russell, who started on the front row, dropping to fourth overall and ⁠level with Norris.



Antonelli was fourth, with Alpine’s Pierre Gasly fifth and teammate Franco Colapinto sixth. Carlos Sainz was eighth for Williams in the Spaniard’s ⁠250th race.

“I think that must have been the most chaotic ⁠race ever in the history of Formula One,” said Norris.

“I didn’t know what was happening half the time. I didn’t know if I was going to have the best race and have a chance to win or end up last. It had ‌everything this race.”

Piastri, who started 17th, could only agree.

“They say Las Vegas is the entertainment capital of the world and that was pretty entertaining to be a part of,” said the Australian.

“It was ‌pretty ‌random. You would pass someone on one straight super easy, then the next straight you would struggle and then with someone else it would be different strengths and weaknesses.”

World.title: Indonesia factory fire kills three, 36 missing
World.content:
Rescue crews continue looking for missing workers in destroyed three-story facility near Jakarta.

A fire at a sweets factory in Indonesia has killed at least three people and 36 others are missing.

At least 15 people were rescued from the Fonusa Agung Mulia factory in Banten province, which borders the capital Jakarta, including four taken to hospital, said the National Search and Rescue Agency in a statement on Sunday.

“The fire is still burning in several locations and firefighting teams are continuing extinguishing and cooling operations,” rescue official Rizky Dwianto told The Associated Press news agency.

Firefighters from Serang district and Banten province were battling flames in several parts of the facility more than 12 hours after the fire began, Dwianto said.

Rescue workers along with fire department personnel and the Indonesian Red Cross searched different sections of the factory, focusing on areas where victims might be trapped, he added.

Around 60 people were in the factory when the fire started. Banten province governor Andra Soni told reporters.

The factory produces milk-based snacks and sweets, known as Milkita.

Photos and videos circulating online captured black flames and thick smoke coming from the three-storey building. Footage from inside appeared to show the fire caused extensive damage, with equipment blackened and destroyed.

Local broadcasters and social media accounts shared footage of families gathering outside the factory.

The disaster agency said the cause of the fire was under investigation.

Indonesia has suffered a number of deadly fires in recent years. A fire in an office building in Jakarta killed at least 22 people last December. An explosion at an Indonesian nickel-processing plant killed at least 13 people in 2023.

World.title: Wembanyama scores 50 points, bags 19 rebounds in Spurs’ 14th win of season
World.content:
Wembanyama became only the third NBA player since the 1973-74 season with at least 50 points, 15 rebounds, four steals and five blocks in a game.

Victor Wembanyama has scored 50 points and grabbed 19 rebounds to power San Antonio to a 114-91 victory over New Orleans as the Spurs matched the National Basketball Association’s best record at 14-3.

The 22-year-old, 7-foot-4-inch (2.24m) Frenchman made 20 of 29 shots from the floor, 5 of 11 from three-point range, and added five blocked shots, four steals and an assist in 32 minutes on the court on Saturday.

San Antonio won for the 14th time in 15 games, and Wembanyama became only the third NBA player since the 1973-74 season with at least 50 points, 15 rebounds, four steals and five blocks in a game.

“It is very special, but unlike many of my peers, I’m not very good at stat-padding,” Wembanyama said.

Wembanyama was just shy of his career-high score of 52 points, set in a victory over Dallas on November 4.

“Wemby” scored 17 points in the first quarter as the Spurs jumped to a 32-29 lead over the visiting Pelicans and had 32 points and 13 rebounds at half-time with San Antonio ahead 61-45.

“I thought he started the game off aggressive, and I thought he was trying to play with a lot of force offensively, specifically, just in terms of taking up real estate, trying to get to the rim,” Spurs coach Mitch Johnson said.

“I thought he did a really good job of playing with force.”

Johnson did not relish taking Wemby to the bench but wanted to avoid any chance of an injury in a game well in hand.



“Was it tough to pull him out after he got 50? No, I was just hoping he got to 50 when he did,” Johnson said. “That would have been hard to take him out that close to 50.”

The Spurs levelled with the Los Angeles Lakers and Philadelphia 76ers for the best record in the league, the Sixers having matched the mark earlier in a 132-129 victory over Milwaukee.

Joel Embiid led the Philadelphia 76ers to a fifth consecutive victory despite Tyler Herro’s career-high 50 points for the Bucks.

Embiid delivered 26 points, a season-high 17 rebounds and nine assists for the host Sixers as they dropped the league-worst Bucks to 1-16, stretching Milwaukee’s losing skid to 13 games.

Herro added 11 rebounds and seven assists, but he missed a chance to send the game into overtime.

He sank a three-point shot at the finish, but officials ruled after consulting video replay that the shot left his hand after the final buzzer.

Four-time NBA Most Valuable Player LeBron James scored 21 points, grabbed six rebounds, recorded three steals and provided six assists for the 76ers.

“For us to be a super complete team, I think the power of the pass is very infectious,” James said. “It’s key for our other guys as well to make sure they feel in a rhythm and they feel confident.”

Anfernee Simons added 18 points off the Philadelphia bench while Tyrese Maxey added 17 and VJ Edgecombe scored 16 as the 76ers withstood a late Bucks rally.

“Soon we’re going to have to put together a 48-minute game,” Maxey said.

Bridges buzzer winner

At Madison Square Garden, Mikal Bridges sank a three-pointer at the final buzzer to give the reigning champions New York Knicks a 97-96 victory over Portland.

The Trail Blazers rallied from a 26-point deficit to seize a 96-94 lead on two free throws by Deni Avdija with 3.2 seconds remaining.

The Knicks tried to inbound the ball to star Jalen Brunson for the last shot but went to Bridges when Brunson was covered.

“They played harder than us in that second half,” Bridges said. “That’s on us, but we just finished the game. It goes 48 minutes, and we just kept persevering through the time and ended up winning.”

The Knicks, without injured starters OG Anunoby and Karl-Anthony Towns, improved to 10-6 with their fourth consecutive victory while Portland fell to 10-6.

Brunson led New York with 30 points, 19 of them in the first quarter, while Landry Shamet added 20 and Bridges had 12 points.

In other games, Jaden McDaniels scored 25 points to lead Minnesota’s 104-95 home win over Memphis, while Kyrie Irving had 25 points and Cooper Flagg added 22 in a 110-100 Dallas home win over the Los Angeles Clippers.

World.title: Why Somalia’s president turned against his former ally, the UAE
World.content:
Behind Somalia’s break with the UAE lies a domestic power struggle with regional leaders close to Abu Dhabi.

Share Why Somalia’s president turned against his former ally, the UAE on social media

Three years ago, at a town hall meeting in Mogadishu, Somali President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud defended one of his country’s most controversial foreign partnerships.

The United Arab Emirates, he declared, was “one of the greatest pillars” of Somalia’s war against the al-Qaeda-linked armed group al-Shabab. He praised Abu Dhabi’s support for the country’s armed forces despite longstanding concerns about its political influence.

Having returned to power in 2022, Mohamud sought to repair relations with the Gulf state after a period of strained ties under his predecessor, while reassuring a sceptical Somali public that the UAE’s involvement was a boon rather than a hindrance.

This year, that relationship unravelled spectacularly.

On November 19, Somalia ordered the Emirati ambassador to leave the country and recalled its own envoy from Abu Dhabi, marking the sharpest rupture yet in a relationship that had shifted from close security cooperation and deep commercial ties to open hostility.

The UAE said it had already withdrawn its diplomatic staff from Mogadishu in January.

The decision came 10 months after Somalia annulled several commercial, defence and security agreements with the UAE, accusing its former ally of undermining its sovereignty.

In a sharp public rebuke two days before the expulsion order, Mohamud accused the UAE of heightening political divisions, financing rival regional administrations and supporting armed actors operating beyond the federal government’s control.

“A brother does not burn your house. A brother does not buy your property without your knowledge. A brother does not divide your family,” he said.

“After years of diplomatic engagement, the Federal Government assesses that UAE policies threaten Somalia’s national security,” Awes Hagi Yusuf Ahmed, Somalia’s national security adviser (NSA), said in a post on X.



The UAE hit back, accusing Mogadishu of allowing its internal political disputes to strain bilateral ties, in an apparent reference to the president’s contentious relations with some of Somalia’s semi-autonomous regional administrations, which maintain close ties with Abu Dhabi.

Anwar Gargash, a senior Emirati official, said the UAE’s ties with Somalia would “remain deeper and stronger” despite the president’s criticism.

The diplomatic rupture comes amid an escalating domestic power struggle between Mohamud and regional leaders resisting his efforts to reassert federal authority, several of whom have cultivated close ties with Abu Dhabi.

It also marks a striking reversal for a president during whose first term the UAE significantly expanded its foothold in Somalia and who later emerged as one of Abu Dhabi’s strongest defenders.

Somalia divided

Somalia’s efforts to rebuild national institutions since the establishment of a permanent federal government in 2012 have unfolded alongside the consolidation of regional administrations that retain considerable autonomy and political power.

Abu Dhabi’s ties with Mogadishu deepened during Mohamud’s first presidency, from 2012 to 2017.

The UAE reopened its embassy in the capital in 2014, and Mohamud inaugurated a UAE-funded military training centre for Somali forces the following year.

At the same time, the Gulf state cultivated commercial, security and diplomatic ties with regional administrations, including Puntland and Jubbaland, as well as Somaliland, which declared independence from Somalia in 1991.

The UAE is also one of Somalia’s most important trading partners, serving as an important source of imports and a hub for Somali businesses trading in international markets.

But its influence extends well beyond trade, with big investments in infrastructure and security concentrated in Somaliland, Puntland and Jubbaland.

Among the most visible of these investments is Berbera port in Somaliland, where Dubai’s state-owned port operator DP World has invested heavily in expanding the facility and developing a trade corridor connecting it to Ethiopia and the wider region.

Through its subsidiary P&O Ports, the company also operates Bosaso port in Puntland, with both ports providing crucial sources of revenue for their respective administrations.

Somaliland’s Foreign Minister Abdirahman Dahir Adam said the UAE treated it as an independent state, making it an attractive partner, while Emirati investments had created jobs and improved regional connectivity.



“The UAE saw Somaliland’s potential early and backed that view with real investment,” Adam told Al Jazeera.

“The impact on our economy has been significant. DP World’s development of Berbera Port and the Berbera Corridor has turned Berbera into a serious regional gateway,” he added.

Their strategic location along the Gulf of Aden also gives Somaliland and Puntland considerable leverage, making them attractive partners for foreign powers seeking a foothold along one of the world’s busiest shipping routes.

The UAE has developed military facilities near both ports, while in Puntland it helped establish and fund the Puntland Maritime Police Force (PMPF), initially an antipiracy unit that has since become an important counterterrorism force.

More recently, it has supported Puntland’s campaign against ISIL (ISIS) in Somalia with drone attacks and carried out a strike this year against al-Shabab in support of Puntland’s forces, a security official in the region told Al Jazeera.

Abu Dhabi maintains similar commercial and security ties with Jubbaland, which borders Kenya, although the extent of its involvement there is less publicly documented.

A senior Puntland official speaking anonymously told Al Jazeera the UAE’s interventions had helped regional states consolidate their authority, with no equivalent assistance coming from the federal government. “It is obvious why on that level the UAE is a more important partner,” the official said.

Aweis Ahmed, a Somalia expert at Chatham House, told Al Jazeera that while Emirati support had brought tangible benefits to Somalia’s regional states, it had also strengthened their position against the federal government, undermining Mogadishu’s efforts to assert its authority.

“They view these things differently. On the one hand, it helps the peripheries, whilst it undermines the centre,” Ahmed said.

Different priorities and interests

That partnership suffered a setback after Mohamud left office in 2017, when his successor, Mohamed Abdullahi, also known as Farmaajo, refused to take sides in a diplomatic dispute between the UAE and Saudi Arabia on one side and Qatar on the other.

Relations improved after Mohamud returned to power in 2022, but tensions persisted over Abu Dhabi’s increasingly independent dealings with regional administrations, often bypassing the federal government entirely.

Abdinor Dahir, director of the Somalia-based Adkaysi Institute for Research, Peace and Inclusive Resilience, told Al Jazeera that the UAE’s relationships with regional states had deepened disagreements over who had the authority to conclude agreements with foreign partners.

“Overall, the regional states’ external relationship with the UAE and the resulting disputes weaken federal authority, undermine counterterrorism cooperation, and risk turning foreign policy into a permanent source of internal conflict,” Dahir said.

The dispute came to a head in January, when Mogadishu annulled its agreements with Abu Dhabi, accusing the UAE of secretly transporting an Emirati-backed Yemeni separatist leader through Somaliland without authorisation.

Somaliland, Puntland and Jubbaland rejected the announcement, insisting their agreements with Abu Dhabi, particularly over ports, would remain in force.



NSA Yusuf Ahmed accused the regional administrations of compromising national security through their independent dealings with Abu Dhabi.

“Port agreements for Berbera, Bosaso and Kismayo, concluded outside federal authority, take strategic infrastructure out of national control,” he said in a post on X. “That is a security question, not a political one.”

President’s contentious agenda

But the dispute with the UAE has also become entangled with a wider struggle over political power within Somalia, as Mohamud’s efforts to strengthen the central government through constitutional and electoral changes have met resistance from regional leaders.

Puntland and Jubbaland, both federal member states, have opposed changes they say would weaken their autonomy, while functionally independent Somaliland has long rejected Mogadishu’s authority.

Somali officials have also accused the UAE of backing the deposed leader of Southwest State, Abdiaziz Hassan Laftagareen, who has fought to retake several towns around the regional capital, Baidoa, in recent months.

Laftagareen told Al Jazeera that he would remove Mohamud’s ally, who took power following a contested election in Baidoa.

Aweis Ahmed, the Chatham House expert, told Al Jazeera the UAE’s support for Mohamud’s domestic opponents had helped them thwart his efforts to push through contentious constitutional and electoral changes.

“This issue with the UAE is more about the local dynamics than some big question about sovereignty for Hassan Sheikh,” he said.

“A direct line to Abu Dhabi gives these sub-national leaders more room to pursue their own priorities when relations with Mogadishu are difficult,” Dahir said.

Importing UAE’s rivalries

However, Aweis Ahmed warned that the UAE’s involvement, along with that of other powers from the Middle East, was deepening domestic divisions while drawing Somali actors into wider regional disputes.

“They have made important contributions, but overall their involvement is exacerbating Somalia’s internal and external issues,” he said.

The federal government has aligned itself closely with Turkiye, Qatar and Egypt, while some regional administrations have cultivated ties with the UAE and Ethiopia, and Somaliland has drawn closer to Israel.

“These countries have their own issues, and they’re overlapping with Somalia’s internal rivalries,” Aweis Ahmed said.

At home, Mogadishu has increasingly deployed its growing military strength, including Turkish-trained troops, against UAE-aligned rivals opposed to Mohamud’s constitutional and electoral agenda.

Turkish-trained federal forces helped remove Southwest State leader Abdiaziz Hassan Laftagareen from power, while a similar attempt to dislodge Jubbaland’s Ahmed Mohamed Islam, also known as Madobe, following his disputed re-election in 2024 failed.

In Puntland, tensions with Mogadishu prompted regional forces to seize several federal military bases and expel federal institutions.

Beyond Somalia, Sudan has complained to Mogadishu about the UAE’s alleged use of facilities in the port cities of Bosaso and Berbera to supply the Rapid Support Forces (RSF), the paramilitary group fighting the Sudanese army.

A Somali source told Al Jazeera that Sudan’s intelligence chief raised the issue during a visit to Mogadishu in 2025, pressing Somali officials to at least publicly condemn the alleged supply operations if they were unable to stop them.

In early November, Yassir al-Atta, the Sudanese army chief of staff, went further, alleging that fighters from northern Somalia had taken part in the conflict alongside the RSF.



The passage of Abu Dhabi-backed Yemeni separatist leader Aidarous al-Zubaidi through Somali territory has similarly drawn Mogadishu into tensions between the UAE and Saudi Arabia over Yemen.

World.title: The European revolt may be coming to the UK
World.content:
There is enough justified anger among the British youth to spark a wave of mass protests.

The protests engulfing Europe represent a new level of popular mobilisation quite unlike any historical precedent. In France, Spain, Italy, Serbia, Germany and other countries across the continent, mass movements are challenging austerity and government failures.

On Friday, the United Kingdom saw what is likely to be the beginning of its own wave of youth-driven demonstrations. Thousands of students walked out of hundreds of schools and universities around the country, from Aberdeen to Brighton, Swansea to Nottingham, making it one of the largest student mobilisations since the tripling of tuition fees back in 2010.

The protests were called by organisations involved in the International Conference Against War, a pan-European initiative aimed at coordinating the movements against militarism. The University and College Union (UCU) was the first union to back the initiative with a National Day of Action, urging members across the university sector to hold protests and rallies alongside students.

That major unions followed UCU in supporting the walkouts, including Unison, Unite, the National Education Union (NEU), GMB and the Educational Institute of Scotland (EIS), speaks to the potential of union support.

In London, demonstrations from universities and colleges converged on Trafalgar Square to chants of “fight for our future, not their wars” before moving to Downing Street to hear student activists and trade union leaders berate the government for prioritising defence spending over education and public services.



There is indeed much for British youth to be angry about. Like in the rest of Europe, young people in the UK are facing a convergence of high inflation, unemployment, economic stagnation, the gutting of public services and deteriorating living standards, including a housing crisis stoked by property speculation. Combined with police brutality over solidarity with Palestine, unrestrained racism and sexism and expectations of environmental and climate catastrophe, mass protest is rather predictable.

According to government estimates, close to one million people between 16 and 24 years of age are “Neets” – not in education, employment or training; this is more than 13 percent of that age group. Young people make up more than 40 percent of the unemployed in the country. Apart from a tough job market, there is also a rampant mental health epidemic and an education system that few can afford.

Here we have the makings of a social and economic crisis waiting to happen, and yet the government response has been to seek more austerity.

It is a wonder that Alan Milburn, former Labour minister responsible for introducing private finance into the NHS in the late 1990s, was commissioned to write the controversial report on Neets for the government. Why bother to provide welfare when the private sector can solve the crisis? Unsurprisingly, Milburn’s recommendations are market-focused and include cutting certain benefits for youth, including for those with disabilities.

This comes on top of years of austerity in the higher education sector. Job cuts and course closures have become standard responses from university managements dealing with the lack of direct government funding. Many describe it as academic vandalism. What funding cuts have produced is extreme dysfunction, chaos and mismanagement: Faustian bargains with banks, management consultants and corporate outsourcing that serve efficiency and profit over quality provision.

While education and civilian job openings are dwindling, British youth are offered more opportunities in the army, which is now promoting a fully paid 18-month “foundation scheme”.

Military training, bolstered by a public campaign around “warfighting readiness” as part of last year’s Strategic Defence Review, was the brainchild of ministers under Keir Starmer, one of the most unpopular prime ministers in British history. True to form, Starmer pushed through an additional 15 billion pounds ($19.6bn) towards defence immediately before leaving office, for a total of 298 billion pounds ($389.8bn) over four years.



This is a worrying trend across Europe: While there are diminishing funds for public services, military spending is shooting up. This fact has not been lost on young people.

But what is driving this rearmament frenzy is that the European project is increasingly being bound together by NATO, along with Trump’s insistence that the EU should pay its fair share in maintaining the alliance. Support for Ukraine against Russia is at the centre of that project.

If youth mobilisation in the UK reaches the same level as in France, for example, this could be the first major test of Andy Burnham’s government. The French revolt was started over education – not the first strikes in French history over education, considering the origins of the 1968 uprisings. Still, France spends 5.1 percent of GDP on education.

The UK spends 4.1 percent of GDP on education, and even part of this budget has been diverted to defence, with less funding for schools in the coming years.

The UK has had seven prime ministers in the past decade, each one unable to deliver desperately needed income and wealth redistribution. A decade of Tory prime ministers allowed the rich to get very rich. Starmer continued the tradition. He was hammered by Reform and the Greens in the last local elections, firstly because he was unable to come through on the social democratic promises that many were hoping a Labour government would provide.

But second, he failed to recognise the genuine anger over British complicity in the Palestinian genocide, and then responded to mass protest with punitive legislation. Notwithstanding the Burnham bounce, the sitting prime minister has stuck to the same tack as his predecessor. His new foreign secretary has admitted that the government got it wrong over Palestine, but this needs to be backed up by action.

As Burnham faces growing protest, a heavy-handed approach will not work. Nor will more neoliberal reforms. A half-century of privatisation, deregulation and cuts to social welfare has produced the current malaise, and the crisis is only deepening.

The youth and the rest of European society are demanding change – real, lasting change in the political and economic spheres.

The revolutions that convulsed Europe in 1848 were a response to severe economic crisis, unemployment and bad harvests that caused famine. The European protests today unfold under comparable conditions. The task of those who want to see change is an internationalism that can generalise grievances, coordinate the movements and deliver concrete solidarity against austerity and war.

The views expressed in this article are the author’s own and do not necessarily reflect Al Jazeera’s editorial stance.

World.title: Kansas City Current defeat Washington Spirit 2-1 to lift first NWSL title
World.content:
Trinity Rodman left in tears after scoring Spirit’s only goal as DiBernardo and Debinha give Current closely-fought win.

Share Kansas City win maiden NWSL crown as Washington lose third final in a row on social media

Kansas City Current have defeated the Washington Spirit in a closely-contested final to be crowned the NWSL champions for the first time as Trinity Rodman’s bid to avoid a third consecutive final defeat ended in bitter disappointment in Washington, DC.

Vanessa DiBernardo curled in a goal direct from a corner and Brazilian international Debinha added a second in stoppage time to set up Kansas City’s 2-1 victory at Audi Field on Saturday.

Rodman headed in a 98th-minute goal to pull one back for Spirit, but Kansas City held on to win.

“We knew it was going to be a battle; we felt good coming out of the first half,” said DiBernardo, who was named the championship MVP months after returning to professional football following the birth of her daughter.

“We just had to be patient and finish off the game.”

It was another crushing loss for United States star Rodman and her Spirit teammates, who were also beaten in the final in 2025 and 2024.

Rodman, who was in tears at the final whistle, was knocked out of her stride earlier in the game.

The 24-year-old was on the receiving end of a rugged aerial challenge from Kansas City’s Laney Rouse after just five minutes and needed treatment on the sidelines.

Rodman returned to the field grimacing in pain and clutching her shoulder but completed the game.

The opening goal came early in the second half, with DiBernardo’s in-swinging corner looping into the net after Kansas City’s Kayla Sharples cleverly blocked Washington goalkeeper Sandy MacIver.



Deep in stoppage time, Debinha added Current’s second after a sweeping counterattack, before Rodman’s header was too little, too late.

The victory was Kansas City’s first NWSL title after losing in the championship game to the Portland Thorns in 2022.

World.title: New draft deal aims to avert collapse of talks at COP31 climate summit
World.content:
Efforts to avert the collapse of talks at the UN COP31 summit have faced further delays on the second day of overtime, as countries struggle to reach a new global climate deal.

A new draft agreement was published in the early hours of Sunday which the Turkey and Australia co-hosts hoped would bridge the divide between nations.

Although it still includes no specific reference to "transitioning away from fossil fuels" - an omission in the previous draft that sparked threats of walkouts - it does acknowledge a previous commitment made by countries to do just that three years ago.

Countries were expected to reconvene to decide whether to approve a new deal, but that meeting was delayed on Sunday morning.

The president of the talks, Turkey's Environment Minister Murat Kurum, told the BBC he was "hopeful" of a breakthrough as he entered the summit on Sunday.

"We will be happy soon enough," he said.

But that outlook was not shared by the EU, which the BBC understands considers the new text to be a backward step.

The EU and Pacific states had been arguing against the removal of fossil fuels from the draft text. The EU has not yet reacted to this latest draft.

The Africa Group is likely to be disappointed at this latest iteration as it includes no specific figure on money for adaptation and instead kicks that decision to future meetings.

The new draft also includes for the first time a recognition that the world is on track to miss the crucial goal of keeping temperatures below 1.5C of warming.

These talks are approaching the longest-running in the COP history.

If countries cannot reach consensus - as required by the UN's climate talks process - the negotiations could be suspended until next year. This has only happened once before since countries started holding COP climate meetings in 1995.

Just hours before the new text was published, EU Commissioner for Climate Wopke Hoekstra said if the bloc could not get "what is needed in terms of climate action... then there's no deal."

Energy Secretary Miatta Fahnbulleh, the UK's chief negotiator, struck a more hopeful tone, saying her team was still working to get an agreement.

A draft deal unveiled earlier this week called for a faster phase-out of fossil fuels, but a second, pared-down version released on Thursday stripped away all mentions of coal, oil and gas - sparking threats of a walk out.

The fallout led to the summit in Antalya blowing past the original deadline of Friday. On Saturday negotiating teams who had Sunday morning flights were rescheduling them - a sign a deal was still not in sight, and raising the risk that as teams eventually had to leave, the meeting could lose the critical numbers needed to pass an agreement.

As part of a last ditch effort to produce an acceptable text, the European Union and Saudi Arabia - who were deeply divided over the future of fossil fuels - were brought together on Saturday to seek a compromise.

World.title: Zelensky says Crimean Bridge strikes 'fair response' as he meets UK's Streeting
World.content:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has justified Kyiv's repeated attacks on a critical bridge linking Russia to occupied Crimea, calling it a "fair response" to 109 separate Russian attacks on bridges in Ukraine.

In comments to the BBC in Kyiv, Zelensky said the intense attacks on Ukraine by Russia that have followed the strikes on the Crimean Bridge were only a "signal that Vladimir Putin does not want to stop. He wants a reason to escalate".

He rejected the claim by the Russian president that the bridge - which links Russia to the peninsula it illegally annexed from Ukraine - was "exclusively civilian" in use.

"There are facts, not just the words of Putin. We can see," he said.

The Ukrainian president pointed to images online of tanks and other Russian military hardware using the route from Russia into occupied Crimea as a supply line and for logistics.

"If Putin used the internet, he could see that."

The Ukrainian president added that Russia had carried out attacks with missiles and drones on bridges in Ukraine.

This week's combined missile-and-drone strikes by Ukrainian forces destroyed the central road section of the Crimean Bridge, collapsing part of it together with one of the two support arches into the sea and rendering the structure unusable for road traffic.

Russian attacks on Ukraine continued on Friday evening and overnight: a seven-year-old boy was killed in missile and drone strikes on Zelensky's hometown of Kryvyi Rih in the central Dnipropetrovsk region. Local officials say he had been in a playground at the time.

A 20-year-old female medic was also killed. A local official added that when rescuers rushed to the scene, the same site was targeted again with jet powered drones. Another 58 people were injured in the city.

Ukraine's state emergency service DSNS said 11 people were also injured in the north-eastern Kharkiv region, and one person in Rivne, in the north-west.

Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.

World.title: Russia-bound ship attacked in Gulf of Finland
World.content:
A Russian cargo vessel bound for the country's Baltic exclave Kaliningrad has been hit by a drone attack in the eastern Gulf of Finland, Russian and Finnish authorities say.

The ship - the Sparta II - caught on fire after the strike on Saturday morning, before drifting into Finnish waters. Finnish defence forces said Ukraine was likely behind the attack. Kyiv has yet to comment.

"War is spilling over into our immediate vicinity," Finnish Prime Minister Petteri Orpo said. "Ukraine has the right to fight back against the aggressor."

Kaliningrad Governor Alexei Besprozvannykh said two drones had been used, based on preliminary information, and there was "no threat" to the territory's supplies.

The Sparta II was sanctioned by the US in 2022 and Ukraine earlier this year, and is run by a Russian company, according to the Ukrainian and US governments.

The company says on its website that it was established within the structure of Russia's defence ministry in 2011 and since 2015 has been operating within the military construction complex.

Finland's coast guard said it had been alerted to the attack at around 08:50 local time (06:50 GMT) on Saturday and that the cargo vessel had been located approximately 50km west of the island of Suursaari in the Gulf of Finland.

This prompted "temporary aviation and maritime restrictions" around the area, Finnish border officials said.

Shortly after the incident, Finland's defence ministry said a Russian helicopter was suspected of violating the country's airspace, potentially linked to "rescue or tracking operations".

A Russian rescue vessel approached the ship and was told by the crew that they did not need to be evacuated, Kaliningrad's governor wrote on Telegram, adding: "The crew is currently carrying out the necessary work and plans to continue on its way."

The Finnish Border Guard later said the crew had been evacuated to another Russian vessel that was now already en route to Russia. The Russian rescue vessel had remained at the location of the stricken ship.

It added that no environmental damage had been detected and that there was no danger to maritime traffic or people.

Kaliningrad is a Russian exclave that sits between Poland and Lithuania.

World.title: Mexican drug lord on FBI's 10 most wanted list arrested in shoot-out
World.content:
A Mexican drug lord who was on the FBI's 10 most wanted list has been arrested following a shoot-out with Mexican authorities.

Fausto Isidro "Chapo Isidro" Meza Flores and seven others were detained by Mexican special forces in Guasave, Sinaloa on Friday, Mexico's defence secretariat said.

Seven suspects were killed in the operation, as were four members of the Mexican army who were travelling to reinforce security in Guasave, the secretariat added.

Meza Flores was wanted in Mexico on organised crime charges, while he has been accused of "flooding the US with fentanyl, cocaine, heroin and other deadly drugs" by the FBI. The US is seeking his extradition.

Mexico has stepped up efforts to tackle drug-related crime after coming under pressure from US President Donald Trump since he returned to the White House.

Meza Flores, the leader of the Meza Flores Organisation, also known as the Guasave Cartel, is thought to have been active in the drug trafficking trade since the 1990s but managed to evade authorities till now by maintaining a relatively low profile.

World.title: FBI reportedly investigating apparent hack of its criminal database
World.content:
The FBI is investigating an apparent breach of its criminal information database, US media reports, citing two people briefed on the issue.

The National Crime Information Center (NCIC) database is used by federal and local law enforcement to share information on warrants and background checks.

It would not be the first time hackers have targeted the FBI, the domestic intelligence and security service of the US. The agency did not respond to the BBC's request for comment.

When asked about the breach in a Fox News interview on Saturday, President Donald Trump said he had "just heard" about the hack. "I will say that it's not good. I don't like that," he said.

"But maybe we'll learn things that we would've never learned otherwise," Trump added.

This apparent breach of FBI database comes after a string of tech outages which hit banking, air traffic control and other sectors in the US last week. Officials have said they were not caused by cyber-attacks, but the blackouts have sparked scrutiny from lawmakers.

White House National Cyber Director Sean Cairncross was fired this week, with Trump saying he was not good enough.

Dan Lorhmann, a former analyst for the National Security Agency (NSA), told the BBC News Channel that the NCIC's data included "critical information relating to nationwide criminal activity" and needed to be protected.

He added that while US security agencies including the FBI have "an amazing ability" to keep such information safe" and are "globally respected", the level of cyber-attacks is rising globally.

"There's a lot of different reasons why that's happening but I do have faith in our experts in government," Lorhmann said.

In September, the FBI said it was investigating an apparent breach by a cyber-crime group ShinyHunters, which claimed it had stolen sensitive information on all bureau staff - around 38,000 people.

After that hack, one former FBI agent told the BBC he feared for the safety of current employees, whose personal information could soon become available online to criminals and hostile nation-state hackers.

In a separate development, NBC reported an apparent cyberattack against the US Department of Agriculture (USDA).

Employees were informed on Thursday that its farm payment system had been targeted, NBC said.

The USDA has not publicly commented on the issue.

World.title: Denmark accuses Russia of plotting to assassinate US-Ukrainian rapper
World.content:
Denmark has accused Russian intelligence services of plotting to assassinate a Ukrainian-American near Copenhagen, saying they had "planned" and "initiated" the attempt.

Denmark's security and intelligence agency (PET) said it had stopped individuals who were intending to kill the person, named by Danish media as rapper Kyivstoner, at a concert in September. Two people were charged with attempted murder and assisting a foreign intelligence service, and pleaded not guilty.

Denmark's foreign minister said Russia's defence attachÃ© will now be expelled.

Russia's embassy in Denmark called the allegations "unsubstantiated" and said Copenhagen failed to provide evidence of Moscow's involvement.

In a statement, the embassy claimed a "Danish model" had emerged, which it described as a "Russian trace" allegedly being discovered and "exploited for a propaganda spectacle". It accused Denmark of "provocations" intending to "frighten the Danish population in order to justify... a prolonged confrontation with Russia".

Russian state media cite the foreign ministry in Moscow as saying it will respond to the expulsion of its official "accordingly".

In a statement on Saturday, European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said: "I strongly condemn the assassination attempt against a US-Ukrainian citizen in Denmark, orchestrated by Russian intelligence services.

"This was an attack on EU soil. And it is unacceptable," she said, adding that "Russia's hybrid threats are becoming less and less hybrid, and more and more real."

The rapper's real name is Albert Vasiliev.

PET said the individuals who allegedly tried to assassinate him were associated with a banned Danish gang named Loyal to Familia. The group is "known for extensive, serious and violent criminal activity", according to the agency.

PET, which worked with police on the case, said three individuals were stopped while travelling by car near the music venue where Kyivstoner was set to perform on 25 September.

Firearms and knives were found in the vehicle, PET said.

Since then, two people linked to the case have been charged with attempted murder and assisting a foreign intelligence service.

Both individuals pleaded not guilty to the charges, local media reported.

In July, Russia's FSB security service accused Vasiliev and the Ukrainian authorities of organising a "terrorist attack" on military facilities and personnel in Russia. The rapper denied this allegation on social media.

In a statement on Friday, Danish Foreign Minister Lars LÃ¸kke Rasmussen said the alleged assassination attempt was Russian "intimidation" and an attempt to make Denmark "waver" in its support for Ukraine.

Russia's defence attachÃ© must leave the country within seven days, Rasmussen said.

He also said Denmark wants the EU to restrict the ability of Russians to travel throughout Europe, saying even though Copenhagen was already very reluctant to issue visas, Russians could still get a Schengen visa in another country and travel to Denmark.

Copenhagen wants these visas to apply only in the country that has issued them, he added.

World.title: Man convicted of starting Palisades fire in Los Angeles
World.content:
Rinderknecht was found guilty of lighting a fire on 1 January last year which burned undetected deep in root systems before flaring back up six days later.

One of the charges was for starting the original brush fire, while the other centred on the damage caused when it reignited into a catastrophic blaze.

"We were determined to hold him accountable, and today's guilty verdict delivers a measure of justice for the families who lost loved ones and the thousands whose lives were upended," said Bill Essayli, who leads the US Attorney's Office for the Central District of California.

Rinderknecht is a Los Angeles resident and former ride-share delivery driver.

Defence attorney Steve Haney had argued at trial that prosecutors lacked sufficient physical evidence or records to prove their case.

Lawyers for the defendant said they were "disappointed" by the verdict but respected the jury's decision.

Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass, who was widely criticised for her handling of the fires, said in a statement that "no verdict can bring back the lives lost or erase the pain families have endured".

"So many are still struggling to rebuild," she said. "For those still displaced, the devastation remains a daily reality."

Prosecutors had argued that Rinderknecht was driven by revenge, anger and loneliness because he had nowhere to go for the holiday.

They cited geolocation data from his iPhone, security camera footage that showed his car's location and witness testimony from passengers.

They alleged that Rinderknecht had a "deeply entrenched belief that the wealthy were destroying the world" and in turn purposely started the blaze in the affluent neighbourhood.

The fire was one of several that ignited back-to-back across the LA region in January, which in total left 31 people dead and destroyed 16,000 structures.

World.title: Three killed and dozens missing after fire at Indonesian factory
World.content:
At least three people have been killed and 36 are still missing after a fire at a confectionary factory in western Java on Saturday.

Firefighters were still tackling some flames on Sunday, while rescuers searched for the missing in parts of the damaged building where workers were believed to be trapped.

Indonesia's National Search and Rescue Agency said on Sunday 15 survivors had been located, and four others taken to hospital and a local clinic with undisclosed injuries.

The factory is in Serang district, Banten province, about 50km (31km) west of Jakarta. Authorities have not yet determined the fire's cause.

Banten Governor, Andra Soni, told media about 60 people were believed to be inside the factory when it caught fire on Saturday evening.

Photos and footage of the scene showed the large factory taken over by flames during the night, firefighters battling the flames, and first responders retrieving at least one body from the wreckage on Sunday morning.

"All members of the joint SAR team are making every effort to locate the missing victims while prioritising the safety of personnel on the ground," the rescue agency said.

Relatives of the missing workers had gathered outside the factory waiting for updates, according to local broadcasts cited by AFP.

Firefighters had been called to the building at 16:30 local time (09:30 GMT) on Saturday - but it was already engulfed in flames, broadcaster Kompas TV reported, citing fire official Tubugas Machfudz.

"When we arrived (on location)... a large area was already on fire. So we could not determine whether the company's protection system was functioning properly or not," he said.

The factory is owned by PT Fonusa Agung Mulia, according to search and rescue authorities.

On LinkedIn the company describes itself as a subsidiary of UNIFAM, one of Indonesia's largest food and beverage companies.

World.title: 2027: Abia government alerts public on fake post about Otti
World.content:
The Abia State Government has alerted the public to a fake statement claiming Governor Alex Otti said he would not campaign for re-election ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The fake statement, presented as Mr Otti’s post on X (formerly Twitter), read: “As an incumbent, you have no business running around, wasting public money on campaigning. Your achievements should do the campaigning for you, and that is why I’m not campaigning.

“When you see an incumbent running around campaigning and making promises, it means he didn’t achieve anything.

“Abia people should re-elect me if they feel that I’ve performed.”

Ferdinand Ekeoma, the special adviser on media and publicity to Mr Otti, said in a statement on Saturday night that the statement attributed to the Abia governor was fake.

“Please note that both the X (twitter) handle and the said statement are FAKE and did not emanate from the Governor,” Mr Ekeoma stated.

“The Governor believes that campaigns are legitimate parts of the electoral process and thus could not have dismissed it or cast aspersions on those campaigning.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The general public is therefore enjoined to disregard the FAKE statement and the FAKE account that published it.”

Mr Ekeoma advised those dishing out the disinformation on their social media pages to delete it and desist from misrepresenting Governor Otti.

“Those who desire to trend or drive traffic leveraging the popularity of the Governor must ensure that they publish the truth at all times to avoid incurring the wrath of law enforcement agents,” he said.

In contrast to the fake social media post, Mr Otti has been campaigning for re-election. For instance, on 11 November, Mr Otti was in Obingwa East to solicit support from the residents. The governor used the opportunity to commission two roads built by his administration–the 12.5km Ohanze-Ntighauzo-Obete-Akirika Obu Road and the Oberete-Umuokpara Road.

Mr Otti last month, at the Michael Okpara Auditorium, Umuahia, inaugurated the Labour Party Campaign Council for the 2027 general elections.

World.title: ALBUM REVIEW: On ‘OG Forever’, Mr P has ‘Nothing to Prove’ and plenty to explain
World.content:
Five years after his first solo album, “The Prodigal”, Nigerian singer Peter “Mr P” Okoye has returned with “OG Forever”, a project that reflects his determination to establish himself beyond P-Square. The album arrives amid the ongoing dispute between him, his twin brother Paul “Rudeboy” Okoye, and Jude Okoye, the group’s ex-manager, over royalties from the defunct group.

Mr P released the 15-track album on 20 November, collaborating with producer Golden “Goldswarm” Shedrack on most of the songs. The team also used additional mixing techniques and AI-assisted tools on selected tracks. He enlisted Nigerian rising star Qing Madi, Ghanaian music heavyweight Stonebwoy, Tanzanian singer Jux and former Mavin Records artiste Reekado Banks, giving the project a varied mix of voices and musical influences.

The singer previously unveiled the album’s tracklist and cover art, explaining that he spent two years completing the project. He described a demanding recording experience marked by sleepless nights, repeated studio sessions, mixing and mastering, and several revisions as he pursued the sound he wanted.

The album combines earlier singles with new collaborations, balancing club-friendly records with romantic songs and reflective moments. Through this blend, Mr P attempts to appeal to both P-Square’s established fanbase and a newer generation of Afrobeats listeners.

In this review, PREMIUM TIMES examines the P Classic Records release and how Mr P uses his sophomore solo album to demonstrate artistic growth, resilience and a stronger sense of personal identity.

Track listing: P-Square disputes

Nothing To Prove

Mr P opens “OG Forever” with a statement of independence. “Nothing To Prove” captures the mindset of an artiste who believes he has moved beyond the need to justify his talent or defend his place in the music industry.

During his press run with Do2tun, Mr P singled out the song as the track that best describes him at this stage of his career. He produced the three-minute-and-50-second record, which sets the album’s emotional direction before the guest appearances begin.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The song draws heavily on the criticism he has faced since P-Square broke up, making it one of the project’s most personal moments. For years, critics and rival fans have questioned Mr P’s contribution to the group, often reducing his role to dancing while crediting Rudeboy with the vocals and songwriting.

Mr P confronts that perception head-on. He begins by recalling the criticism: “They say I fail, they say I fall. They say my time don pass and stall.” He then points to what he considers the irony of those who doubt him: “Same people wey dey doubt my name oh no. Still dey dance when dem hear my song.”

The singer does not use the track to trade insults with his brothers or critics. Instead, he turns the chorus into an affirmation of his own confidence: “If you no believe me, I believe me too. I got nothing to prove.” He reinforces the message with “Still my lane, still my pace. God no dey make mistake.”

These lines suggest that Mr P now sees his solo career as a journey that needs no permission or validation from others. In the second verse, he addresses the broken relationship without naming those involved: “I forgive, I no fight. I just live my life. Love for the ones wey stay.” His declaration, “If you ride with me, cool. If you don’t, no rules”, further underscores his willingness to accept the people who support him and move on from those who do not.

Wish You Well

Mr P turns inward on “Wish You Well”, the album’s sixth track and its longest record. The 4-minute, 25-second song drops guest appearances and heavy club production, focusing firmly on his relationship with Rudeboy.

He revisits the twin bond that existed before P-Square, recalling their shared dreams and their late mother’s desire to keep them united. “One face, one name, same blood, same birthday” captures their common beginnings, while “mama dressed us the same, she say nothing come between you two” highlights the painful distance between her wish and their present reality.

The song’s strength lies in its refusal to repackage the feud as another diss track. After years of public exchanges, royalty disputes and management disagreements, Mr P chooses to address the fallout through a message of peace.

His declaration, “I chose peace over fight, I chose silence over war”, sums up the track’s emotional direction. He acknowledges the hurt but refuses to remain trapped by it, extending goodwill to his brother while maintaining his own solo identity.

Placing “Wish You Well” after “OG Forever” and near “Nothing to Prove” and “Winning” gives the album a coherent narrative. Mr P presents himself as an artiste who has moved beyond the P-Square era without denying its importance to his career.

Musically, the track favours a warm, mid-tempo Afrobeats arrangement over dramatic drops or aggressive percussion. The restrained production complements its reflective lyrics and gives the song room to breathe.

Though it lacks the immediate energy of a club record, “Wish You Well” delivers one of the album’s more affecting moments. Mr P frames the breakdown of a childhood partnership as a personal loss, but ultimately chooses peace over resentment.

Winning

The album’s ninth track revisits the strained relationship between Mr P, Rudeboy and Jude. At 4 minutes and 23 seconds, the mid-tempo record arrives against the backdrop of the long-running P-Square controversy. The production is solid, with a catchy chorus and a well-executed instrumental that supports the song’s message of perseverance and positivity.

Mr P encourages listeners to celebrate one another’s progress rather than harbour resentment. While some may interpret the track as a direct response to his family dispute, its message extends beyond the feud, promoting unity and mutual support.

The song becomes more personal when he addresses family conflict, urging his brother to abandon negativity and embrace the bond they share.

“Why you dey hate on your brother, why you dey stab am for corner?” he asks, before reminding listeners to “stick with your brother and stick with your sister”. The repetitive chorus, “I see you winning, I’m winning, we all are winning for life”, reinforces the song’s central idea: success should not come at the expense of another person’s happiness.

Despite its effective arrangement and relatable message, “Winning” relies on familiar musical and lyrical tropes. Its lack of innovation limits its impact, even as Mr P delivers a straightforward appeal for unity and perseverance.

OG Forever

“OG Forever” sets the tone for Mr P’s album, serving as both the fifth track and its title record. The 3-minute, 47-second song follows “Dutty Whine” and shifts the album towards a more confident celebration of longevity and independence.

Mr P draws on his two-decade career to assert his place in the industry, from his years with P-Square to his solo journey under P. Classic Records. His declaration of being an “OG Forever” reflects a belief that experience and relevance can survive changing musical trends.

The lyrics reinforce that confidence. “From day one, I dey here, same course, still clear,” he sings, presenting himself as an artiste who has remained consistent despite personal and professional challenges. The song also builds on his remarks at the Lagos album launch, where he spoke about establishing a solo legacy and maintaining his status among Nigeria’s leading artistes at 50.

Musically, the record blends polished Afrobeats production with a mid-tempo groove. Its repetitive hook and infectious cadence give it an anthem-like quality, while the absence of guest features keeps the spotlight on Mr P.

However, the song’s reliance on familiar phrasing and a predictable structure makes it more effective as a statement of intent than as a bold musical experiment. Still, “OG Forever” fulfils its purpose. It establishes Mr P’s confidence, reinforces his solo identity and reminds listeners that he sees his career as an ongoing journey rather than a chapter defined by P-Square.

Tracklisting: Love and attraction

“I Can’t Look Away”

Following the introspective opener “Nothing to Prove”, Mr P switches gears with “I Can’t Look Away”, a lively Afropop record that trades family drama for romance and dancefloor energy. Released as a lead single in mid-2026, the three-minute track revisits the infectious, rhythm-driven sound that made him a household name.

The production combines modern Afro-fusion with the high-energy party feel of classic P-Square love songs. Mr P wastes little time getting into the groove, relying on catchy chants and familiar call-and-response patterns to keep the record moving.

He keeps the lyrics playful and straightforward, celebrating a woman whose beauty and confidence mesmerise him. Rather than pursuing elaborate wordplay, he builds the song around memorable hooks, particularly the exchange, “Omo, the level? Highest! Omo, the body? Finest!”

The second verse further celebrates her commanding presence: “Anywhere she dey, na lockdown. Anywhere she go, na shutdown. Camera flash as she touch ground”.

Although the song favours repetition over lyrical depth, its brisk arrangement prevents it from overstaying its welcome. It also provides a smooth transition into the more soulful “Brown Sugar” featuring Qing Madi.

Brown Sugar

Mr P softens the tempo on “Brown Sugar”, a romantic collaboration with Qing Madi that brings a refreshing change of pace to OG Forever. The song trades the club-ready energy of its predecessor for a mellow Afropop/R&B sound, allowing the singers to focus on melody and vocal chemistry.

Mr P delivers his lines with familiar rhythmic ease, while Qing Madi adds a soulful touch that gives the record its emotional appeal. The songwriting remains uncomplicated, celebrating affection and mutual attraction through sweet, accessible lyrics. “Oh mine, brown sugar, sweet like sugar cane, you made my sugar low low…” captures the song’s playful romantic mood.

Qing Madi’s entrance, “I’ve searched around the world, babe you’re the one I want…”, strengthens the chorus and balances the collaboration. While the song does not venture far beyond familiar love-song themes, the vocal chemistry and restrained production make it one of the album’s more cohesive moments.

Dutty Whine

“Dutty Whine” delivers a quick dose of dancefloor energy, switching from the mellow sound of “Brown Sugar” to a lively dancehall-infused groove.

The two-minute record draws on Mr P’s performance background, placing rhythm and movement ahead of elaborate songwriting. Its Caribbean-inspired bounce and repetitive hook make it an obvious fit for clubs and live performances.

Little goes beyond the party atmosphere, but the song’s brevity keeps it from becoming tedious. Mr P gets in, establishes the groove and leaves before the energy fades. As a short interlude within the album’s broader sequence, “Dutty Whine” provides a welcome change of pace.

I Love You Because

Mr P delivers a heartfelt declaration of love on “I Love You Because”, a solo record that looks beyond physical attraction to celebrate the deeper bonds of marriage. Unlike “I Can’t Look Away”, which focuses on the excitement of falling for someone, this song explores why a relationship endures.

Mr P celebrates companionship, emotional comfort and the memories that strengthen a lasting partnership. His restrained vocal delivery suits the song’s intimate mood, while the absence of a guest feature allows him to carry the message without distraction.

The official video, which features his wife, Lola Omotayo-Okoye, adds another layer to the record. Against the backdrop of the prolonged P-Square family feud, her picture appearance gives the song the feel of a personal affirmation of their marriage.

Having addressed his brothers and critics on “Nothing to Prove” and “Wish You Well”, Mr P turns his attention to the family he has built at home. The result is one of the album’s most personal and emotionally grounded tracks. The song becomes a tribute to loyalty and companionship, celebrating a partner who has stood beside him through personal and public challenges.

Other songs on the album include “I Dey Active”, “Chukwu Mee”, “Permanent Address”, “Peteru” and “Back 2 Back”. It also features collaborations with Juma Jux and Stonebwoy on “No Case”, and Reekado Banks on “Shebi You Dey Whine Me”.

Verdict

One major issue is Mr P’s failure to embrace a new artistic direction fully; instead, he spends considerable time addressing his strained relationship with his brothers and responding to critics. The recurring themes across “Nothing to Prove”, “OG Forever”, “Wish You Well” and “Winning” make the album sound like a prolonged response to the P-Square fallout.

Mr P’s embrace of artificial intelligence, which he defended as a modern production tool and acknowledged in the mixing of “Back to Back”, raises questions about the album’s sonic direction. The excessive vocal processing and polished arrangements leave several songs sounding sterile, missing the raw musical character of his earlier hits.

Tracks such as “Nothing to Prove”, “Brown Sugar”, “Wish You Well”, “Winning”, and “I Love You Because” lean heavily on mid-tempo Afropop. Their similar arrangements make the 15-track project drag in places and offer little energy variation.

“Dutty Whine” and “Permanent Address” provide some of the album’s most energetic moments, yet Mr P gives them little room to develop. Both tracks end prematurely, while several slower songs stretch familiar ideas for longer than necessary.

Despite its shortcomings, the album delivers highlights through “Wish You Well”, “I Love You Because” and “No Case.” However, Mr P could have achieved a stronger result by cutting repetitive material, experimenting with different tempos, and letting the production feel more natural.

Rating: 6/10

World.title: SERAP sues NDPC, INEC over alleged AI manipulation of voters’ register
World.content:
The Socio-Economic Rights and Accountability Project (SERAP) has filed a lawsuit against the National Data Protection Commission (NDPC) and the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) over “the alleged use by some INEC officials of AI-generated photographs to manipulate INEC’s preliminary Register of Voters, and the failure to ensure the protection of voters’ personal data and investigate the alleged violations.”

The lawsuit follows INEC’s acknowledgement of suspected AI-generated photographs and questionable records in the preliminary Register of Voters. On 1 November 2026, INEC reportedly disclosed that its Automated Biometric Identification System (ABIS) had flagged 268 records for review, with some individuals allegedly exploiting official registration credentials.

In suit number FHC/ABJ/CS/2863/2026, filed last week at the Federal High Court in Abuja, SERAP is seeking “an order of mandamus to direct and compel the NDPC to make an independent and reasoned determination on the allegations of suspected AI-generated photographs, alterations to personal data and unverifiable records in INEC’s preliminary Register of Voters, including whether to initiate an investigation.”

SERAP is also seeking “an order of mandamus to direct and compel the NDPC to obtain and examine relevant records, documents and electronic data held by INEC to establish the nature and extent of the reported irregularities and determine whether the Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023 has been violated.”

SERAP is further seeking “an order of mandamus to direct and compel the NDPC to exercise its enforcement powers under the Act, including issuing corrective orders, imposing appropriate fines and sanctions, and facilitating remedies or compensation for voters affected by any established violations.”

In the suit, SERAP is arguing that: “The alleged irregularities raise serious concerns about the security and integrity of Nigerians’ personal data and the reliability of the voters’ register ahead of the 2027 general elections.”

SERAP is also arguing that: “The security and accuracy of the voters’ register are fundamental to the protection of Nigerians’ personal data and their right to participate in public affairs. Nigerians should not have to worry that their personal information could be altered, manipulated or accessed without proper safeguards.”

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

SERAP is further arguing that: “INEC’s acknowledgement of questionable records and suspected AI-generated photographs makes an independent investigation particularly important. The public needs to know what happened, whether the law was breached and what measures are being taken to prevent a recurrence.”

According to SERAP, “The NDPC should exercise its statutory powers independently and without delay. Any investigation must establish the facts, protect affected voters and ensure that those responsible for any unlawful conduct are held accountable.”

The lawsuit, filed on behalf of SERAP by its lawyers, Oluwakemi Agunbiade, Kehinde Oyewumi, Andrew Nwankwo, and Valentina Adegoke, reads in part: “The investigation should establish the nature and extent of the reported irregularities, including the number and geographical distribution of affected records, when and how they were created or altered, and the persons or institutions responsible.”

“The introduction of questionable records, including photographs suspected to have been artificially generated, raises legitimate concerns about the accuracy and reliability of the register and the safeguards protecting its integrity.”

“The reported irregularities may involve the unlawful alteration or processing of personal data, possible misuse of authorised access credentials and failures to ensure the accuracy, integrity and security of personal data held and processed by INEC.”

“The court should direct and compel the NDPC to conduct an independent forensic examination of the affected database and systems to determine whether personal data were unlawfully accessed or altered and whether INEC complied with the Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023.”

“The court should also direct and compel the NDPC to determine whether the incidents constitute a personal data breach under section 65 of the Act and whether INEC has complied with its applicable notification and record-keeping obligations.”

“According to INEC’s statement of 27 October 2026, the Commission acknowledged public concerns regarding ‘suspected AI-generated photographs appearing in the Preliminary Register of Voters’ published on its website.”

“INEC stated that, during the physical display of the register nationwide from 9 to 15 October 2026, ‘a number of questionable registration records were identified and flagged for further examination’. The Commission said it had commenced a review and was taking ‘appropriate corrective action’.”

“INEC also acknowledged that the online publication ‘does not reflect all ongoing data-cleanup activities’ and that it was ‘examining the circumstances surrounding the suspicious photographs, including possible technical or procedural lapses’.”

“INEC stated that the preliminary register was not the final certified register and undertook to complete the necessary verification, adjudication and data-cleanup processes before certifying the final Register of Voters on 15 December 2026.”

“INEC has reportedly acknowledged the existence of questionable voter-registration records and indicated that some registration officers may have used their official access credentials to introduce irregular records, including photographs suspected to have been generated using artificial intelligence.”

“While the Commission has indicated that it is reviewing the matter, an independent investigation by the NDPC is necessary to establish the full circumstances, determine the extent of the irregularities and ensure accountability.”

“An internal review by INEC cannot substitute for the NDPC’s independent exercise of its statutory data-protection mandate.”

“The reported irregularities in INEC’s voter-registration database are particularly concerning because the database contains the personal data of millions of Nigerians and is fundamental to the exercise of their constitutional and democratic rights.”

“Any unlawful alteration, manipulation or compromise of this information could undermine public confidence in the electoral process, compromise the accuracy and reliability of the voters’ register, and expose eligible voters to the risk of wrongful exclusion.”

“The Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023 gives the NDPC clear powers to investigate possible violations, obtain relevant information and documents, and require compliance by data controllers and processors. Sections 24 and 39 of the Act require personal data to be processed accurately and securely, and protected against unlawful alteration, loss or unauthorised access.”

“Section 65 of the Act defines a personal data breach to include a breach of security leading, or likely to lead, to the unlawful alteration, loss, unauthorised disclosure of or access to personal data.”

“Under section 40, data controllers must notify the NDPC of a breach likely to pose a risk to individuals’ rights and freedoms within 72 hours of becoming aware of it, and communicate the breach to affected individuals where it is likely to result in a high risk. The Act also requires the maintenance of records of personal data breaches.”

“The reported involvement of registration officers with authorised access to the database makes it particularly important to establish whether adequate safeguards were in place and whether those safeguards were circumvented or misused. The use of authorised credentials does not, by itself, establish that subsequent access or processing was lawful or within the scope of the officer’s authority.”

“The reported irregularities also raise concerns about Nigerians’ constitutional and international human rights, including the rights to privacy and political participation.”

“Section 37 of the Nigerian Constitution 1999 (as amended) guarantees the right to privacy. Article 13 of the African Charter on Human and Peoples’ Rights and Article 25 of the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights protect citizens’ rights to participate freely in government and to vote in genuine elections.”

“These rights require effective safeguards to ensure that eligible voters are not arbitrarily prevented from exercising their political rights.”

“The integrity and accuracy of the Register of Voters are indispensable to the effective exercise of the rights to participate in public affairs and to vote in genuine elections. The reported irregularities must be treated with the seriousness they deserve.”

“INEC has indicated that it will complete the necessary verification and data-cleanup exercises before certification of the final Register of Voters. It is therefore essential that the reported irregularities are promptly and independently investigated and effectively addressed before the register is finalised.”

“Nigerians must be able to trust that the register on which the 2027 general elections will be conducted is accurate, reliable and adequately protected against manipulation.”

“The protection of personal data, the integrity of electoral institutions and the effective exercise of political rights are mutually reinforcing obligations under the Nigerian Constitution and international human rights law.”

“Addressing the reported irregularities transparently and effectively would strengthen public confidence in the electoral process and safeguard Nigerians’ right to participate freely in public affairs.”

No date has been fixed for the hearing of the suit.

Kolawole Oluwadare

SERAP Deputy Director

World.title: Jim Iyke unveils wife after nearly five years of marriage
World.content:
Nigerian actor and entrepreneur Jim Iyke has broken his silence on his largely private marriage, unveiling his wife to the public nearly five years after they met.

The actor posted a video on his Instagram page on Saturday, accompanied by a lengthy account of how their relationship began. However, he did not disclose his wife’s name.

Recalling their first encounter, the 50-year-old said he met her at the Delta Lounge in Houston, United States, almost five years ago. According to him, she initially rejected his attempt to take the seat beside her, claiming that it was already occupied.

Iyke said: “Almost five years of us. No proof needed. No audience required. Five years in, and you still feel like a secret I’m not ready to share, not because you’re hidden, but because you’re sacred. I met her at the Delta lounge to Houston. I asked if the seat next to her was taken.

She said briskly, “It’s taken”— trying to get rid of me. I sat down anyway. She said, “Sir, I said the seat is taken.” I said, “I don’t see a name tag on the seat.” She gave me a “bombastic” side eye. I chuckled. Enjoying myself thoroughly. We ignored each other for an hour. Then they called for boarding, and we realised we were on the same flight — and we started laughing.”

Family

Reflecting on their relationship, the actor said he and his fair-skinned wife had built a family together and explored eight countries as a couple.

He described her as his closest friend, prayer warrior, and partner, adding that he felt fortunate to have her in his life.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

He said their commitment to loyalty, trust, and lasting love had helped them navigate the different stages of their marriage.

“5 years later, a whole family unit, 8 countries later. And we’ve never stopped laughing at each other and at life together ever since. You’re my best friend. My prayer warrior. My wifey. My dude. All in one person; how did I get that lucky? Same soul. Different seasons. We didn’t count days. Days counted us.
