Analysts stressed the importance of tax remittance and said the disclosure obligations that come with listing on the NGX make it easier to scrutinise companies’ tax affairs.

The Vice-President of Highcap Securities Limited, Mr David Adnori, said listed companies could face higher tax bills this year, with implications for shareholder returns.

Adnori said failing to remit taxes could expose companies to enforcement action, including branch closures and operational disruption. He called for a simpler tax system to make remittance easier and reduce disputes between companies and revenue authorities.

He added that tax remittances helped finance economic development and urged companies to meet their obligations, including those owed to state governments where they operate. He said companies should comply with the applicable laws and make full disclosures.

Adnori said some categories of income may qualify for tax exemptions, citing income from Treasury bills, government bonds and agricultural loans. He said differences in income composition could explain why some banks have lower effective tax rates than manufacturing companies.

World.title: NUPRC Opens Portal for 40 Oil, Gas Blocks in 2026 Licensing Round
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

Emmanuel Addeh in Abuja

The Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission (NUPRC) at the weekend opened the registration portal for its 2026 oil and gas licensing round, offering 40 blocks across onshore, shallow water and deep offshore terrains to prospective investors.

Registration on the portal, it said, commenced on November 20, 2026 and will close on January 15, 2027, for 17 onshore blocks, 14 shallow water and nine deep offshore assets.

The commission urged interested investors to visit the portal to access the full list of available blocks, bidding guidelines and frequently asked questions, explaining that the platform was designed to provide a seamless experience for prospective bidders.

The licensing process, a statement by the commission said, will run through five stages, including registration and prequalification, access to data, submission of technical and commercial bids, technical evaluation and commercial conference.

According to the upstream regulator, the next major activity would be a pre-bid conference scheduled to hold in Lagos on December 16, 2026, stressing that further information and updates would be communicated through the portal and its official social media platforms.

The 2026 licensing round was announced by the Commission Chief Executive, Oritsemeyiwa Eyesan, on October 6, following approval by President Bola Tinubu, who also serves as Minister of Petroleum Resources.

Meanwhile, the commission has pledged to ensure timely delivery of Nigeria’s upstream climate commitments, declaring that its gas flaring and methane reduction targets were regulatory obligations rather than mere aspirations.

It disclosed that metering compliance across flare sites had reached 92 per cent, describing the progress as part of efforts to strengthen emissions monitoring and ensure that climate commitments are backed by verifiable data.

Speaking on behalf of Eyesan at a side event organised by the African Green Economy and Sustainability Institute (AGESI) at the Gabon Pavilion during COP31 in Türkiye, Assistant Director, Remediation and Sustainability, Ibrahim Alhaji, said the commission was moving from estimates to evidence in monitoring emissions.

Under Nigeria’s Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs) 3.0, the country said it was committed to ending routine gas flaring by 2030 and reducing fugitive methane emissions by 60 per cent.

According to the NURPC, the development has a potential to reduce more than 27 million tonnes of fugitive methane emissions and 2 million tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent from flaring by 2035.

Eyesan identified transparency, investment readiness and capacity building as the three critical pillars for achieving the targets, stressing that credible emissions data would make climate-related projects more attractive to investors and improve access to climate and blended finance.

The session, convened by AGESI, the Society for Planet and Prosperity and Natural Eco Capital, ended with a follow-up plan focused on partnerships, data disclosure, capacity building and progress reporting beyond COP31.

World.title: FG Increases Admission of Medical Students from 5,000 to 12,000, Targets 20,000 Annually
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

Kemi Olaitan in Ibadan

The federal government has increased annual admission into medical schools from 5,000 to 12,000 students, the Minister of Education, Dr. Tunji Alausa, has said.

Alausa, who stated this yesterday on the sidelines of the inauguration of a 192-bed hostel at the College of Medicine, University of Ibadan (UI), said that the federal government targeted enrollment of 20,000 students annually.

The minister said the increase in enrollment was part of efforts to address manpower shortages in the health sector amid the migration of Nigerian medical professionals abroad.

He said that the government, since President Bola Tinubu assumed office, had increased nursing enrollment from about 28,000 annually to more than 130,000.

According to him, the country was making progress in producing more healthcare professionals.

Alausa, who represented Tinubu at the inauguration, said the administration was investing in infrastructure to expand the capacity of medical schools and other tertiary institutions to accommodate more students.

According to him, annual admission into medical schools had risen to about 12,000, from 5,000 students recorded before the administration began in May 2023.

“We decided that in four years, we will increase the number to 20,000 annually.

“Three years into it, we are enrolling about 12,000 medical students now across all our medical schools in the country, and by the end of 2028, we will meet our target of enrolling over 20,000 medical students,” he said.

Alausa said the government had also increased admission into dentistry, pharmacy, physiotherapy, and other allied health programmes to strengthen the country’s healthcare workforce.

He said the expansion was being complemented by investments in infrastructure, including hostels, to support increased enrollment and improve the learning environment.

The minister added that the government was also investing in the education sector through the Nigeria Education Sector Renewal Initiative.

“This includes the construction and rehabilitation of schools, expansion of medical schools, and re-equipping of engineering workshops,” the minister said.

Alausa said the administration had invested nearly N500 billion in educational infrastructure, adding that the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND) had also expanded access to tertiary education for students irrespective of their economic backgrounds.

He urged journalists to verify the figures on nursing and medical students enrollment through the relevant regulatory bodies, including the Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria.

World.title: Babachir Lawal: Peter Obi Will Win 2027 Election, What Happened in 2023 Won’t Repeat Itself
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

Sunday Aborishade in Abuja

A former Secretary to the Government of the Federation (SGF) and chieftain of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Mr. Babachir Lawal, has reiterated that the party’s presidential candidate, Mr Peter Obi, would clearly emerge victorious in the 2027 presidential election, insisting that the circumstances surrounding the 2023 presidential poll would not be repeated.

Speaking during a television interview at the weekend, Lawal predicted that Obi would emerge victorious, expressing the belief that the political dynamics of the next election would be different from those of 2023.

He also questioned the outcome of the 2023 presidential election, arguing that there should have been a runoff as Obi got the highest number of votes, a development, he believed, would have changed the political calculations surrounding the contest.

“Peter got the majority of votes; he didn’t get the spread. Bola Tinubu got the spread and came second. There should have been a runoff in that election,” he said.

The former SGF further projected that Obi would win Kogi, Benue and Plateau states, and would also defeat former Vice President Atiku Abubakar of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) in his home state of Adamawa.

“I give it to you that Peter didn’t have more spread. This time, Peter will get the spread in Nigeria.

“Atiku will come third in Adamawa State this time around,” he added.

On the ADC candidate’s chances in the forthcoming election, Lawal argued that the former vice president would not have sufficient ethnic support to secure the presidency.

Comparing the NDC ticket with those of other political parties, he described it as a better option.

Lawal also disclosed that the party’s campaign strategy would prioritise town hall meetings, which he considered a more effective means of engaging voters.

He said Nigerians would look in the direction of Obi due to his character and competence.

“First of all, he is incorruptible. Second, he is detribalised. Third, he is a businessman that understands market forces. And fourth, he is a man who sticks to his words,” the NDC chieftain added.

Asked whether the former Anambra State governor made any promises to him, the former SGF said, “No, he doesn’t need to”.

The 72-year-old said he would go back to his 4,000 hectares of farmland where he produces cash crops and livestock, and watch Nigeria grow.

Asked whether he does not want to partake in Obi’s government if he wins, Babachir said, “I’m 72 years old. I have a 40-year-old son. What is wrong if Peter says, ‘I’m going to make you Minister of Agriculture,’ and I say Peter, instead, give my son Minister of Agriculture. Is that wrong? In those days when we were young, that’s how things were done.”

World.title: ‘Serial mugger’ linked to several recent attacks on Lion’s Head
World.content:
Hiker safety on Lion's Head is back in the spotlight. Image: Supplied

Hikers visiting one of Cape Town’s most popular nature attractions have been warned to exercise extreme caution following a series of violent robberies on Lion’s Head this week.

The latest incidents, which included a stabbing, were reported on Friday evening, 20 November. A suspect is believed to be linked to an earlier double mugging on the mountain.

According to the Take Back Our Mountains (TBOM) community group, two separate attacks occurred at approximately 21:30 and 21:45 on Friday.



In the first incident, a male and female hiker were approached by a man wearing a head torch, track pants and a backpack. He reportedly offered to help illuminate their path before launching an attack.

A struggle broke out, during which the male victim was kicked and punched while on the ground. He was also stabbed in the knee, approximately 500 metres from the trailhead.

A group of four hikers came across the injured man and assisted with first aid. They contacted the SANParks helpline, which dispatched police and an ambulance. However, concerned about the victim’s significant blood loss, the Good Samaritan group rushed him to hospital themselves.

The suspect allegedly continued further up the mountain, where he robbed another group of three tourists near the paragliding mat. Their belongings were stolen, although no injuries were reported.

Friday’s incidents were confirmed by City of Cape Town Councillor Emre Uygun, who noted that the male victim was recovering in hospital, where SAPS members were obtaining a statement from him.

“The victim sustained a stab wound that severed an artery, causing severe blood loss,” Uygun wrote on Sunday.



“This was an extremely serious and potentially life-threatening attack, and I hope that this perpetrator is brought to justice.”

Suspect linked to previous Lion’s Head muggings

The suspect is believed to be connected to another robbery reported on Wednesday, 18 November.

On that occasion, two visitors were reportedly held at knifepoint by two suspects at approximately 16:45. Backpacks, cellphones and wallets were stolen.

“[Friday’s] assailant is believed to be tied to the incident on Wednesday 18 November on Lion’s Head where two people were mugged,” said TBOM’s post.

“The assailant is also believed to be part a group responsible for muggings earlier this year. But this assailant got away.”

The South African contacted a spokesperson for TBOM, who said Friday’s attacker matched the description of a suspect linked to several previous incidents in the area.

“I do believe up until October, there have been reports of a bravo male with short dreads robbing people on Lion’s Head,” he said.

A call for increased security in Table Mountain national park

Friday’s incidents have since been escalated to SAPS management and the City’s Safety and Security Directorate.

TBOM has also called for increased security on the mountain, including thermal-imaging drones, additional rangers and more CCTV cameras.

Uygun urged hikers to remain vigilant, avoid hiking alone and to report suspicious activity to the relevant authorities immediately (dial 021 480 7700 or 10111).

“Please share this warning to help keep other hikers and visitors safe,” Uygun added.

World.title: Almost half of South African home loan applicants are first-time buyers
World.content:
South Africans are finding ways to buy their first homes despite higher borrowing costs. Image: canva

South Africa’s property market is seeing a notable increase in first-time buyers, with almost half of all home loan applicants now looking to purchase their first property.

According to ooba Home Loans data cited by Pam Golding Properties, first-time buyers accounted for 48.5% of home loan applications in October.

This brings the year-to-date average to 46.9%, highlighting the continued demand among aspiring homeowners despite pressure on household finances.



The figures suggest that more South Africans are finding opportunities to enter the property market, supported by competitive home loan conditions and relatively modest deposit requirements.

Smaller deposits helping first-time buyers

One of the biggest barriers to buying a first home is saving enough money for a deposit.

However, ooba’s figures show that first-time buyers are putting down an average deposit of just 8.5% of the purchase price.

This compares with an average deposit of 12.8% across all homebuyers during the year to October.

Competition between financial institutions is also helping prospective buyers secure more favourable lending conditions.

According to the data, effective home loan approval rates averaged 83.9% this year, while ooba secured an average interest rate of prime minus 0.77% in October.



Applications for home loans that include transaction costs (legal, tax, and administrative expenses) have also increased, accounting for 10.1% of applications in September and October.

These financing options could help qualifying buyers who have limited savings available for the upfront costs associated with purchasing a property.

Interest rates remain an important consideration

The increase in first-time buyer activity comes despite a challenging borrowing environment.

The South African Reserve Bank raised interest rates twice earlier in 2026, before keeping the repo rate unchanged at its November meeting.

The decision leaves the prime lending rate at 10.75%.

While the latest rate hold provides some stability for prospective buyers, higher fuel and living costs continue to put pressure on household budgets.

Pam Golding Properties chief executive Andrew Golding said the increase in first-time buyer applications demonstrates that the aspiration to own property remains strong.

He added that buyers are adapting their expectations and purchasing decisions to prevailing market conditions.

With competitive lending conditions and a growing share of first-time buyers entering the market, the entry-level and middle-market property segments could remain important drivers of residential property activity heading into 2027.

World.title: How to top up your MyCiti card online
World.content:
Top-up your MyCiti Card before travelling. Image: Pexels

Faithful MyCiti travellers have stood in queues or used clunky self-service kiosks to load points.

But that’s not necessary.

In May, MyCiti quietly launched a method to load points online with a debit or credit card. Here’s how.



Guide to Loading MyCiti Points online

To load MyCiti Points online, visit the online portal. You can select the option to top up through the app or visit the link directly: https://www.myciti.org.za/en/myconnect-topup/topup/.

Enter your MyConnect Number, email address, and select the type of product you’d like to load.

You can only load Mover points or a Monthly Pass on the system.



However, only those with MyCiti’s new MyConnect card, not the legacy bank-linked cards, can load a Monthly Pass on the system.

Finally, select Submit.

MyCiti will direct you to their payment gateway to enter your card details.



Before you can use what you’ve loaded, activate your points.

MyCiti says to wait 24 hours before doing this.

You have three options:

Using the bus validator. Activation can take up to 24 hours with this method. While the points are on your card, they only become active within 24 hours.

Station validator. Tap your card on the station validator. It should activate within 5 minutes.

Info terminal. Tap your card on the info terminal; activation should take 5 minutes.

Once you’ve activated your points, you can use those points to travel.



If you need the points immediately, MyCiti suggests using the kiosk to load points.

Using MyCiti to get around during the festive season

MyCiti is encouraging tourists and locals to use the bus service during the festive season and avoid traffic and parking.

MyCiti will launch several festive services, including a route to watch the Festive Light Switch-on.



Festive Light Switch-on

When the City switches on the Festive Lights on Sunday 29 November, MyCiti will operate a late-night service on the following routes:

T01: 22:30

D02 and D04: 22:35 and 23:00

D01: 23:00

The Festive Lights will run from 16:00 to 22:00.

Christmas Shopping

Between 4 and 23 December, MyCiti will resume its late-night bus services from Canal Walk.



The last buses will depart from Century City; these include the D08 at 22:35 and T03 at 22:30.

Connecting 241, 242 and 243 buses will depart from Atlantis Station at 23:55.

The service will also be available at the V&A Waterfront between 11 and 23 December. It won’t be available on Christmas Eve or Christmas Day, but will resume on 26 December and continue until 30 December.



Only the T01 will be impacted by the new schedule.

The last bus will depart Waterfront Station at 22:15.

Connecting buses D02 and D04 will depart Civic Centre at 22:35.

World.title: Three Kaizer Chiefs players set to miss Sundowns clash
World.content:
Kaizer Chiefs are set to be without several players when they face Mamelodi Sundowns in the Carling Knockout Cup semi-final on Sunday.

Having reached their first semi-final of the season, Fernando Da Cruz’s men will be hoping to upset Masandawana and book their place in the final.

Since taking charge in July, the French coach has steadily improved the team, with their cup performances particularly impressive compared to their inconsistent league form.



Which Kaizer Chiefs players will miss the Sundowns clash?

Amakhosi will be without Miguel Inacio, with the vice-captain suspended for Sunday’s encounter.

Another player expected to miss the match is goalkeeper Renaldo Leaner. The shot-stopper suffered an injury during training last month and is unlikely to be available for the trip to Loftus Versfeld.

Key midfielder Siphesihle Ndlovu is also doubtful after picking up an injury, leaving Da Cruz with another potential selection headache.

However, there could be some positive news for the Chiefs coach, with Khanyisa Mayo and Langelihle Phili potentially returning to the squad.

Phili could be particularly important for Amakhosi, having scored when Kaizer Chiefs faced Sundowns earlier this season.

With a place in the Carling Knockout Cup final at stake, Da Cruz will be hoping to have as many options available as possible for Sunday’s showdown. Chiefs are unbeaten against Sundowns in their last four meeting across all competitions.



Kaizer Chiefs expected starting XI v Sundowns: Petersen, Frosler, Kwinika, Moloisane, Dortley, Cross, Maboe, Mthethwa, Mmodi, Shabalala, Duba.

Can Amakhosi upset Downs or will they get hammered?

World.title: Johannesburg tightens water restrictions as supply pressures grow
World.content:
Johannesburg residents and businesses will face stricter water restrictions from Saturday, 21 November, as the City moves to reduce consumption and stabilise its strained water supply.

The City of Johannesburg (CoJ) announced the implementation of Level 2 water use restrictions until further notice, following increased demand on the system.

The restrictions aim to reduce consumption by 200 million litres per day and help restore reservoir levels.



The new rules apply to residential, commercial, institutional and other consumers across the city.

What is prohibited under Level 2 water restrictions?

Under the new restrictions, using municipal drinking water to irrigate gardens, lawns, parks and public spaces is prohibited at all times.

This replaces the limited watering hours previously allowed under Level 1 restrictions.

Residents and businesses are also prohibited from:

Hosing down driveways, paved areas, sidewalks and other hard surfaces.

Using municipal drinking water to dampen building sand.

Irrigating gardens and public spaces with municipal drinking water.

The restrictions also apply to City departments and municipal entities.

Residents and businesses have also been urged to reduce their consumption through everyday water-saving measures.



These include:

Fixing leaking taps, toilets and pipes.

Taking shorter showers.

Turning off taps when brushing teeth or washing dishes.

Running washing machines and dishwashers only with full loads.

Using buckets instead of hosepipes when washing vehicles.

Reusing suitable greywater for purposes that do not require drinking water.

The City confirmed that municipal departments will use treated wastewater instead of drinking water for certain activities.

The Johannesburg Roads Agency and its contractors will use treated effluent for road construction, while Johannesburg Water will use it for jetting activities.

Fines and enforcement for violations

Johannesburg Water will intensify its leak detection, repair work, pressure management and monitoring as part of efforts to stabilise the system.

The City has also warned that it will strengthen enforcement of the restrictions.

Consumers who fail to comply could face action in terms of the City’s Water Services by-laws.

The Level 2 restrictions will remain in place until further notice and will be reviewed according to water demand, reservoir levels and prevailing supply conditions.

World.title: Malgas wildfire destroys 24 homes in Western Cape
World.content:
A devastating wildfire destroyed 24 homes in the Malgas area near Swellendam in the Western Cape, with flames tearing through residential properties. Image: X

A devastating wildfire has destroyed 24 homes and burned through nearly 25 000 hectares in the Western Cape’s Overberg region, leaving firefighters racing to contain the remaining flames.

The fire broke out in the De Hoop Nature Reserve area on Thursday, 19 November, before spreading towards Potberg and Malgas, near Swellendam.

By Saturday evening, 21 November, authorities confirmed that 22 homes had been destroyed in the Riverine complex, one in Lemoentuin and another in the Potberg complex.



No injuries had been reported as of 21:00 on Saturday.

MALGAS FIRE DESTROYS 24 HOMES

According to the Greater Overberg Fire Protection Association, firefighters spent Saturday protecting homes, farms and infrastructure as the blaze spread through the area.

The situation worsened on Saturday afternoon when flames swept through dense vegetation and reached the Riverine complex.



Overberg District Municipality fire chief Reinard Geldenhuys said the fire reached the residential area at approximately 16:00.

Speaking during an earlier update, Geldenhuys said 15 houses were burning while crews desperately tried to protect neighbouring properties.

“We still have vehicles trying to protect the rest of the houses,” he said.



The number of destroyed homes subsequently rose to 24.

The Overberg District Municipality urged residents to follow evacuation instructions and keep roads clear for emergency vehicles.

FIREFIGHTERS BATTLE TO CONTAIN BLAZE

By 21:00 on Saturday, the fire had affected approximately 25 000 hectares.



Firefighters focused on containing the blaze near the Malgas–Infanta Road to prevent further destruction.

Geldenhuys said the head of the fire was approximately 5km from Infanta, on the southern side of the road.

“The objective for tonight is to close the head of the fire,” he said.



According to SABC News, most fire lines had been contained by Saturday evening, although crews still faced active areas requiring attention.

Firefighters planned to continue operations through the night, particularly along the northern and eastern sections of the fire.

DE HOOP NATURE RESERVE FIRE REMAINS A CONCERN

CapeNature warned that shifting winds and extensive vegetation had complicated efforts to bring the blaze under control.



The fire also threatened agricultural land near Potberg Mountain.

Firefighting teams from the Overberg District Municipality, CapeNature, the Greater Overberg Fire Protection Association and Volunteer Wildfire Services joined forces to prevent further damage.

Working on Fire crews, landowners and volunteers also assisted.



Authorities urged motorists to avoid unnecessary travel in affected areas while emergency teams continued their operations.

The full extent of the damage and the fire’s containment status on Sunday morning remained subject to further official updates.

World.title: Retired SASSA pensioner wants to work again for one simple reason
World.content:
A retired pensioner in the Western Cape says his SASSA grant no longer stretches far enough. He now wants to return to work to keep his household afloat.

The grant recipient, who is over 65 and asked to remain anonymous, receives the Older Persons Grant of R2 400 a month. He has collected the grant for more than five years, with payments going straight into his Capitec Bank account.

SASSA pensioner says R2 400 runs out before month-end

The pensioner owns his home, but that has not shielded him from rising prices. He told The South African that his grant does not cover his basic needs and that he regularly struggles to make ends meet.



By the end of each month, the money is gone. He spreads it across a mix of household expenses, and one or two people depend on his income.

His biggest financial worry is the cost of living and rising food prices. Asked what one thing he would change about SASSA, he chose an increase in the grant amount.

Despite the pressure, he said nobody in his household went without food in the past month.

Retired grant recipient eyes admin work close to home

The squeeze has pushed the pensioner to look at the job market again. He listed administrative and office work as the type of work he is looking for or has experience in.

He can only travel under five kilometres for work, so any job would need to be close to home.

His story reflects a growing reality for older South Africans, for whom retirement no longer guarantees financial rest. For many, a fixed monthly grant cannot keep pace with grocery, transport and utility costs.



Pensioners who take on paid work should keep in mind that SASSA applies a means test, so additional income could affect their grant eligibility.

Pensioner unaware of other government support

The grant recipient has never applied for any government support beyond his pension. He said he did not know what else was available.

He rated SASSA’s communication with recipients as very good and said he has never had a problem with his grant. Still, his experience shows that smooth payments do not always mean recipients know about every support option open to them.

Win R2 000 in the South African SASSA grant survey

If you receive a SASSA grant and want to share your story, we want to hear from you.

Take part in our survey and stand a chance to win R2 000. Your responses help us tell the stories that matter.

World.title: Carte Blanche coming up: Justice at last
World.content:
The Sunday, 22 November episode of Carte Blanche delves into the painstaking investigation of a rape case that remained unresolved for years, highlighting how one determined detective eventually brought the perpetrator to justice.

Despite the preservation of a rape kit, the case had gone cold, leaving the survivor without answers for years.

However, a major breakthrough reignited the investigation, with the detective’s relentless efforts ultimately helping to identify the rapist and secure justice in a case that had long appeared to have reached a dead end.

World.title: Family searching for Mathibestad granny who went missing on Durban trip
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The family of an elderly woman are in desperate search after she went missing in Durban on Monday.

Selinah Boiyane Peete (84) from Mathibestad near Hammanskraal was part of a group of elderly women who regularly play soccer together.

The group, that had been visiting Durban, went to the beach before checking into the Albany Hotel.

Peete is said to have disappeared between getting off the bus and reaching the hotel.

A missing person's case has been opened with the Durban Central Police. However, there has been no breakthrough as yet.

Her grandson and a councillor from Moretele Local Municipality have since travelled to Durban, to join the search party.

World.title: Summer rains temporary relief as SA farmers brace themselves for drought
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - South Africa has over the past few weeks been experiencing rainy weather that is bringing much needed relief to the country's farmers.

According to Agbiz Chief economist, Wandile Sihlobo, despite this, there is still a risk of a drought.

Improved soil moisture and grazing conditions do not necessarily mean the drought threat has passed.

Sihlobo says while some areas might have experience flooding, which might many farmers think the country is out of the woods. The data shows that South Africa will experience a delayed drought.

World.title: DA, ActionSA failing to find each other
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Democratic Alliance leader Geordin Hill-Lewis has accused ActionSA leader Herman Mashaba of trying to justify his U-turn on working with the ANC.

The DA has made what it has called its full and final offer to ActionSA. The offer includes offering Tshwane in exchange for Johannesburg and Ekurhuleni.

This will mean that Nasiphi Moya remains mayor of the Tshwane if elected by council.

Mashaba, however, has rejected the proposal, saying it does not deserve a response.

Hill-Lewis insists that compromises are necessary, describing the offer as reasonable.

"He has to find a way to justify his betrayal to the voters wishes," Hill-Lewis says about Mashaba.

World.title: Fossil fuels still missing from latest COP31 draft deal
World.content:
The COP31 presidency proposed an eleventh-hour deal Sunday that again fails to mention fossil fuels -- an omission that deepened a tense standoff at the UN climate talks.

The latest offering by summit co-hosts Turkey and Australia published deep into overtime leaves unresolved tensions over planet-heating fossil fuels but retains a much-sought goal to electrify the global economy.

The proposal needs consensus approval from nearly 200 nations at a closing session Sunday but they have struggled to bridge differences during two weeks of grinding negotiations.

The European Union and other nations have pushed for strong language on transitioning away from fossil fuels, a call that has faced resistance from oil-rich Saudi Arabia.

An EU official told AFP the latest proposal was a "backwards" step, warning there was a "very real possibility" that COP31 ends with no deal.

"I am more pessimistic today than I was yesterday," the official said on condition of anonymity.

"The situation is difficult, and the outcome is uncertain. The oil-producing countries are putting up a fierce fight," a German official said.

A Saudi official declined to comment when approached by AFP.

Fossil fuels are a flashpoint at the climate talks and the summit comes against a difficult backdrop of soaring energy prices and geopolitical tensions stemming from the war in Iran.

A draft deal unveiled earlier this week called for a faster phase out of fossil fuels but a second, pared-down version released Thursday stripped away all mentions of coal, oil and gas.

Threats of a walkout prompted Turkey and Australia to convene a hurried meeting between the European Union and Saudi Arabia in a bid to broker a compromise.

The latest text introduces a reference to a previous global deal in 2023 to shift the world away from fossil fuels -- but stops short of naming them explicitly.

And it retains a contentious push to expand carbon capture and storage, a technology championed by the fossil fuel industry but criticised as costly and ineffective in cutting emissions.

"We are very disappointed with how the text looks," the environment minister of Antigua and Barbuda, Michael Joseph, told AFP after leaving the COP31 presidency's offices.

"I can't honestly say that I'm okay with it passing" in its current state, Joseph said, adding that the draft was "quite silent" on fossil fuels.

- Goal to electrify -

The draft also calls for global efforts to boost the share of electricity in total final energy consumption to 35 percent by 2035 and the expansion of "clean energy".

The summit had been under pressure to show progress in tackling soaring greenhouse gas emissions in a year of climate-linked disasters from Europe to Nepal and Indonesia.

Facing blowback over fossil fuels, Turkey and Australia pointed to "electrification" as a way to cut heat-trapping emissions and bolster energy security.

This works by replacing technologies that burn fossil fuels directly -- like diesel cars and gas heating -- with electric alternatives.

But some nations had demanded an explicitly "clean" target to ensure the electrification push was powered by renewable energy and not fossil fuels.

Around one-third of global electricity is produced using coal and another fifth using fossil gas.

Attempts by Saudi Arabia, India and Kenya meanwhile to delay the next set of reports by the UN's Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) have been another major source of friction at the talks.

The draft text "highlights the importance" of these reports for an upcoming stocktake of global carbon-cutting efforts in 2028.

Dozens of countries across Europe, Africa and the Pacific want these assessments by the global scientific authority on climate change published in time for that crucial stocktake.

Countries have also disagreed at COP31 over how to respond to the looming breach of the 1.5C warming target set under the Paris climate accord.

The latest draft expressed "deep concern" that global warming would cross 1.5C above pre-industrial levels in the next few years.

The talks also jammed over long-running complaints that rich nations are shirking their obligations to help developing nations confront climate change.

The removal of a $120 billion target for climate adaptation angered developing nations.

By Laurent Thomet, Nick Perry And Fulya Ozerkan

World.title: New Zealand reach 119-2 to trail by 233 after India's record 720-9
World.content:
New Zealand were 119-2 at stumps on day four of the first Test Sunday, still needing 233 to make India bat again after they declared earlier on a record 720-9 .

Devon Conway was unbeaten on 59 and Rachina Ravindra was 27 at the close of play.

India scored the highest innings total in Test matches in New Zealand earlier, declaring at a mammoth 720-9 midway through the fourth afternoon.

India surpassed the previous record for Tests in New Zealand, the hosts' 715-6 declared against Bangladesh in Hamilton in 2019.

It was also India's record score in an overseas Test and the 18th highest innings in Test history.

Rishabh Pant, who resumed on 55, made 128 before falling to the last ball before lunch as India reached the break on 629-6.

The diminutive wicketkeeper brought up his hundred by lofting Glenn Phillips over long-off for six, before kissing the badge of his helmet and pointing to the sky.

It was his ninth hundred in Test cricket, and included 10 fours and six sixes.

Dhruv Jurel was the last man out, stumped from the bowling of Glenn Phillips for a brisk 78 off 79 balls.

Kamboj took on the role of aggressor at the start of play with a flurry of lofted drives and outright slogs.

He fell for a swift 38 from 42 balls, hitting six fours and a six.

Pant then opened up and whacked Phillips out of the Basin Reserve ground, the ball seen running down neighbouring Cambridge Terrace alongside the Sunday morning traffic.

In reply New Zealand lost Tom Latham second ball without scoring, a dreaded "pair" for the captain after he was also dismissed by Bumrah in the first innings.

Nicholls, who made 175 not out in the first innings, fell for 31 after an edge onto his pads ballooned to a diving Jurel at short leg.

Conway and Ravindra then combined for an unbroken 59-run partnership to guide the team to stumps.

India set creative fields in an attempt to pry the partnership apart, using a variety of close catchers and leg side lines, while also throwing the ball to Devdutt Padikkal in an attempt to surprise the batsmen.

New Zealand's Ravindra took 2-44 with the ball from 10 overs during India's innings, while Glenn Phillips had 3-154.

Seamer Jacob Duffy conceded the second most runs in an innings by a bowler in New Zealand Test history, returning 1-201 from 33 overs.

Each of India's top five batsmen had scores of 80 or higher, the first time that has happened in a Test.

KL Rahul made 136 opening the batting alongside Yashasvi Jaiswal, who made 85, Devdutt Padikkal scored 80 and Shubman Gill 98 before Pant's century.

World.title: Four killed in Khayelitsha tavern shooting
World.content:
CAPE TOWN - Western Cape are searching for gunmen who stormed a tavern in Khayelitsha on Saturday.

They opened fire, killing four men and wounding five others inside the tavern.

The gunmen fled the scene in a hijacked vehicle that was found abandoned a few kilometres from the crime scene.

A case of murder and attempted murder has been opened. While no arrests have been made, there motive of the shooting is still unknown.

World.title: Messi furore after Columbus thrash Miami in MLS Cup
World.content:
Columbus Crew coach Laurent Courtois said Lionel Messi should have been sent off after hurling a throw-in at an opponent as Inter Miami crashed to a 3-0 defeat in the MLS Cup playoffs on Saturday.

Messi's frustration boiled over on the stroke of half-time when he aimed a forceful throw-in into the face of Columbus Crew forward Gonzalo Tapia with 10-man Miami trailing 1-0 at the time.

Messi and Tapia both were shown yellow cards for the incident by referee Allen Chapman, but Courtois said afterwards the Argentina superstar should have been given a red card.

"Everybody knows that he deserved more than a yellow card," Courtois said in a post-game press conference when asked about the incident. "It's just really sad."

Referee Chapman later defended the decision to only show Messi a yellow.

"The force used was negligible and the offense did not reach the level of violent conduct," Chapman told a pool reporter.

Inter Miami had already been reduced to 10 men when the incident occurred and were 1-0 down after Chile international Tapia's early penalty.

Reigning MLS champions Miami went on to suffer a 3-0 defeat, with Tapia grabbing a second after a Taha Habroune strike just after half-time at Miami's Nu Stadium.

The result means seventh seeds Columbus, the 2023 champions, can eliminate Messi and Miami from the playoffs with a victory in game two of the best-of-three series in Ohio next Friday.

"It was a game where nothing went right for us, and we effectively created their chances for them," Miami coach Kily Gonzalez said afterwards.

"We didn't produce the great performance we had hoped for. Everything went wrong, but we have to learn from it because next time, if we don't win, we're out," he added.

"There's no better challenge for us as a team than this. It's a test of character, and I know my team has that character."

In other MLS playoff action on Saturday, Joaquin Valiente scored two goals as host Dallas beat Portland 3-0 in their Western Conference series opener.

The 25-year-old Uruguayan midfielder scored in the 53rd and 55th minutes and Samuel Sarver added an insurance goal in the fourth minute of stoppage time for Dallas, who can advance by winning at Portland next Saturday.

US teen Peyton Miller scored one goal and set up another in New England's 2-0 victory over visiting Philadelphia.

Miller’s 10th-minute shot deflected in off Philadelphia defender Nathan Harriel to make it 1-0 and the 19-year-old scored in the 73rd minute off a Jack Harrison cross to complete the scoring.

New England can advance to the MLS Eastern Conference semi-finals with a road victory next Saturday.

World.title: Three dead, 36 missing after Indonesia factory fire
World.content:
A fire at a confectionery factory west of Jakarta killed three people and 36 remain missing, an Indonesian rescue official said on Sunday.

Drone footage showed large parts of the factory destroyed, with the roof collapsed in places and smoke still rising from the complex.

Photos and videos shared by rescuers also showed officers entering the charred building in search of the missing victims, with small fires still burning in some spots.

Relatives of the missing victims flocked near the factory's entrance, seeking updates about their loved ones, footage aired by local broadcasters showed.

The Fonusa Agung Mulia factory, located in the Serang district around 50 kilometres (31 miles) from the capital, caught fire on Saturday afternoon, local search and rescue agency official Rizky Dwianto said.

"All elements of the joint SAR (search-and-rescue) team are making maximum effort to locate the victims while prioritising the safety of personnel in the field," he added.

Rizky said four people were injured and taken to a nearby hospital and health clinic.

Firefighters were alerted around 4.30 pm (0930 GMT) on Saturday and found the building already engulfed in flames when they arrived, fire official Tubagus Machfudz told local broadcaster Kompas TV.

"When we arrived (on location)... a large area was already on fire. So we could not determine whether the company's protection system was functioning properly or not," he said.

Banten province governor Andra Soni told reporters overnight that an estimated 60 people were inside the factory when it caught fire.

Confectionery maker Fonusa Agung Mulia describes itself on the professional networking platform LinkedIn as a subsidiary of UNIFAM, one of the Southeast Asian nation's major consumer-food companies.

The cause of the incident is still under investigation, the local disaster agency said in an Instagram post on Sunday.

Deadly fires are not uncommon in Indonesia.

In December last year, a blaze that was likely caused by a drone battery explosion tore through a seven-storey building in Jakarta and killed at least 22 people, police said.

In 2023, at least 13 people were killed in the country's east after an explosion at a nickel-processing plant.

World.title: From web of court battles to internal wrangles and political mistrust: Inside IEBC's numbing reality
World.content:
IEBC chairperson Erastus Ethekon. [Elvis Ogina, Standard]

Stakes in the 2027 elections could not have been higher; however, nothing seems to be working in that direction. At least, going by the bickering from politicians, the court cases and the stalled tendering process.

Stakeholders in the electoral process have raised concerns over the ability of the Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC) to conduct credible polls next year, citing shrinking timelines and the numerous challenges facing the commission.

World.title: Narok Senator under fire after threatening to shoot auctioneers in Sh1.2m dispute
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Narok Senator Ledama ole Kina is at the centre of a national uproar after a viral video captured him threatening to shoot individuals during a volatile confrontation involving auctioneers and a former Senate office employee.

The dramatic standoff erupted when court-backed agents attempted to seize a milk delivery truck over an unresolved legal dispute and has since ignited intense public debate regarding political accountability and the rule of law.

The controversy surrounds long court battle after Zakayo Rotiken, who served sacked as Narok North Constituency Coordinator between 2017 and 2020, was sacked.

According to records, the claimant was illegally dismissed amidst unpaid salary arrears.

On October 31, 2023, the Employment and Labour Relations Court ruled in Rotiken's favour , a decision that was subsequently upheld when the Senator lost his appeal.

With accrued interest, the court decree now stands at Sh 1.2 million.

Consequently, when the debt remained unsatisfied, licensed auctioneers moved in to execute lawful warrants which in turn provoked a furious reaction from Senator Ole Kina, who fiercely framed the entire episode as a political witch-hunt.

The lawmaker argued that Rotiken was hired by the Narok Senate office rather than his personal capacity, maintaining that any resultant liabilities ought to be handled by the Parliamentary Service Commission (PSC) rather than attaching his private property.

Defending his harsh words in the widely circulated footage, the senator dismissed the agents as trespassers and asserted action against them.

"Anybody who trespasses will get a bullet in their head or leg because that is trespass," said Ole Kina.

“Nitakupiga Risasi!” Senator Ledama Ole Kina embroiled in confrontation with alleged auctioneers over unpaid car loan https://t.co/k4OSXpNsdi November 21, 2026

The claimant's legal team condemned the threats made against statutory court officers emphasizing that a court judgment is an enforceable command rather than a mere suggestion, calling upon the Inspector General of Police of Police and the Director of Criminal Investigatons to urgently investigate the alleged death threats.

Rotiken noted that he merely sought justice through proper judicial channels and should not be penalized or intimidated for pursuing his lawful entitlements.

"When I was illegally dismissed with unpaid salary arrears, I did not resort to violence or politics—I went to the Employment and Labour Relations Court. Nobody is above the law, and I appeal to the police to protect the officers doing their job so that justice can finally be served," he said.

Ultimately, as pressure mounts on security agencies to look into the firearm threats, the unfolding saga highlights a tense intersection between public office obligations and the absolute sanctity of judicial decrees.

While the senator maintains that his assets were unjustly targeted by political rivals, legal experts and the public continue to demand that the rule of law must prevail without exception.

World.title: Ruto defends IEBC, challenges rivals to present alternative policies
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

President William Ruto during his tour of the Western region. [PCS]

President William Ruto has launched a scathing attack on opposition leaders over their demands on the Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC), accusing them of attempting to interfere with the electoral agency because they fear losing the 2027 General Election.

The President challenged opposition leaders to allow IEBC to prepare independently for next year's elections, saying they should instead focus on identifying their presidential candidate, developing a manifesto and presenting alternative policies to Kenyans.

Ruto accused his competitors of attempting to play the roles of both contestants and referees by seeking to influence decisions on the procurement of election materials and equipment.

He spoke a day after opposition leaders walked out of a meeting convened by IEBC, alleging bias by the commission.

“Please give IEBC a chance to arrange the elections next year. The people of Kenya will decide. You go and first look for your candidate, find your policies, agenda and plans and sell them to the wananchi. We shall meet at the ballot,” said Ruto.

Speaking during his development tour of Western Kenya, Ruto questioned why opposition politicians were concentrating on determining how IEBC should procure election materials instead of preparing to face voters.

“How can somebody who is in a competition want to decide where the pitch will be, who the referee will be and where the ball will be placed? Leave IEBC alone. Those who will vote are the citizens, and they are the ones who will decide,” he said.

The President accused his opponents of lacking a clear political agenda and capacity to deliver, claiming their campaigns were centred on slogans and personal attacks against him.

He challenged them to explain what they would do differently in agriculture, education, healthcare, infrastructure and employment rather than mobilising Kenyans around the slogan 'Kasongo Must Go'.

“The reason why my competitors cannot develop a plan is that they have no capacity. The reason why they have no agenda is that they have no knowledge. The reason why they cannot develop anything is that they know they have no capacity to deliver on anything that they will say,” he said.

His remarks were echoed by Kakamega Governor Fernandes Barasa and National Assembly Speaker Moses Wetang'ula, who rallied Western Kenya leaders behind his re-election bid and defended IEBC against what they termed unnecessary political pressure. President William Ruto during his tour of the Western region. [ Benjamin Sakwa, Standard]

Speaking in Butere, Barasa said the region's political leadership, including Prime Cabinet Secretary Musalia Mudavadi, Cabinet Secretary Wycliffe Oparanya, Wetang'ula and trade unionist Francis Atwoli, was united behind Ruto's development agenda.

“IEBC will conduct the elections according to the law. Opposition leaders should leave IEBC alone and allow it to do its work,” he said.

Wetang'ula maintained that IEBC was independent of both the government and the opposition and should be allowed to conduct its work without interference.

“IEBC is independent of the government and independent of the Opposition. You stand there to do your work fairly, truthfully and equally,” he said.

He added: “Just as Arsenal supporters cannot dictate what uniform the referee should wear, the referee's responsibility is to ensure the game is played fairly and the winner emerges through a legitimate process.”

The exchanges underline the growing political contest over the management of the 2027 elections, with the government side accusing the opposition of undermining the electoral agency before campaigns gather momentum.

Beyond the political exchanges, Ruto used his Western Kenya tour to highlight development projects, saying his administration was committed to correcting years of neglect and unequal distribution of national resources.

He also announced plans for a second phase of the Nyota programme targeting an additional 200,000 young people, each expected to receive Sh50,000 to establish or expand businesses.

The government is also targeting 100,000 college graduates for internships from January, with each expected to receive a monthly stipend of Sh20,000.

Ruto's tour comes amid growing competition for Western Kenya's support ahead of the 2027 General Election, with emerging opposition alliances seeking to challenge his influence.

World.title: Ruto sustains attacks on Gachagua, dares Opposition to name 2027 flagbearer
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

President William Ruto launches Matisi-Bokoli-Milani-Teremi road in Webuye West on November 19, 2026. [Benjamin Sakwa, Standard]

President William Ruto has challenged Opposition leaders to name their presidential candidate and unveil a clear political agenda, accusing them of wasting time hopping from one hotel to another and holding meetings in private residences in search of a flagbearer and campaign manifesto.

The President said the Opposition was yet to settle on a flagbearer or agree on a common agenda despite the clock ticking towards the 2027 General Election.

He dismissed the rival camps' political engagements as endless consultations and manoeuvres, arguing that their leaders were more preoccupied with political meetings than developing policies to convince Kenyans.

Speaking in Bungoma during his development tour of Western Kenya, Ruto challenged his opponents to stop what he termed political confusion and present an alternative development agenda, insisting he was ready to face them in the 2027 contest.

"These people do not have a candidate. They are struggling, moving from one hotel to another and from one person's house to another, trying to find an agenda and a manifesto before they can start campaigning. Time is running out, yet they are still struggling to agree on an agenda," he said.

Ruto also launched a fresh attack on former Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua, accusing him of promoting tribalism and hatred while questioning his remarks about relocating to Texas, United States.

The President mockingly referred to Gachagua as "Mr Chuki wa Texas", questioning why he would allegedly acquire a house in the US while engaging in politics that could divide Kenyans and fuel hostility.

"Mr Chuki wa Texas has gone to buy a house in Texas. He wants to know whether he will flee our country after spreading tribalism and hatred, dividing people and turning them against each other, before boarding a plane to Texas and leaving others to deal with the consequences," Ruto said.

He accused the former Deputy President of attempting to turn communities against one another for political gain, warning that he would not allow anyone to undermine national unity through ethnic mobilisation.

Ruto said he was ready to confront his political opponents directly but insisted that political competition should not become an avenue for spreading hatred and inciting Kenyans against one another.

The President also questioned Gachagua's allies over their reported visit to the Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC) offices in Kizirani, accusing the Opposition of picking unnecessary fights with the electoral agency ahead of the 2027 General Election.

He suggested that politicians who begin questioning the electoral commission before elections could be preparing grounds to reject the results should they lose.

"Whenever you see someone picking a fight with IEBC, that person is already looking for an excuse to fail. Now they are coming up with all sorts of excuses, asking whether it is IEBC that votes. Is IEBC responsible for the votes?" He posed.

Ruto urged politicians to stop harassing the electoral agency, maintaining that the power to elect leaders rests with Kenyans and not the commission.

"I want to tell Kenyans to stop harassing IEBC. IEBC does not have votes. The votes belong to the people of Kenya," he said.

The President maintained that his administration was focused on delivering development, challenging the Opposition to explain its alternative plans on electricity connectivity, education, healthcare and infrastructure.

He questioned what the Opposition considered its development agenda, dismissing what he described as recycled political slogans and simplistic promises.

The President particularly took issue with promises centred on providing porridge to Kenyans, questioning whether such pledges could constitute a credible national development agenda.

He urged voters to interrogate the policies and development track records of politicians seeking their support instead of being swayed by political rhetoric and personal attacks.

The latest attack marks an escalation in political exchanges between Ruto and his rivals as competing camps intensify mobilisation ahead of the 2027 General Election.

It also comes amid efforts by Gachagua and other Opposition figures to consolidate their political formations and build a formidable challenge to Ruto's re-election bid, with Western Kenya emerging as a key battleground.

World.title: Ruto lists measures to lower cost of living, put more money in Kenyans' pockets
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

President William Ruto during his State Of The Nation Address at Parliament, Nairobi. November 18th, 2026. [Elvis Ogina, Standard]

President William Ruto has outlined a raft of government interventions aimed at reducing the cost of living, increasing household incomes and creating more employment opportunities for Kenyans.

Addressing Parliament during the 2026 State of the Nation Address on Wednesday, Ruto said his administration had prioritised lowering the cost of essential goods and services while increasing earnings across key sectors of the economy.

“Our economic proposition was simple: Reduce the cost for families and increase the income from what they do,” he said.

On food prices, the President cited the government’s fertiliser subsidy programme, which has reduced the price of a 50-kilogramme bag of fertiliser from Sh7,500 in 2022 to Sh2,000 this year.

He said the government had distributed 38.5 million bags of subsidised fertiliser to farmers, contributing to an increase in maize production from 44.3 million bags in 2022 to 71 million bags last year.

Consequently, maize imports declined from 9.9 million bags to 3.3 million bags, while the average price of a two-kilogramme packet of sifted maize flour dropped from a high of Sh230 in September 2022 to Sh152 in September this year.

Ruto also highlighted gains in the tea, coffee, dairy and sugar industries, saying government interventions had helped improve production and increase farmers' earnings.

He said the Cherry Advance Revolving Fund had disbursed Sh15.07 billion to 684,000 coffee farmers, while tea export earnings increased from Sh163 billion in 2022 to Sh187 billion in 2025.

In the dairy sector, milk production rose from 4.5 billion litres to 5.52 billion litres, while average earnings for farmers increased from Sh32 to Sh60 per litre last month.

Sugar production, he added, increased by 60 per cent between January and October, with cane crushing rising by 57 per cent. The industry is projected to produce more than 900,000 tonnes by the end of the year, with Sh1.2 billion in bonuses expected to be paid to sugarcane farmers.

On healthcare, Ruto said the Social Health Authority (SHA) was designed to ease the financial burden of medical expenses on households through a shared health financing system.

In education, he said the government had employed 100,000 teachers and was preparing to recruit an additional 20,000 to address staffing shortages and reduce the burden on parents who pay teachers hired through Boards of Management.

He added that 23,000 classrooms had been constructed, while 1,600 laboratories were being built and equipped.

The President said the annual education allocation had increased from Sh521 billion in the 2022/23 financial year to Sh784 billion in the current financial year.

"These investments improve the quality of education while progressively reducing the need for Kenyans to finance education," he said.

On affordable housing, Ruto said more than 313,000 homes were at different stages of construction across the 47 counties, with over 1.37 million Kenyans registered on the Boma Yangu platform and more than 18,000 homes already allocated.

He said households could work towards homeownership through monthly payments starting at Sh4,000, which he argued would help ease the burden of rent.

The housing programme, according to the President, had also generated more than 1.1 million employment opportunities and reserved orders worth over Sh61 billion for Jua Kali artisans.

On employment, Ruto said 350,000 Kenyans had secured jobs through the digital economy programme, while another 707,000 had obtained employment abroad through international labour mobility initiatives.

He also cited the Hustler Fund, saying more than seven million Kenyans had established credit records through the programme, with cumulative borrowing reaching Sh94 billion.

Under the NYOTA programme, more than 133,000 young entrepreneurs had received training, mentorship and Sh50,000 each in start-up capital, he said.

The President further announced proposed tax measures aimed at increasing disposable incomes, including exempting workers earning Sh32,333 or less per month from Pay As You Earn (PAYE).

Other proposals include scrapping stamp duty on land transactions valued at Sh1 million or less and removing the 25 per cent import duty on mobile phones.

On pending bills, Ruto said the government had approved the settlement of 28,726 verified claims amounting to Sh27.8 billion, covering debts of Sh50 million and below dating back to 2005.

He added that Sh18 billion owed to public universities and another Sh16 billion owed to public and private hospitals under the former National Hospital Insurance Fund (NHIF) had been approved for payment and were undergoing Treasury processing.

“These are not isolated interventions, but parts of one comprehensive undertaking,” Ruto said.

He maintained that the government's economic strategy was anchored on reducing household expenditure, increasing incomes and expanding opportunities for Kenyans.

World.title: After 22 years of waiting, woman welcomes quadruplet boys
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Samuel Langat speaks to journalists outside St Clare's Kaplong Mission hospital in Sotik Subcounty, Bomet county after his wife Lily Langat gave to quadruplets at the hospital. [Kiprono Kurgat, Standard]

After 22 years of waiting to become a mother, a woman has welcomed quadruplet boys in a rare and joyful birth that has brought immense happiness to her family.

Lily Langat delivered the quadruplets through a Caesarean section at St Clare’s Kaplong Mission Hospital in Sotik Sub-County on November 14, 2026.

The four boys arrived after more than two decades of waiting for a child in what the family described as a double blessing.

The 43-year-old mother could not hide her joy, saying the arrival of the four babies was an answer to years of prayer.

“I am very grateful to God for giving me four babies at once. This is a great blessing to my family. I thank the hospital staff for ensuring I got to see these bundles of joy,” she said.

“I have been praying and waiting upon God to give me double for the trouble. I have been childless for a long time, and God could not have given me a better gift than this,” she added.

She said she had been looking forward to the moment after doctors informed her early in the pregnancy that she could be carrying quadruplets.

Hospital staff celebrated the successful delivery, describing it as a rare occurrence at the facility.

A nurse who spoke with The Standard said the mother and her four newborns were in stable condition.

“We were delighted to deliver the babies. The mother faced some difficulties because of the combined weight of the four babies, but both she and the newborns are now stable,” she said.

The nurse said the babies had been placed in the nursery for observation and were doing well.

“This is a rare case in this hospital. We have had twins before, but this is different. None of the babies has developed complications so far, and we expect them to be discharged once they are fully stable,” she said.

She added that the mother was also recovering well and was expected to be discharged once doctors were satisfied with the condition of the newborns.

Lily's husband, Samuel Langat, appealed to well-wishers to support the family as they prepare to raise the four children.

“Raising four babies at once is no easy task. I am calling on well-wishers to lend a helping hand as we begin this extraordinary journey,” he said.

“Our four precious miracles have arrived safely, and while our hearts are overflowing with gratitude, the reality of caring for four newborns at once has brought challenges,” he added.

Naturally conceived quadruplets are extremely rare, although the likelihood varies depending on several factors, including maternal age and fertility treatment.

The birth marks a remarkable new beginning for the Langat family after 22 years of waiting for a child.

World.title: TSC picks Cheptumo Ayabei as new Chief Executive Officer
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Teachers Service Commission headquarters in Nairobi. [File, Standard]

The Teachers Service Commission (TSC) has picked Cheptumo Ayabei as its new Secretary and Chief Executive Officer, making him the first person with a disability to head the commission.

Ayabei emerged top in interviews conducted on Monday, beating four other candidates, including the commission’s acting chief executive, Dr Evaleen Jesang Mitei, to become the country’s top teachers’ employer.

His selection ends a prolonged search for a substantive head of the commission, which has operated under acting leadership since the departure of former CEO Nancy Macharia in June 2025.

Ayabei, who hails from Baringo County, is currently TSC’s Director of Finance, having served at the commission for more than two decades. He joined the institution in 1999 as a Finance Officer before rising through the ranks to become Director of Finance in 2009.

His elevation marks a significant milestone for the representation of persons with disabilities in the country’s public institutions.

Ayabei was the first candidate to face the selection panel at 9am at the commission’s headquarters in Upper Hill, Nairobi. He was followed by Mitei at 10am, Robert Odette at 11am, Lawrence Ngai Kaburu at noon and Farah Abdi Saman at 1pm.

The five candidates were shortlisted from 124 applicants who responded to a fresh  issued on September 29. Applications closed on October 30.

Ayabei holds a Bachelor of Education degree in Mathematics and Economics from Kenyatta University and a Master’s degree in Finance and Banking from the University of Stirling in the United Kingdom. He is also a Certified Public Accountant.

Before joining TSC, he worked at the Ministry of Education between 1990 and 1999.

He takes over at a critical time for the commission, which oversees the employment, deployment, promotion and discipline of teachers across the country. He will inherit mounting pressure over teacher shortages, recruitment, promotions, transfers and the management of the teaching workforce.

The recruitment process had faced legal challenges, with a petition filed at the Employment and Labour Relations Court in Kisii seeking to halt the exercise.

The case, filed by Evans Morara Nyangongo under Cause E038 of 2026, challenged the fresh recruitment and raised questions about Mitei’s participation in the process while serving as acting CEO and seeking the substantive position.

Nyangongo sought to stop the commission from proceeding with the appointment until the issues raised in the petition were determined.

However, the court dismissed both the application and the suit, with no orders as to costs, clearing the way for the interviews.

In its defence, TSC maintained that the decision to advertise the position had been made collectively by the commission’s board and not by the acting CEO.

In a replying affidavit, TSC chairman Jamleck Muturi John maintained that Mitei had neither participated in the board’s deliberations on the recruitment nor influenced the process.

The fresh recruitment followed an earlier court decision that nullified the previous exercise over procedural irregularities, forcing the commission to restart the search for a substantive chief executive.

World.title: Thwake Dam project reaches 94pc completion
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Thwake Multipurpose Dam, which is 94.2 per cent complete, with the government targeting April 2027 for water impoundment.[File,Standard]

Thwake Dam is 94.2 per cent complete, with the government targeting April 2027 for water impoundment as residents seek a review of alleged construction-related damage claims.

Principal Secretary for Water and Sanitation Julius Korir told the National Assembly Departmental Committee on Blue Economy, Water and Irrigation that construction had reached 94.2 per cent.

The dam is being built at the confluence of the Athi and Thwake rivers along the Makueni-Kitui border. It is designed to provide water for domestic use, irrigation and electricity generation.

Martin Kimeu, a resident of Wote, said the project would improve access to water for farming in the region.

“Ukambani is fertile. Water has been the biggest impediment to the realization of our agricultural potential. Thwake Dam water is the clear solution to this,” he said.

Kimeu also defended the compensation process, saying he had followed the project since its inception and believed the exercise had been conducted properly.

Jacob Mwanzia, a resident of Madangi Village, said households in his area had been assessed and compensated. He argued that outstanding complaints should be addressed without delaying the project.

Mariam Mwikali, another resident, said assessments had been conducted on affected properties and residents given an opportunity to raise concerns.

However, some households have complained that construction-related blasting damaged their homes. Residents have reported cracks in walls, windows and foundations as well as dust, noise and ground vibrations.

In August 2026, residents from villages in Mavindini Ward, organised under the Thwake Dam Blasting-Affected Community Committee, sought an independent review by the African Development Bank (AfDB).

The residents alleged that some properties had been left out of assessments and compensation. They also sought access to assessment reports, photographs, measurements, valuation records and estimates for repairs or reconstruction.

A project official said the dam's safety department invited competitive bids for an independent assessment of properties potentially affected by blasting. Agile Consulting was selected to conduct the exercise.

The official said the consultant assessed 330 households within a two-kilometre radius of the construction site and submitted its report to the project implementation team. A large proportion of those assessed were satisfied with the exercise, the official added, without giving a breakdown.

Ben Mwongela, a director at Agile Consulting, said the assessment reviewed blasting records, vibration data and compliance with regulatory standards.

The exercise also involved documenting households, classifying structural defects and preparing bills of quantities and cost estimates for repairs or reconstruction, he said.

The AfDB conducted a field mission to the project between September 21 and 25, with its report published on October 21, 2026.

The bank's team, led by project task manager Nancy Ogal, met residents whose homes had been affected by blasting and identified outstanding health, safety, environmental and social issues, including homeowner grievances.

The bank called for timely compensation and continued monitoring of the project's environmental and social performance.

During a stakeholder engagement visit to Mavindini in October, Korir said the government had secured additional funding after the project experienced cash-flow constraints.

“When we ran short of cash, we engaged with our development partners, and they allocated additional funding, and this money will now go towards total completion of the project,” he said.

In June 2026, the AfDB approved additional financing of €68.39 million to support completion of the first phase, alongside funding from the Kenyan government.

The bank said the financing would support engineering refinements and safety works, including strengthening foundations, raising the dam and constructing two additional saddle dams.

The project has four phases. The first involves construction of the dam, while the subsequent phases cover hydropower generation, water supply and sanitation infrastructure, and irrigation.

The dam is approximately 80.5 metres high and has a planned storage capacity of 688 million cubic metres.

Once the water supply component is operational, the project is expected to provide 150,000 cubic metres of treated water daily to an estimated 1.3 million people in Makueni and Kitui counties and Konza Technopolis in Machakos County.

The irrigation scheme is designed to cover 40,000 hectares, equivalent to about 100,000 acres of agricultural land.

The project is also designed to generate 20 megawatts of hydropower.

The water supply, irrigation and hydropower components require infrastructure beyond the dam structure, including treatment and distribution networks and power generation facilities.

World.title: Russian ‘triple-tap’ attack in Ukraine kills emergency worker and 7-year-old in Zelensky’s home city
World.content:
A seven-year-old boy and a 20-year-old paramedic were killed Friday night in a Russian “triple-tap” strike on the Ukrainian city of Kryvyi Rih, according to local authorities.

In the attack on the home city of Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, ballistic missiles hit a restaurant parking lot, then jet-powered drones struck rescue workers responding, city mayor Oleksandr Vilkul said. A third drone strike hit the location for a short time later.

This latest Russian assault comes after a busy week of diplomacy, including an unprecedented meeting between US President Donald Trump, China’s Xi Jinping and Russia’s President Vladimir Putin. Trump described Putin as a “friend” when they met – but in a CNN interview after, Zelensky said “for us, he is a killer.”

Nearly 60 others including rescuers and police officers were injured in the initial strike and follow-up attacks, Vilkul said.

He described the events as a “tragic evening and a tragic night for our city,” adding that the attack occurred “in the city center, near a popular restaurant, on Children’s Day.” In Ukraine, Children’s Day falls on November 20 and serves as a reminder of the need to protect children’s rights and advocate for their safety.

Dramatic footage from authorities showed people moving away from debris strewn across the street, only to scramble for cover as the sound of another incoming strike rang out.

Of those wounded, 28 remain hospitalized, including a three-year-old girl. Five of the 28 are in intensive care.

“Doctors are doing everything necessary to save their lives. Our condolences go out to the families and loved ones of those who died… We pray for the swiftest possible recovery of the injured,” the mayor said.

Local broadcasting outlet Rudana named the seven-year-old boy who was killed in the Russian attack as Tikhon, describing him as kind, quick-witted and talented.

The boy’s family did not live in Kryvyi Rih, which is Zelensky’s hometown, but had been in the central Ukrainian city on business and decided to stop by their favorite restaurant, the outlet reported.

“We didn’t live here because it’s dangerous… but danger caught up with us,” the boy’s mother, Olena, told the outlet. According to the report, two of Olena’s other sons are in intensive care following the strike.

Zelensky said the attack on Friday night hit an ordinary civilian area of the city. “There are no military facilities nearby, and there never have been,” he said.

“Cities and villages in the Kharkiv, Donetsk, Dnipro, Rivne, Chernihiv, Mykolaiv, and Zaporizhzhia regions were also hit. In the Sumy region, a railway station came under attack,” the Ukrainian leader added.

Trump held talks with Putin and Xi at the APEC summit in Shenzhen, China, on Thursday, a meeting which was followed by a large “Coalition of the Willing” gathering in Berlin, attended by European leaders as well as US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner.

In a joint statement after the meeting, the group of key Ukrainian allies declared they were ready to join direct negotiations with Moscow, while German Chancellor Friedrich Merz stressed that Russia’s “maximalist demands are not realistic.”

Zelensky on Saturday described the three-way meeting between Putin, Trump and Xi as “very unsuccessful” for the Russian leader, who he said had failed in his goal of trying to recreate a Yalta-style conference at which Allied powers divided up the postwar world in 1945.

“China did not let itself be drawn in. As for the United States, I don’t know what went on between them and Russia in their bilateral talks, but Ukraine was not discussed. Nothing was said publicly,” Zelensky said in audio messages shared with journalists.

“So, the plan to redraw the world’s borders didn’t work out… I think the summit was a major failure for Russia.”

World.title: Ten years on, is the UK preparing to undo Brexit?
World.content:
Leaders from the United Kingdom and European Union have reached what’s been hailed as a “win-win” deal, in a summit held as British Prime Minister Andy Burnham pushes for a closer relationship with the bloc a decade after the Brexit vote.

A new package of agreements to create new opportunities for young people to live, study and travel on the continent, link emissions trading, and remove trade barriers on food products has been agreed, a UK government spokesperson told CNN on Friday.

Burnham welcomed the “landmark” deal, saying it draws a line “on a decade of drift and division by reconnecting with old friends.”

“We’re 10 years on from Brexit, but I think we can all confidently say this is a good day for Britain, and this is a good day for Europe. The agreement that we’ve reached together is a win-win,” he said at a news conference following the Brussels summit.

European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen set out a range of areas for further collaboration on economic security, defense capabilities, artificial intelligence and illegal immigration.

She said the deal marked a “turning point” in UK-EU relations, Britain’s Press Association news agency reported.

After Friday’s negotiations concluded, the UK government spokesperson said both sides would work toward the implementation of the schemes. The spokesperson added that talks would continue “on some areas,” alluding to key sticking points which remain.

Britain’s center-left Labour government inherited Brexit from its predecessors, the Conservative Party, and has long spoken of “resetting” ties with Brussels.
