World.title: Saudi Arabia signs 12 aviation deals at global conference in Montreal
World.content:
RIYADH: Saudi Arabia signed 12 aviation agreements and cooperation documents with international partners at a global air transport conference in Montreal, aimed at expanding international connectivity and strengthening the Kingdom’s aviation sector.

The deals were concluded during the 7th Worldwide Air Transport Conference, organised by the International Civil Aviation Organization from Nov. 16 to 20, according to the Saudi General Authority of Civil Aviation, as reported by the Saudi Press Agency.

These included bilateral air services agreements with Belize, Samoa, Cambodia and Jordan, as well as memorandums of understanding with Saint Lucia, Antigua and Barbuda, Montenegro, Cabo Verde and Turkiye. Saudi Arabia also signed records of discussion with Macao, Congo and Equatorial Guinea.

The agreements come as Saudi Arabia steps up investment in its aviation industry under Vision 2030, seeking to position the Kingdom as an international transit and logistics hub linking Asia, Europe and Africa.

The Saudi Aviation Strategy targets annual passenger traffic of 330 million, connectivity to more than 250 destinations and air cargo capacity of 4.5 million tonnes by 2030. The program is backed by an estimated $100 billion in government and private-sector investment across airports, airlines and aviation support services.

“The Kingdom achieved a number of outcomes, most notably the signing of 12 agreements, memoranda of understanding, and a record of discussions, the presentation of 8 working papers, and the holding of more than 32 bilateral meetings, in addition to organizing an exceptional edition of the Future of Aviation Conference,” the SPA report stated.

The Saudi delegation, led by GACA President Abdulaziz Al-Duailej, comprised 44 representatives from 18 national entities.

The working papers addressed economic regulation, sector resilience, investment, innovation and sustainable growth, reflecting the Kingdom’s priorities in shaping international aviation policy and strengthening cooperation with global industry stakeholders.

The delegation also met ICAO Council President Toshiyuki Onuma and Secretary-General Juan Carlos Salazar, alongside representatives of Airports Council International and aviation officials from several countries.

Discussions focused on regulatory cooperation, knowledge exchange and opportunities to develop the civil aviation sector.

Al-Duailej also chaired the eighth meeting of regional civil aviation organisations, in his capacity as chair of the Executive Council of the Arab Civil Aviation Organization.

During the conference, Syria and Lebanon formally submitted accession documents to join the Riyadh-based Middle East and North Africa Regional Safety Oversight Organization, bringing its membership to 10 countries.

The organisation aims to strengthen aviation safety oversight and cooperation among regional authorities.

GACA also hosted a special edition of its Future Aviation Forum on the sidelines of the conference in Montreal, bringing together industry leaders and policymakers ahead of the next forum, scheduled to take place in Riyadh on April 19-21, 2027.

World.title: Saudi Arabia condemns Iranian attack on civilian industrial facility in Bahrain
World.content:
RIYADH: Saudi Arabia on Sunday condemned Iranian attacks on a civilian industrial facility in Bahrain, expressing full solidarity with Manama.

The Foreign Ministry denounced the attacks and said the Kingdom supported all measures Bahrain takes to protect its security and stability.

World.title: Russian cargo ship still on fire off Finland after attack
World.content:
HELSINKI: A fire onboard ‌a Russian cargo ship that was struck by drones in the Baltic Sea continued to burn through the night even as efforts were made to douse the flames, Finland’s coast guard said on Sunday.

The Finnish military has said the strike on the Sparta II on Saturday was likely carried out by Ukraine and that the vessel later drifted into Finnish waters where it remains at anchor. The 16 crew ‌members were ‌evacuated onto a nearby Russian ship. Pictures ‌and video released by the coast guard showed several vessels spraying the Sparta II with water cannons during the night in a bid to put out the flames and cool down containers stacked on its deck.

Ukraine has sent waves of military drones toward Russia’s northwest coastal Leningrad region this year, including some that strayed ‌into the airspace of ‌nearby Baltic countries, leading to fears that the war was ‌spilling onto NATO territory. The ship, bound for ‌Russian exclave Kaliningrad, was damaged in international waters west of Russia’s Gogland island, Finland’s Defense Forces have said, corroborating an account by Russian officials.

The risk of further attacks in the ‌Gulf of Finland, a narrow arm of the Baltic Sea, cannot be ruled out, Estonian Navy Commander Ivo Vark told public broadcaster ERR on Sunday. Finland’s military said last week it had detected a strike on a Russian warship in the same area during Ukrainian drone attacks.

The Sparta II is a 121-m (397-foot) Russian-flagged cargo vessel owned by Russian shipping company Oboronlogistika that left St. Petersburg on Friday, according to LSEG data. The vessel is subject to US sanctions, according to the US Treasury Department.

Oboronlogistika provides logistics services for the Russian Defense Ministry, according to the company’s website.

World.title: Manufacturing, mining drive 12% rise in Saudi operating revenues: GASTAT
World.content:
RIYADH: Saudi Arabia’s Operating Revenues Index rose 12.2 percent year on year in September, led by double-digit growth in manufacturing and mining, according to official data.

Manufacturing revenues increased 15 percent from a year earlier, while mining and quarrying activities surged 27.5 percent, the General Authority for Statistics said in its latest Short-Term Business Indicators report.

Financial and insurance activities recorded 19.3 percent growth, while wholesale and retail trade, including motor vehicle repairs, rose 2.1 percent. Construction activities edged up 0.4 percent.

The increase reflects stronger operating revenues across several key sectors of the Saudi economy, particularly manufacturing, mining and quarrying, and financial services.

Separately, Saudi Arabia’s non-oil private sector continued to expand in October, although growth moderated amid regional disruptions. The Kingdom’s Riyad Bank Purchasing Managers’ Index, compiled by S&P Global, stood at 54 in October, down from 55.3 in September. The reading marked the seventh consecutive month of expansion and was the second-highest since February.

The October survey also highlighted the impact of shipping disruptions linked to regional tensions, which increased freight and insurance costs and weighed on business confidence.

In its latest report, GASTAT stated: “On a monthly basis, the Operating Revenues Index increased by 6.6 percent, supported by a 3.5 percent increase in manufacturing activities, a 37.3 percent increase in mining and quarrying activities, a 4 percent increase in financial and insurance activities, and increases of 3.5 percent and 1.2 percent in human health and social work activities and professional, scientific, and technical activities, respectively.”

Employees Compensation Index

Saudi Arabia’s Employees Compensation Index increased 6.8 percent year on year in September, driven primarily by a 9.4 percent rise in manufacturing, GASTAT said.

Compensation in wholesale and retail trade and motor vehicle repair activities increased 6.8 percent, while financial and insurance activities rose 5.6 percent. Mining and quarrying recorded a 5.2 percent increase, and construction grew 2 percent.

On a monthly basis, the index advanced 0.5 percent. Manufacturing compensation increased 0.3 percent, construction rose 0.8 percent and mining and quarrying gained 0.2 percent. Financial and insurance activities and transportation and storage each recorded a 1 percent increase.

The number of building permits issued in the Kingdom reached 6,092 in September, up 14.6 percent from 5,317 in the same month a year earlier, according to GASTAT. The total was also 8.4 percent higher than the 5,621 permits issued in August.

World.title: Qatar’s film committee partners with Watermelon Pictures
World.content:
DUBAI: The Film Committee at Media City Qatar has partnered with independent film studio Watermelon Pictures to develop and co-produce a slate of films highlighting stories from the Global South and beyond.

Announced during the closing day of Doha Industry Days, the collaboration will seek to champion visionary filmmakers and compelling stories, supporting projects across a variety of genres with an emphasis on culturally authentic storytelling and international appeal.

Productions will be filmed substantially in Qatar or structured as Qatari co-productions. The agreement will also seek to involve Doha-based post-production companies and help eligible projects access the Qatar Screen Production Incentive, creating opportunities for local crews and businesses.

“Through this partnership, we want to give filmmakers the resources to tell stories rooted in their communities and bring them to audiences around the world,” said Hassan Al-Thawadi, chair of the Qatar Film Committee, in a statement.

For Watermelon Pictures, founded in 2024 by brothers Badie and Hamza Ali, the agreement marks an expansion into larger-scale production, building on its work in film distribution.

The company has championed Palestinian and Arab cinema through titles including “From Ground Zero,” “Palestine 36” and “The Voice of Hind Rajab.” Its creative team previously included Alana Hadid, sister of models Gigi and Bella Hadid.

The two parties will jointly select projects for the initial slate, with further details announced in due course.

World.title: Drone strikes hit homes in Sudan’s capital: witnesses
World.content:
KHARTOUM: Drones struck residential areas in and around Sudan's capital Khartoum early on Sunday, destroying homes, witnesses said.

"People were trying to rescue family members trapped under the rubble," one witness said.

Authorities did not immediately report on casualties.

The explosions began at around 2:00 am (0000 GMT) and continued until 4:30 am (0230 GMT) in different parts of the city, witnesses said.

The war since April 2023 between the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) and the Sudanese army has killed more than 200,000 people, aid workers estimate, and triggered the world's largest hunger and displacement crises.

The United Nations has repeatedly criticised both sides' rampant use of drones, which killed more than 1,100 people in the first half of 2026.

A Sudanese army drone strike killed 15 people including four children in a West Kordofan village days ago, as the army pushes through the state, recapturing territory from the RSF.

Of the hundreds of child casualties this year, two-thirds were killed or injured by drone strikes, the UN said last week.

World.title: Pakistan FM hopeful for US-Iran deal, warns against prolonged war
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: Pakistan’s Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar voiced optimism about reaching an agreement between the United States and Iran, saying the world could not afford a prolonged conflict in the Middle East.

“I’m a born optimist. I think I would certainly expect that sooner or later — I hope it’s sooner — we will achieve that objective,” Dar said in an interview with Euronews aired by PTV News on Saturday.

He warned that continued fighting would deepen disruptions to energy supplies, drive up prices and worsen civilian suffering, including in Pakistan.

Despite what he described as subsequent violations of the June 18 agreement, Dar said Islamabad remained committed to the peace process and continued to press both Washington and Tehran to honor their commitments.

He reaffirmed Pakistan’s support for an independent, multilateral foreign policy and outlined its efforts to facilitate direct negotiations between the two sides.

Dar said diplomacy remained the only viable way to resolve major international conflicts, rejecting unilateral action and bloc politics. He added that Pakistan had advocated peaceful dispute resolution and respect for national sovereignty during its 2025-26 term on the UN Security Council.

World.title: South Korea education chief resigns amid AI cheating scandal
World.content:
SEOUL: South Korea’s education minister resigned Sunday over an AI-assisted cheating scandal that erupted ahead of the country’s key college entrance exams last week.

The country has been gripped by fears of AI-assisted exam cheating since last Sunday, when the top scorer in a national tax accountant exam confessed to using a miniature camera and smartphone to achieve a near-perfect score, just four days before the crucial college entrance exam known as the Suneung.

The annual nine-hour Suneung is widely seen as a ticket to prestigious universities, well-paid jobs and even better marriage prospects in the highly competitive country.

The confession sent officials scrambling to roll out a slew of preventive measures — including blocking public Wi-Fi in testing areas and placing stickers over clothing buttons — but Education Minister Choi Kyo-jin struggled to reassure the public, particularly after remarks he made three days before the exam.

“The exam concluded without any major incidents... However, as the minister in charge, I do not believe I am immune from public criticism that we failed to prepare adequately in advance,” Choi wrote on X.

“Now that the exam is over, I take full responsibility and hereby offer my resignation,” he added.

President Lee Jae Myung has accepted his resignation, the presidential office said.

Asked during a parliamentary hearing on Monday whether he was confident that authorities could catch would-be cheaters on exam day, the 72-year-old replied: “Due to my age, I am not confident I could.”

His response quickly drew public backlash.

Choi did not appear at press conferences in the days leading up to Thursday’s exam, where a vice minister instead announced the preventive measures.

Officials said 111 cases of misconduct involving electronic devices were identified during Thursday’s exam, nearly half of which were detected through three emergency alerts sent by the government to identify smartphones that test takers had failed to hand over.

World.title: Iraq qualifies for 2027 AFC U-17 Asian Cup in Uzbekistan
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Asian Football Confederation (AFC) has officially confirmed the final 16-team lineup for the 2027 AFC U-17 Asian Cup, including Iraq, which topped Group B during the qualifiers in Thailand with 10 points—putting the young Lions of Mesopotamia just three group-stage matches away from securing a berth at the 2027 FIFA U-17 World Cup in Qatar.

Under head coach Salam Shaker, Iraq clinched first place in Group B after defeating tournament hosts Thailand 2–1 in their decisive final qualifier in Buriram on Friday, November 20, ending a nine-year continental qualification drought for the national under-17 side.

The finals are scheduled to take place in the Uzbek capital of Tashkent from May 13 to 29, 2027, following the official tournament draw on February 18, 2027.

Per AFC competition regulations, the top eight finishers at the tournament in Uzbekistan—specifically the eight teams that advance out of the group stage into the quarterfinals—will automatically qualify for the 2027 FIFA U-17 World Cup in Qatar.

Reaching the World Cup also carries a secondary continental incentive: under AFC rules, all Asian nations that qualify for the global finals earn direct entry into the 2028 AFC U-17 Asian Cup without having to contest the preliminary qualifying rounds.

The 16 participating nations in Tashkent comprise the seven qualifying group winners alongside the nine AFC representatives from the 2026 FIFA U-17 World Cup who received automatic entry:

Qualification Route Qualified Nations Qualifying Group Winners Iraq (Group B), Indonesia (Group A), Syria (Group C), Iran (Group D), India (Group E), Yemen (Group F), Lebanon (Group G) Automatic Qualifiers Uzbekistan (Hosts), Australia, China PR, Japan, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, South Korea, Tajikistan, Vietnam

Coach Salam Shaker and his squad now shift their focus toward preparing for February’s draw, aiming to replicate the historic success of Iraq’s 2016 U-16 championship generation and re-establish Iraqi youth football on both the Asian and global stages.

World.title: Japanese cyclist killed in highway collision in southern Iraq’s Muthanna Governorate
World.content:
Samawah (IraqiNews.com) – A Japanese bicycle traveler died on Friday, November 20, 2026, following a traffic collision along the Rumaitha–Samawah highway in southern Iraq’s Muthanna Governorate.

According to a security source, the tourist was riding a bicycle along the highway when he collided with a Dodge Charger sedan.

The impact proved fatal for the cyclist and also injured a passenger riding inside the vehicle, identified as a security officer.

Traffic police and forensic investigators conducted an on-site inspection of the crash scene following the incident. Based on their preliminary field assessment, authorities determined that the Japanese cyclist was at fault for the collision.

World.title: Iraqi Energy Police establish 12 checkpoints along Jurf Al Sakhar oil pipelines
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Ministry of Interior’s Directorate General of Energy Police continued field operations on Saturday, November 21, 2026, to secure vital oil pipeline corridors across the Jurf al-Sakhar (Jurf al-Nasr) subdistrict in northern Babylon Governorate.

Marking the second consecutive day since Baghdad formally inaugurated its new joint command center in the area, Energy Police units established full operational control along a pipeline stretch exceeding five kilometers.

In an official statement, Ministry of Interior Head of Relations and Media Major General Miqdad Miri confirmed that the deployment is being directed on the ground by Energy Police Director-General Lieutenant General Hamid Abdullah Ibrahim.

Executing the mission with a regiment from the Commando Brigade (Liwa al-Maghawir), engineering teams deployed specialized heavy machinery to carve a dedicated patrol road parallel to the pipeline bundles through rugged terrain, enabling rapid troop mobility and sustained field surveillance.

To lock down the corridor against illicit tampering, Energy Police established 12 new security checkpoints spaced roughly every 500 meters along the route, alongside a permanent regimental headquarters.

Major General Miri emphasized that these preventive measures are designed to elevate field command, safeguard crude transport infrastructure, and protect national wealth.

The deployment represents the first concrete operational phase following the expiration of Prime Minister Ali Faleh Al-Zaidi’s Friday ultimatum to Kata’ib Hezbollah.

On Friday, November 20, federal authorities inaugurated the joint control headquarters (Al-Musaytir)—commanded under the Federal Police and uniting Army, Federal Police, Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF), and Energy Police formations—initiating a permanent security reorganization in Jurf al-Sakhar that includes securing pipeline networks and reopening closed transit arteries to civilian traffic.

World.title: US dollar steadies near 170,000 dinars across Baghdad, Erbil, and Basra
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqqiNews.com) – The exchange rate of the U.S. dollar against the Iraqi dinar edged slightly lower across major domestic parallel markets on Saturday morning, November 21, 2026, hovering right at the 170,000-dinar threshold for retail sales while buying bids settled below that mark across key commercial hubs.

According to morning monitoring figures, physical banknote rates opened across Baghdad, Erbil, and Basra as follows:

In Baghdad, currency exchange counters posted retail selling rates at 170,000 IQD against buying offers of 169,500 IQD per $100.

In Erbil, currency desks quoted retail selling rates slightly higher at 170,050 IQD alongside purchasing bids holding at 170,000 IQD per $100.

In Basra, foreign exchange offices matched Baghdad’s selling quote at 170,000 IQD, with buying offers dipping to 169,250 IQD per $100.

Despite the downward drift at the start of the trading week, parallel cash rates maintain a spread of roughly 18,000 dinars above the Central Bank of Iraq’s (CBI) official rate of 152,000 IQD per $100 (1,520 IQD per dollar).

World.title: Gulf alternatives may save Excelerate Energy’s LNG project in Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The liquefied natural gas (LNG) project in Iraq is witnessing rapid on-site progress amid efforts to overcome geopolitical challenges and navigation risks associated with the Strait of Hormuz.

According to project updates, the field team and the materials required for constructing the marine jetty and terminal infrastructure have arrived in Iraq, Attaqa News reported.

US-based Excelerate Energy, which is carrying out the project, expects the pace of work to accelerate over the coming weeks, with construction activities progressing at the marine terminal and the facility’s infrastructure.

The firm aims to complete and commission the project during the second quarter of 2027, following a delay in 2026 caused by the crisis in the Strait of Hormuz.

Once Iraq begins imports, it will become the sixth Arab nation in history to import LNG—joining Kuwait, Egypt, the UAE, Jordan, and Bahrain.

The consequences of the Iranian conflict have caused delays for Iraq’s LNG project, which had originally planned to open in the third quarter of 2026. As a result, Excelerate Energy has moved the Excelerate Acadia, its floating storage and regasification unit (FSRU), to Jordan for nine months.

To overcome disruptions to maritime traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, the company plans to utilize an FSRU already stationed within the region, eliminating the need to traverse the strategic waterway.

The company is likely to utilize the FSRU currently stationed in the UAE, known as Express.

The US firm indicated that it is working to arrange the import of LNG from countries within the Gulf region, a statement that strongly suggests Qatar or the UAE.

World.title: US dollar exchange rate rises in Iraq’s parallel market
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The exchange rate for the US dollar against the Iraqi dinar experienced a slight increase on Thursday in both Baghdad, the Iraqi capital, and Erbil, the capital of the Kurdistan region of Iraq.

The US dollar exchange rate rose in Baghdad’s al-Kifah and al-Harithiya stock exchanges, reaching 1,706.5 Iraqi dinars compared to 1,706 Iraqi dinars on Thursday morning.

The exchange rate in currency exchange shops in Baghdad ranged between 1,710 Iraqi dinars and 1,700 Iraqi dinars, Shafaq News reported.

In Erbil, the US dollar exchange rate also increased, fluctuating between 1,709.5 and 1,708.5 Iraqi dinars.

US dollar exchange rates rose noticeably in the Baghdad and Erbil markets on October 7, following the cabinet’s decision to revalue the official rate of the local currency, causing turbulence and instability in the parallel market.

Iraq officially depreciated its national currency, with the baseline dropping from about 1,300 Iraqi dinars to 1,500 dinars per US dollar.

The Iraqi cabinet approved the structural adjustment, which marks a 14.5 percent decline compared to the previous official framework that had been in place since early 2023.

Following the announcement, parallel market rates in Baghdad and Erbil soared, with exchange shops reporting market gains of more than 1,700 Iraqi dinars per US dollar.

World.title: Iraqi PM orders reopening of closed roads in Jurf al-Sakhar
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister and Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces, Ali al-Zaidi, ordered on Thursday to expedite the reopening of all closed roads in the Jurf al-Sakhar district in the central province of Babil.

During his meeting with security officials, al-Zaidi emphasized that the army and security forces would uphold the authority of the state across all Iraqi territory, according to a statement released by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO).

The prime minister emphasized that the enforcement of state authority would be carried out in accordance with the constitution and the law. He affirmed the government’s commitment to protecting the lives and interests of citizens across the country and to preventing any violations or assaults on public and private properties.

According to al-Zaidi, the security forces operate as a unified entity, with their numerous branches and units cooperating with one another.

These directives come ahead of the deadline set by the government for Kataib Hezbollah, an Iran-backed militant faction, to withdraw from Jurf al-Sakhar—a deadline expiring on Friday—paving the way for security forces to enter and redeploy in the area.

The deadline for the withdrawal from Jurf al-Sakhar, also known as Jurf al-Nasr, follows an investigation by a government committee, which Baghdad stated uncovered evidence of oil smuggling operations in the area.

The armed faction rejected the smuggling allegations, claiming the sites inspected by investigators were abandoned facilities or fuel tanks for military vehicles.

World.title: Iraq’s trade exchange with China drops to $19.8 billion
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Chinese Ambassador to Iraq, Xiang Bo, said on Thursday that the decline in trade exchange with Iraq—which fell to $19.8 billion—is due to the escalating security tensions in the region.

During a press conference in Baghdad, Bo projected that trade between the two countries would recover, reaching $26 billion by the end of 2026 or early 2027.

According to Bo, China is a trusted partner to Iraq. He noted that the two countries share deep historical and cultural ties, dating back thousands of years.

Bo emphasized that bilateral relations have seen significant development, with Iraq serving as a key trade partner. Trade volume between the two countries reached $51 billion in 2025, reflecting the strength of their mutual commitments and relationship.

Bo mentioned earlier that major Chinese firms are involved in the construction and development of several industries in Iraq, such as oil, energy, and infrastructure.

The Chinese diplomat expressed his hope that this collaboration will continue and grow into other sectors, contributing to the development of a complete partnership between Iraq and China.

Chinese companies have been heavily involved in the oil industry and in significant infrastructure projects, such as the construction of major bridges and schools, with more than 600 schools completed in several Iraqi provinces.

World.title: ‘Vote Chori’ allegations: Nitin Nabin to lead BJP's Hyderabad rally to counter criticism
World.content:
NEW DELHI: BJP president

will lead a rally in Hyderabad on Monday to counter criticism of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and allegations of "vote chori" (vote theft), Union minister Bandi Sanjay Kumar said on Sunday.

The BJP MP from Karimnagar described the rally as a "historic" event, predicting a massive turnout of party workers and members of the public, ANI reported.

He accused those opposing the exercise of acting against the country's interests, arguing that only Indian citizens should decide who becomes the prime minister or chief minister and elect their representatives.

"We will not let a Pakistani, Bangladeshi, Afghan or others to decide.



That's why, SIR has been brought," he told reporters, as per ANI.

Kumar also dismissed Telangana chief minister A Revanth Reddy's recent assertion that the Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS) was the Congress's principal political rival in the state. He alleged that the Congress and BRS were working together and said the chief minister's remarks indicated this.

Claiming that Reddy was concerned about the BJP's growing presence in Telangana, the Union minister questioned how the BRS could be considered a major challenger when it had no Lok Sabha members and had not won a municipal corporation.





He alleged that the Congress and BRS were attempting to prevent the BJP's expansion in the state and expressed confidence that his party would form the next government after the 2028 Assembly elections.

The BJP has been organising rallies in several cities to counter allegations of electoral malpractice levelled by the Congress and other opposition parties.

World.title: Sabarimala pilgrimage: Kerala puts security, transport arrangements in place amid devotee rush
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Sabarimala Lord Ayyappa Temple in Kerala witnessed a significant rise in the number of devotees on Sunday as the annual Mandala-Makaravilakku pilgrimage season began.

The state government and temple authorities have put extensive security and administrative measures in place to manage the rush and ensure a smooth pilgrimage, according to new agency ANI.

The temple, located in Pathanamthitta district, reopened on November 16, marking the beginning of the annual pilgrimage season.

State health minister K Muraleedharan said the government had made arrangements to handle the expected increase in the number of devotees.



These include improvements in infrastructure, transport services and other essential facilities.

Speaking to the media, Muraleedharan said the renovated road connecting Chalakkayam and Pamba had been inaugurated on Saturday. He added that the Kerala state electricity board (KSEB) had completed electrification work along the route.

He also said that Kerala state road transport corporation (KSRTC) buses were operating, while additional private buses had been hired to ferry pilgrims between Nilakkal and Pamba.





The minister said the government was satisfied with the preparations and appreciated the cooperation extended by the Devaswom Board. He noted that the number of devotees increases every year and that arrangements had been made to manage the expected heavy rush this season.

Meanwhile, the state police have deployed additional personnel at the temple and other important locations to ensure the safety of pilgrims throughout the season.

Pathanamthitta superintendent of police and district police chief R Anand said comprehensive security, traffic regulation and surveillance arrangements had been made in coordination with the district administration and local bodies.

Speaking to reporters, Anand said police personnel had been deployed at major temples, while parking facilities had been arranged at designated idathavalams (pilgrim resting centres).

Arrangements for refreshments and other facilities were also being coordinated with local authorities.

He added that special police officers and battalion personnel had been deployed to support the security arrangements. In case of heavy traffic at Nilakkal, vehicles and pilgrims could be temporarily held at designated resting centres to prevent congestion.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Anand also highlighted the round-the-clock AI-powered surveillance arrangements in Pandalam, along with special traffic management measures.

He assured that the police would work to ensure a safe and smooth pilgrimage.

The first phase of the annual Mandala-Makaravilakku season will continue from November 16 to December 27, ending with the Mandala Pooja.

After the Mandala period, the shrine will reopen on December 30 for the Makaravilakku festival, scheduled for January 14, 2027. The temple will close for the season on January 20.

With the pilgrimage season underway, devotees from across the country have started arriving at the hill shrine in large numbers. The government, police and Devaswom Board have coordinated their efforts to manage the influx and ensure that pilgrims have access to necessary facilities throughout the season.

World.title: ‘Pretending to speak for ordinary people’: Vijayan on PM Modi's remarks on corporate jobs, wages
World.content:
NEW DELHI: CPI(M) veteran

on Sunday accused Prime Minister

of making a political spectacle of his recent appeal to corporates to raise salaries and generate more jobs, questioning why the PM had not shown similar concern for workers over the past 12 years.

Taking to X, the former Kerala chief minister said the Modi government had spent years extending tax benefits and concessions to big businesses, while ordinary people continued to grapple with stagnant wages and rising living costs.

The CPI(M) leader was reacting to Modi's recent address at the annual general meeting of the Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FICCI) in Delhi. During the event, the PM questioned industry leaders over the lack of adequate job creation and salary growth despite several concessions offered by the government.

World.title: ‘JD(U) has only a few months left’: JMM leader after Nitish Kumar skips 'Nitish Setu'  inauguration

, claiming that the JD(U) had only a few months left and was moving towards its political end.

Pandey's remarks came amid a political controversy over Kumar's absence from the inauguration of the Nitish Setu bridge in Vaishali district. ....Nitish Kumar is finished. The JD(U) now has only a few months left. Based on the political developments that have unfolded, it is clear that the JD(U) is heading towards its end...â





Pandey told ANI.

's inauguration of the Rs 4,280-crore bridge over the Ganga on November 21. Kumar was not present at the main ceremony in Vaishali, which was attended by Modi, Bihar CM Samrat Choudhary and Union Minister Chirag Paswan.

World.title: ‘Saved lakhs from debt’: CTI hails Modi’s appeal to curb gold purchases
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Chamber of Trade and Industry (CTI) has written to Prime Minister Narendra

, thanking him for his appeal to citizens to curb gold purchases, saying the advice helped protect jewellers, traders and investors from potential losses after a fall in

.

In a letter dated Sunday, CTI said the PMâs appeal, which had drawn criticism when it was made, had helped traders avert substantial financial losses. The letter was titled âYour foresight saved lakhs of jewellers and investors from falling into debtâ.

According to the trade body, gold was priced at Rs 1.90 crore per kilogram when PM Modi advised citizens against unnecessary purchases. Its price has since fallen to Rs 1.25 crore per kilogram, a decline of Rs 65 lakh per kilogram.



"If traders had ignored your advice and purchased gold at that time, they would have incurred a loss of Rs 65 lakh per kilogram today. Lakhs of jewellers would have fallen into debt and faced bankruptcy," the letter stated.

CTI said jewellery traders across the country typically maintain stocks worth several months, leaving them exposed to significant losses had they bought inventory at the earlier prices.

"Lakhs of jewellery traders across the country maintain stock worth several months.





Had they purchased their stock when gold was priced at Rs 1.90 crore per kilogram, they would have suffered losses worth crores today," it said.

The organisation added that small traders dealing in gold through online and offline platforms, as well as stock market investors, had also been protected from potential losses. It said messages were coming in from traders acknowledging the Prime Minister's advice.

"Messages are continuously pouring into CTI's groups saying, 'Modi Ji has saved us'," the letter stated, adding that even traders who had initially opposed the appeal were now acknowledging its benefits.

CTI also said the fall in prices had offered relief to consumers during the wedding season, which it said was witnessing 52 lakh weddings.

"Prime Minister, you have not just given advice; you have saved the hard-earned capital of lakhs of families. On behalf of CTI and the entire trading community, we extend our heartfelt thanks and gratitude to you," the letter said.

The letter was signed by CTI chairman Brijesh Goyal and other office-bearers.

The development follows PM Modi's remarks at an event in Lucknow a day earlier, where he recalled asking citizens to avoid unnecessary gold purchases for a year. He compared the appeal with former Prime Minister Lal Bahadur Shastri's call to citizens to skip one meal.

The PM had made seven appeals on May 10, 2026, during an event in Secunderabad, citing the need to conserve foreign exchange and reduce dependence on imports amid the West Asia conflict and rising crude oil prices. World.title: PM Modi announces Rs 2 lakh ex-gratia for families of victims in Kota, Kutch mishaps
World.content:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday expressed grief over the loss of lives in separate mishaps in Kota, Rajasthan, and Kutch, Gujarat, and announced financial assistance for the families of those killed and injured.

In two separate posts on X,

conveyed his condolences to the bereaved families and wished those injured a speedy recovery.

Reacting to the mishap in Kota, PM Modi said, "Pained to learn about the loss of lives in a tragic mishap in Kota, Rajasthan. My thoughts are with the bereaved families in this hour of grief. May the injured recover at the earliest."

World.title: 'Not claiming to win all' : AAP rules out alliance in Uttarakhand; to contest all 70 seats in Assembly polls
